Carrick believes all of his squad share his determination – “If you don’t, this is not the place for you,” he said – and insisted there were no factions. “It’s not divided. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at Bayern training
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany has been ⁠taken ⁠to ​hospital after the Bayern Munich coach felt unwell during training ⁠on Friday.

The Belgian, ​who ‌had been ‌nursing a virus in ‌recent days, was coaching his team before feeling unwell and being taken to ‌hospital.

The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 ​at home against Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, are due ​to ​travel to ​Freiburg on Sunday. Kompany was on the bench for the Arsenal game despite the viral infection.

Bayern said on their website: “Vincent Kompany required medical ⁠attention after collapsing during a training session for ​Bayern’s reserve team. The ‌head coach of the professional squad had been observing ‌the second team’s session.

“Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in the hospital and will remain under medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage all training ‌and match-related operations.“

Max Eberl, Bayern’s sporting director, said: “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. At Bayern, we will do everything ​we ​can to ensure he ​makes a speedy recovery.

“Vinnie is receiving ​all the ‌necessary medical care ​and ​support, and he will be given as much time as he needs. Everyone at FC Bayern wishes Vinnie a quick recovery.”

Sports.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue.

Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Saka missed a large portion of last season due to hamstring, hip and achilles tendon injuries having also been sidelined by another hamstring issue in 2024-25. In total, he has had 11 different injuries since September 2023 and Arteta insisted that he has been trying to ease his workload as a result. “It’s certainly been different in the last year or so,” the Spaniard said when asked if Saka remains robust enough to start every match. “The demands that we are putting on every player are immense. The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.

“Bukayo against Lille [in the Champions League last week] didn’t start the game because we knew what was happening. We have to play three times in less than six days. And especially when the games are so demanding, until the last minute you are there, you are chasing the game, you want to win. The necessity is to win every game, so we know that. So we are preparing the players for those scenarios and we do the best that we possibly can.”

Saka missed only three Premier League matches in three seasons between 2021 and 2024 and broke the Arsenal club record by playing in 83 consecutive top-flight games. He is already approaching 300 appearances for the club he joined as a seven-year-old and was rewarded with a lucrative new contract in February that made him one of the highest-paid players in the club’s history.

Asked whether he feared Saka could suffer from burnout having made his Arsenal debut three months after his 17th birthday, Arteta said: “I don’t have that feeling at all but something we have to be very mindful of is to create the right ecosystem around the player to fulfil his qualities. We really need to understand, whenever he comes back, how we are going to manage his load, what he is capable of to sustain having an impact in the team.”

Saka’s absence could hand an opportunity to Max Dowman on Saturday. The 16-year-old has played only nine minutes in the league this season and Arteta feels sure he is ready to make an impact after he became the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history, against David Moyes’s side in March.

“There is something inevitable to go back to that memory and the feeling of the moment. That’s with us, that’s going to stay in that stadium for a long, long time,” said Arteta. “He’s training and every time he’s got a moment to play, he’s showing that he’s a player that is going to impact the game. For sure he’s going to have minutes.”

Sports.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
Sports.content:
It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers.

Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day.

The Arsenal hierarchy are understood to remain behind Slegers, but for how long? The answer may hinge on Saturday lunchtime’s result. However much goodwill the Dutchwoman gained for guiding Arsenal to Champions League glory in May 2025, the simple truth is, it is unacceptable for a club with one of the biggest budgets in the world to be 12 points behind the leaders after six games.

That gap is why the draw with Birmingham not only pretty much extinguished Arsenal’s title hopes but also burned a hole in their secondary domestic objective – Champions League qualification. The unthinkable prospect of failure appears a genuine possibility: they are nine points adrift of third-placed London City. Arsenal need a derby win on Saturday but also a winning run to reverse the slide, and there is little evidence to suggest such a turnaround is close.

Arsenal have the worst shot conversion rate in the league (4.1%) and, according to Stats Perform, the third-worst shooting accuracy (30.6%) and third-lowest average xG per shot (0.09) despite averaging over 60% possession. Slegers’s persistence in deploying Alessia Russo – widely regarded as one of Europe’s best No 9s – in the No 10 role has baffled supporters and commentators alike. Russo has scored more WSL goals against Tottenham (eight) than any other player so Saturday’s game may be the perfect moment for that to change.

View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s Alessia Russo and Caitlin Foord wheel away after a goal against Tottenham in February 2025 – however, Russo has not flourished as a No 10 this season. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Arsenal have struggled against low blocks for a number of seasons, though, so not all fault lies at Slegers’s door. Nonetheless, the 37-year-old was substantially backed in the summer, with Arsenal enjoying perhaps their strongest transfer window in recent memory. So far though they have looked confounded tactically, bruised mentally and lacking the self-belief to grab a game by the scruff of its neck.

Asked if she was surprised to still be in her job, Slegers said: “That’s not something I think about. It’s about, ‘where are we as a group?’ and ‘what are we working towards?’ It’s absolutely not what we expected [our recent results] or what we wanted. But I’m in the here and now, and we are preparing for the north London derby. We have the group together. Everyone is going in the same direction and the fuel and motivation is sky high, because of the fans that will be there for us. That’s where my focus will be.”

Asked how imperative it is that Arsenal climb back up into a Champions League place this season, Slegers added: “Of course that’s in the back of our heads, but what we need right now is to get back to winning ways. We can only do that with the next game in front of us so that’s why the next game in front of us is the most important right now.”

Slegers has maintained after last weekend’s draw that Arsenal will recover when they fix some “details and margins”. Perhaps taking on a Tottenham side who have become only the second team in history to concede six or more goals in consecutive WSL games is the perfect opportunity.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It is a little bit of game intelligence and smartness in moments,” said the Spurs head coach, Martin Ho, insisting he is not worried about his team’s defending in the long-term. “There have been certain aspects that, collectively, players and staff, we were not happy with in certain moments, and we have to make sure we correct them. At the moment we’re getting heavily punished for some small errors with the ball that we’re making.”

The Englishman also only had praise for Arsenal’s qualities when speaking on Friday morning. “If you try and underestimate a team with Arsenal’s quality you’re in for trouble,” he said. Asked about Arsenal’s poor run, Ho added: “Arsenal aren’t a bad side. Their possession stats are probably the highest in the league, alongside Manchester City. Their goalscoring chances and touches in the opposition box are very, very high. They have world-class players.”

Last season’s runners-up do have world-class players but it is high time for them to play like a cohesive team.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
Sports.content:
MOU AND WHOSE ARMY?

Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story:

“Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.”

War’s a comin’, in other words, so you’d better buy some tomato soup (10 tins of), mushroom soup (eight tins of, for consumption cold) and ice cream (vanilla, one large tub of). Here’s where it gets interesting. The government released their three-day survival plan on Thursday afternoon, three days before the event most likely to cause World War III: José Mourinho’s first Clásico since 2013. Barcelona meet Real Madrid at the Camp Nou on Sunday and suddenly the government are telling us we may need to hunker down. Coincidence? We think not!

OK, OK. Coincidence? We think so! José may be the most charismatic baddie since Dirty Den’s most recent death, but not even he is capable of starting the geopolitical answer to El Clásico. Sunday’s match will spark a form of global conflict, even if it’s just a load of strangers caterwauling at each other on the internet rather than talking to their children, reading a book or practising any of the gazillion behaviours that would make their lives and the world a better place.

Mourinho’s relationship with Barcelona could fill a book, never mind a teatime email. There is love lost, but it’s decades since it went missing. These days they can’t stand the thought of each other, never mind the sight. There is an argument (NB: Football Daily doesn’t actually want to argue) that Mourinho’s greatest achievement in football, apart from finishing second with Manchester United in 2017-18, was to take a La Liga title off probably the greatest club side of all time. He also drove Pep Guardiola into a sabbatical – but that, and the Realpolitik of the Bernabéu dressing-room, took so much out of Mourinho that he has never been the same since that triumphant 2011-12 season.

The Camp Nou was the venue for Mourinho’s “most beautiful defeat” (you know the one, when not even a good hosing could douse his celebrations) and his most humiliating defeat a few months later. He can’t afford any kind of defeat on Sunday: Madrid are six points behind Barcelona, who have won all nine league games, scoring 39 goals in the process. But Mourinho’s team have scored four goals in each of their last three matches and, even in the absence of the suspended Vinícius Jr , have attacking threats galore. And whatever the result, Mourinho’s post-match press conference will be must-see TV.

The match kicks off on Sunday evening, but only if you take these things literally. For Mourinho, it began the moment he was asked a question about it. He has had the face on all week because, well, wouldn’t you if you were treated like this? Barcelona played 24 hours earlier than Madrid in Bigger Cup, an open goal for conspiracy theorists and performative underdogs. “We’re pushing ahead,” he said. “At the moment, we’re missing out on 24 hours of rest, but we’re moving forward.” So is Football Daily, to the supermarket to get some urgent shopping. We’ll Be Ready for Sunday – not with 72 hours of essential supplies, but with a month’s worth of popcorn.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray at 8pm (BST) for red-hot Premier League updates on Ipswich Town 0-0 Nottingham Forest.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry. You know, that’s the position I’m in, and it’s a privileged position” – Michael Carrick delivers a near six-minute monologue defending Manchester United’s values in which he veered close to painting a picture of himself as being akin to another former Middlesbrough manager who once held a brolly while watching his team fail.

View image in fullscreen Steve McClaren: a reminder. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

double quotation mark Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh.

double quotation mark Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis.

double quotation mark May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Justin Kavanagh. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
Sports.content:
Are the team underperforming?

Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA

There have been so many arrivals and departures on Tyneside in recent months that it’s too early to say. Any team that sold their three best players – Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimarães in Newcastle’s case – during the summer would expect a degree of disruption. Eight signings were made, with four aged 20 and under and the others aged 24 and under, and only one (Nico González) had Premier League experience. Throw in a change of manager and an almost entirely new backroom staff and playing style three weeks before the season and teething troubles seem almost inevitable. LT

How much pressure is the manager under?

Sage is sailing extremely close to the wind and was warned after the Brighton game that things must improve quickly or he will be shown the door. It is understood that the Palace chair, Steve Parish, has yet to be convinced by the manager who led Lens to the French Cup last season and has demanded improvements in defence. After the creditable Europa League draw with Besiktas in midweek, Sunday’s meeting with Newcastle is crucial to his future. Thomas Frank and Kieran McKenna are likely candidates should Sage get sacked. Ipswich would be due substantial compensation for McKenna despite him leaving Portman Road in the summer, which could be a major hurdle. EA

View image in fullscreen Adam Wharton (centre) looks dejected during Crystal Palace’s defeat at Brighton. Photograph: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

Very little internally but, externally, the honeymoon is over. Newcastle paid Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli £9.5m compensation for Matthias Jaissle, convinced that the 38-year-old German and his “vertical football” were ideal fits. David Hopkinson, the chief executive, and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, are very impressed by Jaissle’s management style, particularly his collaborative approach. They appreciate that Eddie Howe’s successor is new to the Premier League, did not have a proper pre-season and is coping with a raft of injuries. All parties remain sufficiently realistic to predict a season of “ups and downs” but Newcastle’s Saudi Arabian owners crave a return to Europe. Many fans believe Jaissle’s football is old-school, rudimentary long ball with a fancy name, and believe his system and team selections have been flawed. They fear he may be a slave to philosophy. LT

How much responsibility does the manager bear?

Palace have looked a shadow of the side that won three trophies in the space of 12 months under Glasner and Sage must take some of the blame. He fell out with Parish after failing to sign several of his preferred targets in the summer, but it was his decision to break up the Adam Wharton-Daichi Kamada axis in central midfield having brought in Quinten Timber on deadline day. While the Dutchman, who missed the game in Turkey due to injury, has provided extra energy and Kamada has excelled in a more advanced role, Wharton has been struggling defensively. Palace looked much more solid when Wharton and Kamada started together against Besiktas – surely Sage will now stick with the partnership that served Glasner so well. EA

Jaissle’s belief in a gung-ho 4-2-3-1 featuring a classic No 10 is serving him badly at Newcastle, where he does not possess a natural attacking playmaker. It is also leaving González, a holding midfielder, frequently overrun and in need of additional support. With Malick Thiaw and, particularly, Sven Botman struggling in central defence, a switch to a more stable 3-5-2 may be sensible. More importantly, changing the philosophy to a more contain-and-counterattack approach would help camouflage the flaws and make the most of the team’s blistering attacking pace. Jaissle’s high-pressing, attack-minded tactics often appear overly high-risk. His critics fear he may prove to be another Ruben Amorim but Newcastle insiders insist Howe’s successor will prove more flexible than he may seem. Newcastle have not kept a league clean sheet for 13 games, equalling a club record, but six of those came under Howe. LT

How much is beyond the manager’s control?

A typically chaotic end to the transfer window left Sage with a bloated squad but insufficient leadership at the back after selling Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea. Axel Disasi’s three-match ban due to a reckless red card against Ipswich, after he arrived on loan from Stamford Bridge along with the promising Italian teenager Honest Ahanor, hasn’t helped. Parish and the sporting director, Matt Hobbs, deserve criticism for not bringing in more experienced replacements, with the latter’s position also thought to be under heavy scrutiny. Sage has also had to deal with unhappy attackers in Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, who made no secret of their desire to leave Selhurst Park in the summer. EA

Quite a lot. Given his late arrival, Jaissle had limited influence over Wilson’s eight summer signings. He has, though, apparently swiftly decided that Aladji Bamba (£34m from Monaco) and Bazoumana Touré (£43m from Hoffenheim) are not ready to be thrown into Premier League combat. Similarly, the fleet-footed £51m former Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo looks as if he is going to need time to adjust. Newcastle’s policy of generally recruiting players under 25 dictates the dressing room is a little light on leadership. Meanwhile iIt is hard to say whether the manager’s high-intensity training bears any responsibility for a lengthy injury list, with Anthony Elanga, Tino Livramento and Jacob Ramsey notable absentees. LT

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Matias Fernandez-Pardo, seen here rounding Coventry keeper Carl Rushworth but failing to score, will need time to adjust to the Premier League. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

How important is winning this game?

After seeing positive signs against Besiktas, as Mateta scored on his first start since the opening day, three points on Sunday will be crucial for Sage. Yet while Palace haven’t lost to Newcastle at home since November 2020, Jaissle’s side have had extra time to prepare and will present a difficult challenge. EA

Given that Newcastle are 11th it is far from imperative. And yet after a demoralising 4-1 defeat at Coventry and a 1-0 home reverse against Aston Villa, victory would offer much-needed reassurance regarding the team’s potential and boost player confidence, not to mention quieten the social-media noise surrounding Jaissle and his tactics. LT

Are there any reasons for optimism?

Palace’s summer net spend of almost £40m in profit was the second lowest in the Premier League behind Aston Villa. They also have American owners who are estimated to be worth a combined £10bn. But Parish revealed last month that he is still looking for extra funding for the new main stand at Selhurst Park, with Woody Johnson, Josh Harris and David Blitzer thought to be open to selling their shares after Palace enlisted Raine Group to seek fresh investment in the club. So there is plenty riding on making sure there is no prospect of being relegated. Sage showed at Lens that he is capable of building a winning team and needs time to do that. EA

Yes, quite a few. Jaissle, understandably, does not want to overplay the 18-year-old central midfielder Sean Steur but the summer signing from Ajax is a joy to watch, has a wonderful passing range and looks capable of reaching the top. Lewis Hall, the England left-back, looks to be going from strength to strength and is capable of elevating standards. Despite an undoubted dogmatic streak, Jaissle appears intelligent – and humble – enough to learn from his mistakes and make necessary adjustments. Club insiders cite his refreshing willingness to listen. Newcastle also possess several extremely quick attacking players – and, as coaches rarely tire of pointing out: “If you’ve got pace, you’ve got a chance.” LT

Sports.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
Sports.content:
Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024, the midfielder entered – and won – a running race.

Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor.

Gross was moving from Brighton to Borussia Dortmund after seven years in the Premier League and reported to his boyhood club for pre-season training days later. Running is an obsession for Gross, as it is for his former teammate James Milner, who revealed last month he was training for a marathon after finally hanging up his boots, and that has shown since he returned for a second spell at the Amex in January for a bargain £1.2m.

“I think he’s looking in his free time now: ‘Where can I run a race?’ Because he will never stand still,” joked Brighton’s head coach, Fabian Hürzeler, after the 35-year-old scored the opening goal in a 3-0 victory over Arsenal last month. “ During the off-season he’s never the person who can lay on the beach for several hours and do nothing. He always needs to do something.”

Given that Gross has this season racked up an average distance of more than 11.5km per match and has covered the third-most ground of any player in the Premier League, it is no surprise Hürzeler has compared his compatriot to a good wine: “The older the wine gets, the better it gets.”

That analysis is borne out by the rest of his statistics this season as Brighton have emerged as challengers for Champions League qualification, at the very least, before Sunday’s game at Liverpool. Not only has Gross, the Premier League’s player of the month for September, contributed a combined seven goals and assists, he is in the top five for several other metrics such as big chances created (six), chances created from open play (14) and line-breaking passes leading to a goal (three). In a team that have scored the fourth-most goals (23) in Premier League history after seven games, Gross has been the standout performer.

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross (in white) up against Jablonec's Matej Polidar in the Conference League. The match finished 0-0. Photograph: David W Cerny/Reuters

“Sometimes he’s just one step ahead than his opponent,” said Hürzeler, who is understood to have been instrumental in bringing back Gross. “He might not be the quickest player, but he can be the quickest in the head and sometimes being the quickest in the head is very helpful. No one expected that it would be this good. But it also shows that he still has this capacity in his body.”

At a club where experience is valued despite Hürzeler being the youngest permanent manager in the Premier League’s history, insiders describe Gross as the perfect role model for some of Brighton’s younger players. Charalampos Kostoulas has scored three goals in his past four league matches and the 19-year-old Greece striker is clearly thriving alongside the man who is approaching 300 appearances for the club. Diego Gómez, the dynamic Paraguayan who scored a goal-of-the-season contender against Crystal Palace that will go down in Brighton folklore, the homegrown talent Jack Hinshelwood and the midfield linchpin Yasin Ayari are others benefiting from his vast experience, as is Hürzeler.

Gross managed 75 Brighton goals and assists after joining from Ingolstadt in 2017 in the summer when Brighton were promoted. His departure for Dortmund, a year after his first Germany cap, was to fulfil a boyhood dream but there was always something drawing Gross – who wears a long-sleeve shirt owing to a grass allergy – back to the club where he is known as the Kaiser.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It was really difficult,” Gross said of his Brighton exit. “Only something really special got me out of here. There were a couple of other options [before returning], but Brighton was always the priority. I just stayed in touch with all the lads over the time away. Maybe you watch less of the games or you don’t stay in touch as much any more, it gets less and less. But it never really did.”

Gross retiring from international football after the World Cup has also been to Brighton’s benefit. His status as a club legend was augmented by delivering the free-kick that Palace’s Jaydee Canvot headed into his own net during the 5-0 humiliation on Sunday. That was the third game in a row in which Gross has provided an assist and he has an opportunity to become the oldest player to make it four since Chelsea’s Gianfranco Zola in December 2002.

The trip to Anfield continues a gruelling run of five away fixtures in a row. Brighton drew at the Czech club Jablonec on Thursday in the Conference League and after Sunday they go to Manchester City twice in four days – the first in the Carabao Cup – before heading to Spain to play Getafe. It will test Brighton’s mettle after their spectacular start. Hürzeler can count on Gross – who has started every game in all competitions – to last the course.

Sports.title: LIV Golf exodus continues as Ryder Cup stars become latest big names to ditch struggling breakaway tour
Sports.content:
Tyrrell Hatton and Ian Poulter have joined the LIV Golf exodus in a one-two punch that will severely weaken the league’s chances of survival.

The European Ryder Cup stars have followed Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Louis Oosthuizen in steering away from plans for a rebranded LIV 2.0.

With LIV currently locked in chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings and needing to retain a certain amount of their talent roster to secure promises of future funding, the big-name departures are each landing like a hammer blow. While Bryson DeChambeau has been tight-lipped on his future, there is an acceptance within golf that if he too chooses to jump ship, LIV will be finished.

Hatton, who departure had been widely anticipated and made all but certain once the DP World Tour inferred recently that there would be no route to the Ryder Cup for those on LIV next season, said: '(I) wanted to confirm that I will not be a part of LIV 2.0. A big thank you to everyone for their continued support. I am excited for what the next chapter of my career holds.’ He is expected to return to a full-time schedule on the DP World Tour.

Poulter’s exit, also announced on Friday, doesn’t carry nearly as much clout but he was with LIV from its inception in 2022 and the 50-year-old won’t be the last to go. It is well known that Cameron Smith and Joaquin Niemann are also studying escape routes, which has been the natural consequence of the Saudi Arabian decision to withdraw its backing in April.

The picture around Lee Westwood is less clear, with Richard Bland, Cameron Tringale and Brendan Steele among the few players to commit to the league.

Ian Poulter says he wants to spend more time at home with his family and to travel less

Poulter said: ‘I wanted everyone to hear it direct from me that I have decided to not move forward with being part of LIV 2.0. Needless to say, it was a tough decision and one I thought about and discussed at length with my family and team.

‘Ultimately, the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests was something that I felt was right for me at this stage of my life and career.

‘I'm looking forward to spending more time with my family, continuing to develop The Postman YouTube channel, sharing more of my life, golf, experiences and competing in some senior events.

‘Something I am also particularly looking forward to is being able to spend more time helping [eldest son], Luke as he pursues his career in professional golf, and [youngest son] Joshua as he looks to develop as a golfer in his teenage years.’

Sports.title: New York Knicks slammed after staffers are 'denied NBA championship rings in cruel fake email ploy'
Sports.content:
The New York Knicks ring ceremony on Tuesday night rang hollow for some staff and coaches at Madison Square Garden after the team used the promise of championship jewelry as the backdrop for a cruel phishing test.

Joe Vardon of the Athletic reported that longtime employees at Madison Square Garden - including some that work for the Knicks business operations - would not be receiving rings at all. It's common for most employees of NBA teams to receive rings, however, they are usually not the same quality as the ones received by players and coaches.

But, according to the outlet, those employees discovered the decision at the end of September when the Knicks sent an email to a long list of employees. Recipients of that email got a first glimpse of their would-be championship rings.

'Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here,' read the email, obtained by The Athletic. '(Employee name), this one is on the house. MSG is issuing a complimentary employee championship ring. The same jeweler, the same craftsmanship, personalized with your name. No cost to you.

'There are two designs to choose from: Championship Gold and Garden Classic. Reserve the one you want below.'

However, when employees clicked the link at the bottom of the message to choose their ring, they were automatically flagged by the company and forced to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class.

Some Knicks staffers were fooled by a cruel internal phishing test which falsely promised them championship rings and instead were forced to take cybersecurity courses, per The Athletic

Additionally, the outlet says no assistant coaches received rings - only empty boxes

New York Knicks guard Jose Alvarado looks at his 2025-26 World Champions ring

Sources told The Athletic that this was done to 'satisfy some of [owner James] Dolan's growing cybersecurity concerns.'

A statement from an MSG Sports spokesperson later clarified: 'The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers.

'MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack. Using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake.

'The company is gifting more than 275 championship rings and jewelry to players, coaches, employees and other members of the Knicks family, worth more than $3.7 million, in recognition of their contributions and celebrating this achievement.'

Before the statement was released, the Knicks had been widely slammed online for the 'cruel' ploy.

One fan wrote: 'This is kind of breaking my heart what a cruel thing to do in the face of joy', while another said: 'You have to be a truly terrible person to do this.'

A further post read: 'I get phising emails all the time. Teasing them with rings is just f***ing cruel' and 'All of this is legitimately insane. What an incredibly cruel and humiliating thing to do.'

Even the coaches who rightfully won rings didn't receive them on the night of the ring ceremony, multiple sources told The Athletic.

Team president Leon Rose was the first person to get a ring during the Knicks' on-court ceremony, opening the black box he was given to reveal a sparkling ring specially designed by jeweler Jason of Beverly Hills. But when those same boxes were handed to the Knicks' assistant coaching staff, they were empty.

Two sources told The Athletic that those assistants were informed earlier on Tuesday they wouldn't get their rings that evening. The outlet added that assistants had not been fitted for rings prior to the event.

Those sources 'described assistants' reactions to not getting rings ranging from genuine anger to annoyance.'

Sources told The Athletic that those coaches were told they would receive championship rings eventually.

The outlet also says they received 'conflicting information about whether head coach Mike Brown received his ring on Tuesday and could not immediately verify if he got one.'

Sports.title: Premier League star refuses to take the knee AGAIN: Ipswich defender Issa Diop rejects anti-racism gesture ahead of clash with Nottingham Forest amid growing doubts over its impact
Sports.content:
Ipswich Town's Issa Diop refused to take the knee on Friday night, snubbing the Premier League's anti-racism gesture.

Diop was the only player among the 22 on the pitch to remain standing as Nottingham Forest's starters and his own team-mates all opted to take part at Portman Road.

Premier League players have been given the opportunity to take the knee across two weekends this month in an effort to challenge discrimination.

Diop is one of six players in the Premier League who have decided not to participate, citing growing concerns about the impact and effectiveness of the 'Say No to Racism' campaign.

During the last round of fixtures, Leeds' Dominic Calvert-Lewin chose to remain standing, while parts of Elland Road booed the gesture.

And on Friday evening, moments before the first game of the eighth round of fixtures, Diop stuck out in the heart of Ipswich's defence as those around him sunk to the turf.

Issa Diop (right) can be seen standing while other players take the knee prior to Ipswich Town's clash with Nottingham Forest on Friday night

His defiant move mirrored his actions last week before Ipswich's game against Man City, while opposition centre-back Marc Guehi also chose to stand.

Everton's Ainsley Maitland-Niles also refused to take the knee and was the only player to do so before Everton's game against Chelsea at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Bournemouth's Rayan and Tyler Adams were the two others who refused to take the knee, but more could follow over this weekend's matches.

Diop has not spoken publicly about his stance but the move has divided players, some of whom view it as a hollow gesture.

When asked about Calvert-Lewin's viewpoint last week, Leeds manager Daniel Farke explained his striker's thinking, saying: 'Dom is more or less like, "No, I don't go down. I show my respect by standing up."

'Every individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way. It's definitely a good campaign and a good topic that football and sports, in general, support situations like this because a dressing room is a perfect example of how we should all live together.

'Different passports, different languages, different religions, but they are all together as human beings and friends who work together toward one target. This is how the world should be.'

Every other player on the pitch at Portman Road took the knee while Diop remained standing

The campaign was previously enacted before every game until it stopped in August 2022 having been started in the UK in 2020 following the death of George Floyd in US police custody, which sparked the Black Lives Matter movement.

Subsequently, a decision was made to limit the gesture to match rounds falling during the No Room For Racism initiative.

It was agreed ahead of the season among Premier League captains that they would continue to perform the gesture twice over 38 rounds.

While the vast majority of players have taken part, some strong opposition has been voiced, notably by Wilfried Zaha in 2021, who said: 'I feel like taking the knee is degrading, because growing up my parents just let me know that I should be proud to be black no matter what and I feel like we should just stand tall.'

And last year, the Lionesses chose not to kneel before their Euro 2025 semi-final against Italy following racist abuse aimed at defender Jess Carter on social media.

Captain Lucy Bronze said the anti-racism message is not 'as strong as it used to be' following the abuse of her team-mate.

'It was driven by the group – obviously certain individuals more than others,' Bronze explained. 'I think it was just the fact that we feel as a collective, is the message as strong as it used to be? Is the message really hitting hard? Because to us it feels like it's not if these things are still happening to our players in the biggest tournaments of their lives.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles was one of six Premier League players who refused to take the knee last weekend, pictured standing ahead of Everton's 2-0 defeat against Chelsea on Saturday

'It's about putting another statement out there to say, it's something that still is a problem, it's something that still needs to be put right. More needs to be done in football, more needs to be done in society. What that is right now as an individual, I don't exactly know.'

But the head of football's international anti-discrimination body, Fare, questioned the Lionesses' decision to stop taking the knee.

Piara Powar told BBC Sport: 'The players have taken a decision to stop taking the knee, which is their right.

'Personally don't see the link between the two. The taking of the knee is a powerful anti-racist act and this England team have shown leadership across Europe in taking it for so long.

'Powerful actions are needed right now, to deal with the issues that are being played out as we speak.'

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's five-minute monologue: Under-fire boss admits Man United have 'lost our way', demands 'humility' from Bruno Fernandes and Co and refuses to say if he'll keep the captaincy
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's five-minute monologue: Under-fire boss admits Man United have 'lost our way', demands 'humility' from Bruno Fernandes and Co and refuses to say if he'll keep the captaincy

Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick claimed that the club have 'lost our way' in a five-minute opening speech to the media ahead of their crunch clash with Bournemouth.

There is increasing uncertainty surrounding Carrick's future at Old Trafford following United's humiliating 4-1 defeat away at Como in the Champions League on Wednesday evening.

The defeat by the beautiful lakes of Italy extended United's winless run to seven games in all competitions, with the club not having tasted victory since early September.

The 45-year-old is set to take charge of the Red Devils as they take on the Cherries on Sunday and in his pre-match press conference ahead of the match, Carrick spoke from the heart.

'I'll start today. I just want to say a few things, really,' said Carrick. 'Recently, we haven't had a good time. I think that's pretty obvious. So I totally accept what we're going through at the moment.

'We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things I was seeing and that we were doing as a team. We haven't done well enough lately. We've had a spell that we're really not happy with.

Michael Carrick gave a passionate near-six minute address to the media on Friday afternoon

'Wednesday was a bad night. It was a bad night for a lot of reasons. It hurt a lot.

'It obviously hurt me to see us play that way, to see how the game panned out. As I said after the game, it was really unacceptable.

'The supporters are a huge part of this football club. They have to make the effort and the time and money they spend, to feel how we all felt on Wednesday was a tough moment.'

During the impassioned speech, Carrick seemingly issued a call to arms directly to his current squad by saying that Manchester United is 'bigger than any single individual', even listing names of legends such as Sir Alex Ferguson and Sir Bobby Charlton when making his point.

And while Carrick is happy to 'hold the umbrella to keep everyone else dry', he also wants his players to step up and reach the levels demanded by the 20-time champions.

Carrick continued: 'We need to respect this football club and respect what it means to be here, respect what it takes to win, what you have to do to win.

'I'm not entitled to be here. Entitlement cannot be at this football club. We're not entitled to win. We've won in the past, we've got an incredible history, but that doesn't mean that you're entitled to just win.

'I'm fully aware of that. It takes hard work, takes a lot of sacrifice. You've got to invest yourself in the football club and you've got to do a lot of things that maybe aren't so nice, but you've got to do it for each other, and you've got to win.

United are winless in seven games after being humiliated by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday

Carrick refused to say whether had had spoken to Bruno Fernandes since his captain questioned the head coach's tactics

'I think it's important we live up to that, and it's important for me to push those values, and it's important for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

'We've had it, we've kind of lost our way a little bit if I'm totally honest, and we will get it back. I'm totally convinced we'll get it back. Respect this football club, respect what it takes, because it's very, very important to me.'

Following the speech, Carrick was asked to address whether he is considering stripping Bruno Fernandes of the club captaincy after the midfielder questioned his tactics following the defeat to Como. He refused to answer directly.

However, Carrick claimed that the dressing room is 'not divided' despite the outspoken nature of Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez in recent weeks.

Martinez was first to break ranks, taking aim at his Old Trafford bosses – and director of football Jason Wilcox in particular – following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last week. Fernandes then followed suit to question why United were so passive again.

He said: 'It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.'

Asked if he meant that Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: 'That's on the manager and staff to say, not me.

‘Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with Como, the centre back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.

‘A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide.’

Sports.title: Bukayo Saka is ruled out for up to EIGHT weeks in huge blow for Arsenal - but Mikel Arteta rejects fears that injury-hit star will suffer career burnout
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka is set to miss six to eight weeks with a thigh injury.

The 25-year-old picked up the knock just ten minutes into Arsenal's Champions League clash against Bayern Munich on Wednesday night.

Saka was helped off the pitch by medical staff and now faces a period on the sidelines. The latest injury is his 11th since September 2024, having also played through a prolonged Achilles issue during the World Cup.

When asked if Saka has lost some of his robustness, Arteta replied: 'Well it's certainly been different in the last year or so and obviously the demands that we are putting to every player are immense.

'The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.

'So look at us now, we have to play on Sunday afternoon, then we have to go away, we have to play on Wednesday evening, then we have to play on Saturday.

Bukayo Saka is to have an MRI scan after limping off injured in 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich

'So you go less than 66, 67 hours between games. On top of everything that we are putting every hour is important. If they (football authorities) can support all the demands that we are putting to the players in that sense, that would be as well really appreciated from everybody.

'And I'm saying for every team as well, because we know what we are demanding from those players.'

He added: 'He's got another MRI this afternoon because he had quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury. We will know more probably tomorrow.

'Again we need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. Obviously when a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, he's restricted to movement, they are not good signs.'

Though on whether Saka could get burnt out by the time he reaches his 30s, he added: 'I don't have that feeling at all.

'But certainly what we have to be very mindful of is to create the right ecosystem around the player to fulfil all his qualities.

'And we really need to understand now when he comes back, whenever that is, how we are going to manage that load again.'

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing at Bayern Munich's training ground
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany has been taken to hospital after collapsing while watching Bayern Munich's second team train on Friday.

Kompany, 40, has been suffering from a viral infection which is said to have caused problems with old scar tissue, leaving him in pain and with difficulties climbing stairs.

BILD report that a 'rescue helicopter' had landed at Bayern's training ground on Friday. The former captain of Manchester City, who won four Premier League titles, later went to hospital in an ambulance and is said to be in a stable condition.

Kompany had collapsed as he watched the club's second string. He had earlier taken training for the first team ahead of their Bundesliga clash against Freiburg on Sunday.

The session was then abandoned, BILD said, with those present said to be 'deeply affected' by the incident.

Bayern said in a statement: 'Vincent Kompany had to seek medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during training for FC Bayern's amateurs.

Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital by ambulance from Bayern Munich's training ground

Kompany is pictured with his wife Carla at Oktoberfest in Munich last month

'The first-team coach had been watching the second team's session. Kompany will undergo thorough examination in the hospital and remain in medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage training and match operations.'

Bayern's sporting director, Max Eberl, added: 'The health of Vincent Kompany is our utmost priority. At FC Bayern, we will do everything to ensure he recovers quickly.

'Vinnie is receiving all necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs. His coaching team, which we fully trust, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery.'

After the 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, Kompany said: 'As a coach, you always want to do everything and accomplish everything. I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body, and then at some point my body said, "Stop now!"'

Kompany had missed training sessions and a press conference in the build-up to the Arsenal game but was present on the touchline on the night.

He also watched Bayern's previous game, a 6-1 win against RB Leipzig, from the bench but did not conduct interviews afterwards.

The Belgian was captain of Man City during some of their most successful years under Pep Guardiola but was regularly ruled out through injuries.

Kompany moved to Munich in 2024 and has won two Bundesliga titles with England captain Harry Kane as his star player in attack. He has three children with wife Carla, who he met in Manchester.

His viral infection was the talk of the build-up before Wednesday's Champions League match.

Kompany's assistant coach Aaron Danks said on Tuesday: 'It has affected his legs, yes. He has had pain in his legs.

'The most important thing for him now is to rest and I don't know if he will be ready tomorrow or in two or three days' time.

'Getting him to rest is hard. He's a leader. But it's a virus and it's really important that he rests.'

Bayern are top of Germany's Bundesliga after four wins and two draws in their opening six matches. They lie 14th in the Champions League's league phase after a win and two draws.

Sports.title: Former Man United star Brandon Williams joins League Two side - as he attempts to rebuild his career after dangerous driving conviction
Sports.content:
Former Man United star Brandon Williams joins League Two side - as he attempts to rebuild his career after dangerous driving conviction

Former Manchester United star Brandon Williams has joined League Two side Rotherham United on a short-term deal.

Williams, 26, has been training with the club since pre-season in an attempt to get his career back on track, and he has now penned a three-month contract.

Rotherham described Williams as 'a full-back and forward-thinking defender with incredibly impressive pedigree' who 'joins having worked hard throughout pre-season and into late October.'

The Millers are now managed by Alex Bruce, son of veteran manager Steve, while former United coach Steve McClaren, who served as assistant to Sir Alex Ferguson and later Erik ten Hag at Old Trafford, is also their Head of Football.

Speaking after Williams' arrival was confirmed, Bruce was full of praise for his perseverance and mindset.

'I'm really pleased he's a Rotherham player, he deserves the contract,' he said. 'He's worked really, really hard with us since pre-season.

Former Man United star Brandon Williams has joined League Two side Rotherham United

Williams, 26, was sentenced to a 14-month jail term, suspended for two years, in May 2025

'He's shown a great attitude every day, he's shown an appetite and a hunger just to play. And he's had a tough few years.

'I've really wanted, not that you want to give contracts out willy-nilly, but when someone has shown the appetite, the desire and the hunger to come in every day and not get paid like he has done, especially given where he's been and what kind of career he has had.

'I'm really pleased to get him in and give him the opportunity to get his career to kickstart.'

Williams made 51 appearances for United after coming through their youth academy, but he has endured a difficult period over recent years.

In May 2025, the full-back was handed a 14-month prison sentence, suspended for two years, after crashing his Audi A3 at almost 100mph on August 20, 2023. He was convicted of dangerous driving.

Williams, who was once paid £3.4million a year as a promising young defender, had been 'driving erratically' in his Audi A3 before hitting a Ford Fiesta and careering into the central reservation of the A34 in Cheshire.

Williams didn't play a professional game for 20 months before he signed for Hull City in August last year, 14 months after United released him.

However, that move didn't work out and he left the Tigers by mutual consent in February after making just one five-minute substitute appearance.

The 26-year-old originally broke into United's first team under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer during the 2019-20 season and impressed, before he began to struggle. He subsequently spent time on loan at both Norwich and Ipswich.

Speaking in May 2025, Williams said that he wanted to be '100 per cent focused' on his football again and 'kick on' with a new club, wherever that may be.

'It hurts me watching football now because I just want to be there, I just want to play. I miss being in a team, on the coach, travelling to games, having meals together and just doing things,' he said.

'I want to have that feeling again of winning and being around the changing room environment.

'I've had loads of teams trying to get me out - America, Europe and England - but I haven't been ready. I want to go somewhere 100 per cent focused and kick on.

'I would like to experience that different culture. I'm only 24 so I could do three or four years abroad. Definitely Europe at a good club or an upcoming club.'

Williams has played just five minutes of football in the past two seasons but is hoping to revive his career

In regards to his car crash, Williams admitted he had been trying to show off to a female passenger who was sitting next to him, and a witness is said to have filmed him with a balloon by his mouth. Prosecutors said it was 'fortunate' nobody was seriously injured or killed.

Judge Eric Lamb also banned Williams from driving for three years and ordered him to do 180 hours of unpaid work.

The homegrown United talent announced in June 2024 that he would leave the club at the end of his contract, and when the incident took place - in August 2023 - Williams had been on loan at Ipswich.

Speaking in August in a wide-ranging interview with the Athletic, Williams expressed his remorse at his behaviour.

'It made me grow up as a person and realise that this is real life, this isn’t GTA (Grand Theft Auto) or something like that,' Williams said.

'It was a proper wake-up call. Since then it was about building and changing a reputation that I had and that’s not me.

'I look back at myself now and think what an idiot I was. That is not what an athlete does, it’s not what a footballer does, it’s not what a grown man does. It’s stupid stuff.'

He added: 'I’ve let a lot of people down, to be honest, and I want to prove a lot of people wrong as well.

'That’s one thing that is left to do in my life, to get back onto the football pitch and show what I can do.'

Sports.title: Tearful Simone Biles struggles to come to terms with quick sale of $1M mansion she shared with NFL star husband
Sports.content:
Tearful Simone Biles struggles to come to terms with quick sale of $1M mansion she shared with NFL star husband

Simone Biles broke down in tears as she said an emotional goodbye to her stunning Texas home where she spent six years alongside NFL star husband Jonathan Owens.

The 29-year-old took to TikTok to share the bittersweet moment with fans after the 3,998sq ft property was snapped up just four days after hitting the market.

'Why the f*** am I boohoo crying? F***,' Biles said through tears as she panned around the empty residence.

'This house will be on the market for the first time and I don't know why I'm boohoo crying. I was here for six years and I feel like there were so many good memories.

'I feel like I grew up in this house. It's made me a real adult so I'm going to miss it. Ugh, I didn't think I'd be emotional about a house', the gymnastics icon added.

Biles walked through the vacant rooms before stepping outside to the spacious backyard before sharing a warm message for the future homeowners.

Simone Biles broke down in tears as she said an emotional goodbye to her Texas home

The 29-year-old took to TikTok to share the bittersweet moment with fans after the 3,998-square-foot property was snapped up just four days after hitting the market

'Whoever buys this house, I hope it brings you as much joy as it did for me', she said.

Biles captioned the video: “I was so excited to put in air fresheners for the potential buyers & showing Jonathan the last look. I just cried instead… anyone else?”

The property was initially listed for $1.275 million before eventually being sold for a fee between $1.08 million and $1.24 million, according to the Houston Association of Realtors.

Spanning nearly 4,000sq ft in a gated community near Spring, Texas, the four-bedroom, 3.5-bathroom estate sits on just over an acre of land.

The luxury residence features a heated backyard swimming pool, an in-home sauna, a dedicated dog-washing station and a custom wine display wall.

Inside, the home boasts a waterfall island kitchen with quartz countertops, a hidden walk-in pantry and an oversized three-car garage.

The property went under contract just four days after the listing went live on September 22, with the sale officially closing on October 15.

The gymnastics icon spent six years in the home alongside NFL star husband Jonathan Owens

Earlier this year, Biles shared a glimpse at the stunning property in a series of online posts

The update comes one month after Biles revealed three masked intruders broke into her Chicago home and stole her luxurious Porsche.

The legendary Team USA gymnast dropped the bombshell news during a TikTok video. It remains unclear when the burglary happened or if the police have made any arrests but Biles confirmed the car was recovered.

'Feel like I need a new car because during our last few months in Chicago, three men in masks came to our house and stole my Porsche,' she said.

'Stole the GTS. But that's another story. If you guys want to know, I'll do a story time on that.'

Sports.title: Man Utd fans sent new stadium survey as 100,000-seater ground gathers pace
Sports.content:
Man Utd fans sent new stadium survey as 100,000-seater ground gathers pace

Manchester United fans will be consulted and have the chance to give their view on the club's new stadium as plans continue over a new venue for the club

View 2 Images Man Utd have signalled their plans to build a new 100,000-capacity stadium (Image: Foster and Partners / SWNS)

Manchester United will involve fans in a survey as they get the chance to feedback on the club's plans for a new 100,000-seater stadium, with concept images already being released.

‌



‌



The controversial ‘circus tent’ design is only an impression of what the finished venue could look like and the plans are not set in stone, and could still be influenced by what fans say.

‌



Supporters have been invited to take part in a number of focus groups to discuss key details which could help decide on how the new state-of-the-art stadium takes shape.

‌



The survey will be distributed to season ticket holders, cup season ticket holders, executive members, official members and supporters who have purchased hospitality within the last three years. It will close at 12pm on Friday November 6, reports The Sun.

‌



Collette Roche, CEO, New Stadium Development, said: “Our proposed new stadium is one of the most significant projects Manchester United will undertake in the next 100 years, and it is vital that we shape it together with our fans.

“Above all else, this is a football stadium built for them, so getting the details right matters. We are committed to thorough and transparent engagement, ensuring supporters help inform key decisions on atmosphere, affordability, accessibility and the traditions that have made Old Trafford so special for so long.”

‌



“By working together, we can create a world-class football stadium that supports success on the pitch, reflects the identity of Manchester United, and gives fans a home they can be proud of for generations to come.”

View 2 Images Man Utd fans will be given the chance to influence the new stadium

‌



The club have also said there will be further opportunities for fans to provide their views on other major topics, one of those being pricing, which continues to be a hot topic after some controversial decisions taken by Ineos, who have removed concession prices.

Despite the obvious emotional attachment to Old Trafford it is well documented that the stadium, once renowned as one of Europe's best, has fallen well behind the standard set by the modern stadia. That owing to a continued lack of investment, but Ineos have looked to revamp the club's infrastructure, recently presiding over major improvements to the training ground.

Sports.title: Bukayo Saka delivers Arsenal huge injury blow as extent of thigh issue revealed
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka delivers Arsenal huge injury blow as extent of thigh issue revealed

Arsenal star Bukayo Saka could be out until December with a thigh injury sustained in Wednesday night's Champions League draw at Bayern Munich

View 2 Images Saka is set to be out until December (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Bukayo Saka has delivered Arsenal a huge blow and could be out until December with a thigh injury sustained in the Gunners' draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday night.

‌



‌



Saka is undergoing further scans on the injury which will determine the exact lay-off but Arsenal are already resigned to Saka being out for several weeks.

‌



The England star will also miss the Three Lions' Nations League fixtures next month including the group decider in Spain on November 15 after another massive setback.

‌



Incredibly, this is Saka’s 11th injury since September 2024 and is a huge blow for Arsenal’s title defence and Champions League games as he will be sweating on being ready to face Real Madrid at the Emirates on December 9.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He will definitely miss the Gunners' trip to Anfield on November 1. Manchester City travel to the Emirates on November 29 and it's the north London derby at Tottenham a week later.

Arteta said: “When a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, he's restricted to movement, they are not good signs.

‌



“He's got another MRI this afternoon because he had quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury. We will know more probably tomorrow."

Arteta insisted he does not fear that Saka is suffering from burnout but admits that he has become a “different” player and he may be in danger of losing some of his robustness.

‌



View 2 Images Saka will miss England's Nations League fixtures in November (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

Arteta said: “Well, it's certainly been different in the last year or so. Obviously the demands that we are putting to every player are immense.

‌



“The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.

“So look at us now, we have to play on Sunday afternoon, then we have to go away, we have to play on Wednesday evening, then we have to play on Saturday. So you go less than 66, 67 hours between games.

‌



“On top of everything that we are putting, every hour is important. If they can support all the demands that we are putting to the players in that sense, that would be as well really appreciated from everybody.

“And I'm saying for every team as well, because we know what we are demanding from those players."

Sports.title: Man Utd manager candidate reminded of 'big blows' as ex-boss criticises previous record
Sports.content:
Man Utd manager candidate reminded of 'big blows' as ex-boss criticises previous record

Julian Nagelsmann has been warned against taking the Manchester United job by Oliver Kahn, who cited the lack of managerial continuity at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Julian Nagelsmann has been linked with Manchester United (Image: Joosep Martinson - FIFA, FIFA via Getty Images)

Germany legend Oliver Kahn has told Julian Nagelsmann to avoid the Manchester United job - and has commented on his recent exploits, which have somewhat underwhelmed.

‌



‌



He is understood to be one of the favourites to takeover from Michael Carrick. The current Red Devils manager will be in charge for this weekend's clash against Bournemouth, but that has not stopped the rumours about potential candidates from appearing. Nagelsmann and Aston Villa manager Unai Emery are believed to be the two favourites for the United position.

‌



The former is a free agent having left his position as manager of Germany after they were knocked out of the World Cup round of 32 by Paraguay in shocking fashion. But as the links continue to appear, Kahn believes Nagelsmann should think twice before moving to Old Trafford.

‌



He said: "From his point of view, it's not an easy situation. He isn't someone with a great deal of experience, particularly when it comes to foreign teams."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



On the RTL/Sky Germany show Triple - der Hagedorn Fußballtalk, Kahn added: "The Premier League and Manchester United have not been known for much continuity in the managerial position in recent years.

"He has to ask himself, 'What is my next step? Does it have to be the right one? Or do I immediately associate it with an enormous risk like Manchester United, where essentially every manager in recent years has failed sooner or later?'

‌



"You should look very carefully at where you're going. Bayern Munich and the national team were already big blows for him. You have to think carefully, 'Where do my strengths lie? Which club can I really help?' I think Julian is someone who can develop a club and a team and take them further. Whether Manchester United are the right next step for that is something only he can know."

View 2 Images Kahn warned Nagelsmann about United (Image: Alex Grimm, Getty Images)

‌



Nagelsmann was always tipped to eventually lead a major outfit, and he was given the Bayern job in 2021. He claimed the Bundesliga title in his first season, but has knocked out of the German Cup in the second round, losing 5-0 to Borussia Monchengladbach.

They were also shocked in the Champions League, losing on aggregate to Villarreal who scored their crucial goal in the 88th minute at the Allianz Arena. He failed to see out his second year, being axed in late March with Bayern choosing to appoint Thomas Tuchel.

Article continues below

Nagelsmann did land the Germany job in 2023 but underwhelmed in two major tournaments. They were knocked out of a home Euros in the last eight by winners Spain. This summer their World Cup hopes ended at the hands of Paraguay in the Round of 32, who beat them on penalties.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick makes Man Utd vow in emotional six-minute speech as pressure mounts
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick makes Man Utd vow in emotional six-minute speech as pressure mounts

Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick launched an emotional monologue before taking questions ahead of the Red Devils' clash with Bournemouth

View 2 Images Michael Carrick opened his press conference by addressing the team's current state of affairs

Michael Carrick began his Manchester United press conference with a six-minute passionate speech where he reminded his players that the club was "built on hard work, and we should never forget that."

‌



‌



The Red Devils boss is under pressure having won just two of his opening 11 games, with their most recent outing being a 4-1 reverse at the hands of Como in the Champions League.

‌



Carrick was then called out by his captain Bruno Fernandes, who suggested that the failed tactics were down to him, with the United boss taking the unusual step of beginning his press conference without taking any questions, and instead making his own views clear.

‌



The former player turned manager accepted their dire recent results, but made a point to demand more from his players, referencing how so many of the club's greats have put the team before themselves.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Carrick began: "I think it’s important... recently we haven’t had a good time I think that’s obvious, I totally accept that. We had five months of relative success and I was happy with many things I was seeing.

"We haven’t done well enough recently. Wednesday was a bad night for a lot of reasons, it really hurt a lot, it hurt me to see how the game panned out. As I said after the game, it was unacceptable. Supports pay a lot of money to follow the team and to leave with that feeling... My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that the supporters can identify with, and we have gone away from that recently and we need need to something about it.

‌



"It was never about Ryan Giggs, it was never about Ryan Giggs, it was about Manchester United. Wayne Rooney, the greatest goalscorer in the club’s history, he played for team. Sir Alex Ferguson, the greatest manager in the club’s history... Sir Matt [Busby] and Sir Bobby [Charlton], their resilience was beyond belief what they showed and how they rebuilt this football club. It was built on hard work, and we should never forget that."

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has come under fire following Man Utd's defeat to Como in the Champions League. (Image: (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images))

‌



It comes after Carrick, in response to Fernandes' comments after Wednesday's loss, said: "There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."

The United boss will hope to snap their winless run this weekend when his side host Bournemouth, who themselves have struggled for wins this season, and he also underlined that it as "pretty clear" his players need to stop airing their issues publicly after defeats.

Sports.title: Antonio Conte issues statement to 'clarify position' on Man Utd job prospects
Sports.content:
Antonio Conte issues statement to 'clarify position' on Man Utd job prospects

Antonio Conte has posted a statement on social media hitting back at reports he's looking for control and major wages in his next job

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has spoken out against reports about his approach to his next move (Image: Getty Images)

Antonio Conte has come out and rubbished reports that he's making demands for full control during talks over his next job - with the Manchester United hotseat among those he's linked with.

‌



‌



The Italian is out of a job having left Napoli in the summer following two years in the role, winning the Scudetto in his debut season. His stellar CV boasts league titles with Juventus, Chelsea, Inter Milan and the Naples outfit.

‌



All of which have seen him tipped to replace Michael Carrick if United, who have won just two games in 11 to begin the season, opt to make an early change.

‌



In previous roles, Conte has been accused of making major demands to those above, especially when it comes to recruitment and retention, with the Italian previously being outspoken when missing out on specific transfer targets, but the 57-year-old has rubbished those theories.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He said on his social media account: "Following recent media reports in Italy and abroad, I feel it is appropriate to clarify my position. My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage.

"Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

‌



"I have read reports of financial demand and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, ad well as reservations about what has been described as my 'strong personality'. These are reports are unfounded, as here is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

View 2 Images The Italian has never been shy of speaking his mind, calling out his bosses in previous roles (Image: JUSTIN TALLIS, AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"Should a concrete opportunity arise that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager."

Conte's last job in England saw him axed by Tottenham after he took aim at the club for their continued failures. Prior to that he won the title at Chelsea and then delivered the FA Cup, but it was well documented that he missed out on several of his preferred players in his final summer.

Article continues below

The Italian has been linked with the role on the red half of Manchester previously but pundits have been split on whether he would be the right fit, especially given his relatively short stints in recent roles.
