Sports.title: Dalton Smith Talks Lifetime Bans Before Puello Test
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith is putting Alberto Puello’s failed drug test back into the conversation before Saturday’s WBC light welterweight title defense in Sheffield. If the champion loses, an explanation beyond the boxing will already be circulating.

That doesn’t prove Smith is preparing an excuse. But his comments give a difficult first defense a moral storyline before either fighter throws a punch.

Smith called for lifetime bans for fighters who fail drug tests. Puello tested positive for clomiphene in 2023 and received a six-month suspension. The article reports no new failed test ahead of Saturday’s fight.

“I think it stinks. I’m well against it myself,” Smith said to BoxingScene. “But I went in there and proved last time, sometimes you need more than just steroids. I’ll do it for the fighters in the sport that are clean.”

That last sentence turns Smith’s title defense into something bigger than defending his belt. It casts him as fighting on behalf of clean boxers, with Puello’s past providing the backdrop.

Puello’s violation is legitimate history to discuss. It also cannot explain punches, missed opportunities, or lost rounds before they happen.

Smith has a boxing problem to solve here. Puello’s southpaw movement could make him a frustrating opponent for a champion coming off his fifth-round stoppage of Subriel Matias in January.

Matias gave Smith opportunities to meet him with hard shots. Puello could make him work much harder to find those openings. If Smith follows without cutting off the ring, he risks spending rounds pursuing a challenger who refuses to give him the fight he wants.

Smith and Eddie Hearn have ambitions for a Hillsborough Stadium event. Puello could spoil those plans through positioning, timing and making the champion miss.

“If anything, they need lifetime bans, don’t they? But it’s out of my hands,” Smith said.

Saturday’s performance is in his hands. Smith can hold strong views on drug penalties while still being expected to handle an awkward mandatory challenger.

If Puello wins, his work in the ring deserves to be the first subject discussed. Smith’s comments have already supplied another one.

Introducing a moral crusade into fight week sets up an immediate psychological cushion. If Dalton goes out there and gets outboxed, frustrated, or dropped, the post-fight discourse among his local base will not be about his inability to cut off the ring or solve Puello’s southpaw stance. The talk will instantly circle back to: Well, Puello should have never been in that ring anyway because of 2023.

It gives sympathetic observers a pre-packaged storyline to diminish Puello’s ring IQ and shield Smith from the harsh reality of being tactically exposed in his own backyard.

The fantasy of a lifetime ban is quite telling. If the WBC or sanctioning bodies had handed down a permanent ban, Puello would be out of the sport entirely. That would have cleared him off Smith’s mandatory radar, allowing Matchroom to steer Smith toward an easier, straight-line brawler or an accommodating voluntary defense where the Sheffield crowd gets their highlight-reel knockout without the sweat.

Puello represents the classic “high-risk, low-reward” assignment. He does not come forward recklessly like Subriel Matias did; he refuses to stand still, he is awkward, he fights out of the southpaw stance, and he makes opponents look clumsy. When a fighter starts preaching about how their opponent technically should not exist in the division just days before the opening bell, it reveals anxiety about the stylistic nightmare waiting for them.

It is far easier to argue Puello should not be legally permitted in the ring than it is to actually pin him down and beat him for twelve rounds.

Sports.title: Bakhram Murtazaliev Returns December 12 After Kelly Defeat
Sports.content:
Bakhram Murtazaliev is set to return on December 12 on the Dmitry Bivol–Callum Smith undercard in Yekaterinburg, Russia, nearly 11 months after losing his IBF junior middleweight title to Josh Kelly. The former champion needs activity after spending most of 2026 out of the ring.

Dan Rafael first reported Murtazaliev’s involvement in September. His October 20 schedule lists a 10-round junior middleweight bout against an opponent to be announced. Johan Gonzalez has been mentioned in circulating posts, but he should not be treated as the confirmed opponent.

Bivol’s unified light heavyweight title defense against Smith is official for December 12 at UMMC Arena, with DAZN broadcasting the event. That gives Murtazaliev a prominent card for his comeback, although the opponent will determine how much the fight can tell us about his chances of reclaiming a belt.

Murtazaliev lost his title by majority decision against Kelly in Newcastle on January 31. It was his first professional defeat, leaving him with a 23-1 record and 17 knockouts. Kelly has since signed a new Matchroom contract, while Murtazaliev has waited for his next fight.

The inactivity is becoming a familiar issue. Murtazaliev entered the Kelly fight following a lengthy break, and another extended absence gives him little opportunity to correct mistakes under fight conditions. Training can address technique and conditioning, but it cannot replace rounds against an opponent trying to beat him.

A 10-round comeback is a reasonable starting point. He does not need to jump straight into another title fight after a defeat. He does, however, need this appearance to lead somewhere rather than become another isolated booking followed by months of waiting.

Until an opponent is announced, there is little basis for judging the matchmaking. A durable opponent could give Murtazaliev rounds, while a stronger contender would offer a clearer indication of what he has left at world level.

The immediate job is to win in December and secure an earlier return in 2027. One defeat has not ended Murtazaliev’s chances at 154 pounds, but another year built around a single appearance would make the climb back harder.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Targets Pound-for-Pound Spot Against Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster expects a victory over Emanuel Navarrete on Saturday to earn him a pound-for-pound spot. The harder part could be turning that achievement into the audience and bigger paydays he wants.

Foster puts his WBC super featherweight title against Navarrete’s IBF and WBO belts at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. Three titles would give the winner a strong claim as the division’s best fighter, with one belt left to collect.

Speaking to The Ring’s Manouk Akopyan, Foster made his expectations clear.

“I think this win is going to put me on the pound-for-pound list.”

He has a reasonable argument. Foster’s record includes victories over Rey Vargas, Eduardo Hernandez, Stephen Fulton and Raymond Ford. He also avenged his disputed split-decision defeat to Robson Conceicao. Beating Navarrete would add a three-division champion to that list.

The frustrating part for Foster is that he still needs another major win to get the recognition he believes those results should already have earned him.

Navarrete gives him an opportunity to change that. His pressure and punching power create a different test from beating another technical boxer. If Foster can control him over 12 rounds, it becomes harder to dismiss his success as the product of favorable opponents.

However, pound-for-pound recognition and ticket-selling power are separate rewards. A ranking gives Foster something to put beside his name. It doesn’t guarantee that fans will pay to watch his next defense.

How he wins could influence what follows. A disciplined points victory would strengthen his claim among the sport’s best. A performance with knockdowns, drama or a stoppage could reach viewers who haven’t followed his title reign.

That doesn’t mean Foster should abandon the approach that got him here. Trading unnecessarily with Navarrete would give the Mexican champion the kind of fight he wants.

Foster’s first job is to win. After that, his promoters need to turn three belts into an event fans want to watch. If Saturday ends with another impressive victory followed by another quiet promotion, Foster could find himself making the same argument before his next fight.

Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Jr. Faces Keith Thurman With Little Upside
Sports.content:
Vergil Ortiz Jr. gives the December 5 Benavidez–Cieslak DAZN pay-per-view another fighter fans want to watch. Whether Keith Thurman gives them another fight worth buying is a harder sell.

The former unified welterweight champion brings name recognition to the Glendale, Arizona card. His victories over Shawn Porter and Danny Garcia give promoters something familiar to advertise alongside Ortiz’s knockout record. But those wins offer little evidence of what Thurman can produce against an unbeaten puncher at this stage of his career.

Thurman, 37, enters off a sixth-round stoppage loss to Sebastian Fundora in March. He has not fought since. There is no rebuilding victory between that defeat and another dangerous opponent, leaving buyers to judge his chances largely on a performance in which he was thoroughly beaten. premierboxingchampions.com

That is the weakness in presenting Ortiz–Thurman as a major reason to purchase the event. Adding recognizable fighters improves a poster. Adding uncertainty about who wins improves the argument for paying.

Thurman’s best chance would appear to involve making Ortiz work for clean openings: moving, changing direction, and landing counters before getting away. Trading with the younger fighter would invite the kind of sustained punishment Thurman needs to avoid.

Fundora and Ortiz present different challenges. Fundora’s unusual height and reach helped him control Thurman, so that defeat does not establish exactly how this fight will unfold. Ortiz, however, brings his own pressure through body punching, combinations, and the ability to punish an opponent who stays within range.

The concern is whether Thurman can maintain the movement and concentration that approach requires. Doing it for a few early rounds is one thing. Keeping Ortiz from wearing him down over 12 is another.

The announcement also lists this as a middleweight bout, despite Ortiz’s recent work at 154 pounds. That detail deserves attention, although the release does not specify the contracted weight.

For Ortiz, the clearest benefit is finally getting back into the ring after stopping Erickson Lubin in November 2025. A place beneath David Benavidez also puts him in front of an audience that could follow him into bigger fights.

“Overall I’m just happy to be active again,” Ortiz said in the announcement.

That explains accepting a fight. It does less to establish Thurman as the right opponent for a fighter who has already beaten Serhii Bohachuk, Israil Madrimov and Lubin.

Oscar De La Hoya’s sales pitch was revealing: “Keith Thurman is a crafty, experienced fighter who has been in there with the very best and will give Vergil some good rounds.”

“Good rounds” is a modest promise for a pay-per-view co-main event. It sounds like preparation for a bigger fight rather than the bigger fight itself.

Ortiz also faces an uneven reward. A quick stoppage would be expected against an older opponent coming off a stoppage defeat. A difficult night would invite unfavorable comparisons with Fundora. Thurman’s name would go onto Ortiz’s record, but beating him now would add less than beating him during his championship years. Ortiz–Thurman can contribute action, familiarity, and the possibility of another Ortiz knockout.

Some buyers will value that addition. Fans still deciding whether Benavidez–Cieslak deserves their money, however, need a stronger reason to believe the co-main event will be competitive. Thurman’s last performance makes that belief difficult to sell.

Sports.title: Bob Arum Calls Shakur Stevenson’s $15 Million Price Unviable
Sports.content:
Bob Arum believes paying Shakur Stevenson $15 million per fight makes no financial sense unless outside funding covers what the event cannot earn. His explanation for the Zuffa split puts the focus on the price attached to Shakur rather than the difficulty of finding him an opponent.

Arum argued that a promoter has reason to walk away when a fighter’s purse cannot be supported by the business his fights produce.

“If you can get out of that contract, you get out of it,” Arum said to Fight Hub TV. “Did it cost them any money to get out? I don’t know.”

Arum described a $15 million-per-fight arrangement, although his comments do not establish the terms of Shakur’s contract. He also linked the split to what he believes is a reduction in Saudi funding, without providing documentation for that claim.

“To pay Shakur 15 million … financially, it’s not viable,” Arum said.

That is a hard argument for Shakur’s next promoter to avoid. A fighter can ask for any number, but someone has to cover the guarantee. If ticket sales, broadcast income and sponsorship cannot support it, the promoter needs another source of money or accepts a loss.

Arum applied the same reasoning to the failed Devin Haney negotiations. In his view, the amounts promised to both fighters exceeded what their proposed fight could justify.

“The money didn’t exist in the fight that they would have,” he said.

He considered Shakur–Haney a good fight that would interest fans. He still questioned whether that interest would produce enough revenue to cover the costs.

Shakur’s next deal will test whether another promoter sees a business at that price. Arum’s position leaves little room for sentiment: boxing ability can help sell a fight, but a $15 million guarantee still needs paying.

In MMA, Dana White controls athlete compensation tightly to guarantee promotion profitability. Handing out a reported $15 million guarantee for a fighter who historically struggles to sell out arenas outside of Newark or move domestic pay-per-views directly contradicts how Zuffa operates.

Without third-party subsidies covering the spread, Zuffa was looking at absorbing massive, multi-million-dollar losses per event. Once the Haney clash disappeared, Zuffa attempted to switch to realistic opponents that fit the market. When options like Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela were tabled with reduced, market-corrected money around $7 million, Shakur held firm on his premium valuation.

A promoter cannot keep a fighter active when the athlete demands A-side megastar money for B-level volume fights that the public will not buy on pay-per-view. Shakur’s defensive masterclasses appeal to purists, but casual ticket buyers and mainstream sports fans have never embraced that style.

Promoters are willing to swallow astronomical purses for high-risk, high-action punchers who generate viral knockouts and massive live gates. Shakur’s risk-averse, distance-control approach inside the ring made it impossible for Zuffa executives to justify treating him like Canelo Alvarez or Gervonta Davis at the box office.

Sports.title: Hearn Calls Out Haney and Teofimo for Playing Promoter on Other People’s Money
Sports.content:
The Matchroom promoter questioned how much financial responsibility fighters take on when they become promoters. His criticism targets arrangements that give a boxer company recognition and some control while leaving someone else to fund the show.

“What that means is they’re not willing to put one penny into the show, but they want a logo on the poster and they want to hear their name on the announcements and they want to have some input, which is fine,” Hearn said to the media.

Hearn named Haney and Teofimo while discussing their arrangements with DAZN. He suggested their wish to operate promotional companies helped explain how those deals came together quickly.

There are benefits for a fighter in that position. Having a company involved can give him more influence over his career and a share of revenue that might otherwise go to an outside promoter. It also creates a business identity that could continue after retirement.

But putting a logo on a poster is the easy part. Funding purses, selling tickets, employing staff, and absorbing losses require something beyond a company announcement. If another organization handles those responsibilities, the fighter’s role is different from that of a promoter financing an event.

Shakur Stevenson’s stated plans to start his own promotional company make the subject relevant to his next move, too. That does not establish how his business would operate or whether he intends to invest in shows.

Hearn’s comments also leave a question about the arrangements he criticized: he did not supply financial terms showing what Haney or Teofimo contributes or receives.

A fighter can negotiate a better deal without building a promotional operation. The real test comes when his company stages events, signs other boxers, and accepts the possibility of losing money. Until then, the announcement tells us less than the work that follows.

Hearn is telling an inconvenient truth about the current landscape, even if his motives are entirely self-serving.

From an operational standpoint, he is dead on. There is a massive distinction between being a licensed promoter who takes actual financial exposure and operating a vanity boutique. Sticking an LLC graphic in the corner of a promotional graphic, negotiating a co-promotional fee, or demanding that Jimmy Lennon Jr. say a company name in the ring is basically just an athlete branding exercise.

Real promoting is ugly business: underwriting seven-figure guarantees, absorbing production shortfalls, paying sanctioning fees, moving tickets through grassroots footwork, and taking the bath when a gate flops. When DAZN, Matchroom, or Top Rank fronts the operating capital and takes the hit on red ink, the fighter is still an employee with a boutique label attached to their check.

At the same time, Hearn’s frustration is transparent. Traditional promoters used to control fighters by owning the apparatus: the venue deals, the broadcast pipeline, and the financial leverage. Haney, Lopez, and potentially Stevenson are bypassing that old dynamic by exploiting platforms willing to buy content directly.

From a boxer’s perspective, skipping the financial downside while still extracting extra broadcast money and retaining career independence is simply good leverage. If a network or investor allows them to claim promotional clout without putting up escrow, only a fool would voluntarily volunteer their own cash to absorb risk.

The rubber only meets the road when a fighter tries to build an actual stable. Floyd Mayweather backed up Mayweather Promotions because he eventually signed outside talent, staged shows without being the headliner, and cut checks from his own accounts.

Until guys like Haney or Lopez write checks to support younger prospects on untelevised undercards and stomach a six-figure loss on a slow night, Hearn has a valid point: they are prize fighters with vanity logos, not genuine fight promoters.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Gets His Chance Against Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster isn’t agreeing to a slugfest just because Emanuel Navarrete wants one. With three super featherweight titles available Saturday in San Antonio, Foster intends to make Navarrete fight on terms that suit him.

Their comments at Thursday’s press conference supplied an edge to a fight week that has struggled for attention despite the stakes. Navarrete brings the WBO and IBF belts to Frost Bank Center, while Foster puts his WBC title into the unification.

“What I don’t want is an entire night where we’re just jabbing each other to see who can land more jabs. I think people want to see a good fight. They want to see a war,” said Navarrete.

That request benefits Navarrete. A fight fought at close range would give the Mexican champion more opportunities to put his power and unconventional punches to work. Foster has little reason to volunteer for that when his chances depend on making Navarrete miss and pay.

“I don’t fight to other people’s advantages. Whatever he brings to the table, I’ll adjust,” Foster said.

Foster also questioned whether Navarrete would follow through on his own invitation once punches started coming back.

“He don’t really like getting hit, in my opinion,” Foster said. “He’ll trade with you, but we’ll see. If he does that, it’ll be a great night for me.”

The challenge for Foster is turning that confidence into enough clean work to win rounds. Making Navarrete miss alone won’t do it if the more aggressive champion keeps producing the more noticeable offense.

Navarrete said his camp included changes to nutrition and preparation. Saturday will test whether those adjustments help him maintain the pressure needed to keep Foster from controlling the distance.

Foster says he has chased this fight for almost three years. He finally has the opponent he wanted, with the chance to leave holding three belts.

Navarrete generates awkward leverage from every conceivable angle, and trying to trade hook-for-hook with him is exactly how fighters end up getting broken down and stopped. Foster’s entire game relies on reset steps, shoulder rolls, and controlling distance with the jab. The moment he plants his feet to trade, he throws away his only distinct tactical advantages.

In past fights, Foster has shown flat spots down the stretch, letting rounds slip away because he takes his foot off the gas or looks physically soft around the midsection. When fighters carry extra weight between camps, the late rounds invariably expose it.

Against a tireless volume puncher like Navarrete, that physical drop-off is fatal. Navarrete might look unorthodox and technically sloppy, but his output does not decline in rounds nine through twelve. If Foster gets arm-weary or his legs get heavy from carrying that extra padding into the second half of the fight, Navarrete will pin him against the ropes and drown him in punches.

DAZN’s main broadcast begins at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Albert Gonzalez faces Edward Vazquez in the featherweight co-feature, while Frank Martin meets Tarik Zaina at light welterweight.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Advances Talks For Frank Sanchez Defense
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic’s next fight is moving toward a mandatory defense against Frank Sanchez, leaving the IBF heavyweight champion facing a difficult opponent without the payday he had hoped to secure against Daniel Dubois or the Anthony Joshua–Tyson Fury winner.

Mike Coppinger reports that Hrgovic and Sanchez are in advanced talks for a fight in Croatia during the first quarter of 2027. A date and venue have yet to be announced.

Hrgovic won the vacant IBF belt by stopping Moses Itauma, but Sanchez brings a different test. The Cuban is more likely to make Hrgovic work for openings than give him a stationary target for his right hand.

That could make this an awkward homecoming. Hrgovic will have the crowd expecting him to take charge, while Sanchez has reason to slow the action, move and force the champion to keep finding him. Hrgovic would need to apply pressure without spending rounds following the challenger around the ring.

Sanchez previously accepted a step-aside agreement that allowed Hrgovic’s title fight against Itauma to proceed. His opportunity now appears closer, with the two camps discussing a fight that would settle the champion’s mandatory obligation.

For Hrgovic, the danger is looking beyond the opponent directly in front of him. Dubois remains an obvious target because of their previous fight, which handed the Croatian his only professional defeat. Getting another chance at Dubois would offer Hrgovic something a routine title defense cannot: an opportunity to reverse that result.

Sanchez has his own reason to interrupt those plans. A victory in Croatia would give him the IBF belt and put him into the unification discussions Hrgovic wants to pursue.

The homecoming would belong to Hrgovic. Whether he leaves with the same options he brought into the fight would depend on getting past Sanchez first.

Hrgovic absorbed heavy punishment from Itauma before the youngster ran out of gas in the second half of the fight. Sanchez does not carry that flaw. He is a seasoned Cuban amateur with hundreds of rounds in the bank, excellent pacing, and no inclination to sprint early or blow his engine looking for an early knockout.

Stylistically, Sanchez is built to give Hrgovic nightmares. Hrgovic thrives against heavyweights who plant their feet and let him set up his straight right hands. Sanchez will not stand there. He circles, counters, keeps the tempo slow, and relies on slick upper-body movement.

If Hrgovic approaches this the way he did against Dubois or in the early rounds with Itauma, he risks getting picked apart from the outside while walking into sharp counter hooks. The business side makes it even worse.

A stadium fight in Croatia against Sanchez will not generate the massive purse or international buzz of a Dubois rematch or a major Riyadh Season headliner. Yet a loss completely derails Hrgovic, strips away his title, and hands all his leverage in the division straight to Sanchez.

Ghana News.title: My dream collaboration is with Sade – Gyakie
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian music artiste Jackline Acheampong, known professionally as Gyakie, has revealed the artiste she dreams of collaborating with.

Speaking in an interview on Joy Prime’s Changes show, Gyakie named Nigerian-British singer-songwriter Sade as her dream collaborator when asked which artiste she would love to work with next.

“Sade. I’ve gone to the end of the tunnel literally,” she told the host, Nikki Samonas.

Explaining the reason behind her ambition, Gyakie stated that Sade’s lyrics and vocal tone are centred on love, a quality she believes they have in common.

“Her lyrics, and you know her most of her songs are love songs that’s what draws me closer to her sound, lyrics, tone. I see my sound in her sound as well and I think we’ll really sound good if it ever happens.”

Helen Folasade Adu, known professionally as Sade, is one of the most successful British female artists in history. She is widely recognised for her influence on contemporary music and is known for songs such as Smooth Operator, Your Love Is King, and By Your Side.

Meanwhile, Gyakie, also known as the Songbird, is a Ghanaian R&B and Afro-fusion singer. In 2019, she released her debut single, Love Is Pretty, which paved the way for another single, Never Like This. In August 2020, her song Forever, from her five-track EP Seed, gained significant airplay and topped charts in Ghana, Kenya, and Nigeria.

Gyakie has recently released a new song titled Your Body, which has already attracted public attention within just a few days of its release.

Ghana News.title: 13 first-offender inmates discharged from Wa Central Prison under Presidential Amnesty
Ghana News.content:
Thirteen first-offender inmates have been officially discharged from the Wa Central Prison after benefiting from the 2026 presidential amnesty granted by President John Dramani Mahama. The release ceremony, held on October 23, 2026, marked the discharge and reintegration of these individuals back into society.

Upper West Regional Prisons Commander DDP Alhaji Ousmane Tasembedo revealed that 18 names were initially submitted to the prison headquarters for amnesty consideration. Out of this number, 13 were approved by the President in conformity with Article 72(1) of the 1992 Constitution. However, only 3 inmates were discharged at the ceremony, as the remaining ten had already gone home through the standard one-third sentence discharge process before the amnesty reached them due to bureaucratic processes.

The Regional Commander emphasized that the amnesty represents an opportunity for transformation and a fresh beginning rather than merely a release from custody. He noted that the Wa Central Prisons has successfully reformed and rehabilitated 34 inmates since 2024. Among the 13 approved amnesty beneficiaries, two acquired vocational skills in smock sewing and tailoring. He assured that the service will present them with start-up materials to begin their new lives.

Assembly Member for Jonga and Wa Municipal Justice and Security Chairman Daubile Alhassan Ibrahim, representing the Municipal Chief Executive, cautioned the beneficiaries to conduct themselves properly as they reintegrate into society. He clarified that the amnesty does not provide immunity from future prosecution. "It doesn't mean that when you are granted this amnesty today and you go out there and commit any offense the law will not say oh some time ago the president was granted you amnesty to go home and rest," he warned.

Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, 39-year-old Yakubu Anas expressed deep appreciation to the President for the unique opportunity. Anas also extended gratitude to the regional command for the vocational training received during their incarceration, promising to put the acquired skills to good use and maintain good behavior.

Nuokpem Richard, speaking for the families of the beneficiaries, thanked the government and prison officials for the training provided to the inmates. "We are praying that they should go and continue and then achieve their aim at the end of the day they should be somebody in the near future," he stated.

Ghana News.title: Globe Health Clinic promotes early detection during Breast Cancer Awareness Month
Ghana News.content:
The Globe Health Assessment Clinic has organised a free medical screening exercise to improve access to healthcare and encourage the early detection of diseases among residents.

The exercise, held as part of activities marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month in October, offered community members free health checks, including ultrasound scans, full blood count tests and other medical assessments.

The clinic’s Chief Executive Officer, Daniel Oppong, said the initiative was intended to support people who struggle to pay for medical care and encourage them to check their health regularly.

Speaking to the media during the exercise, Mr Oppong said financial difficulties prevented many people from seeking medical attention, making community-based screening an important way to help them identify health problems early.

“You know, in our community, a lot of people are really struggling to pay for medical bills,” he said.

“That's the main reason why Globe decided to support the community with the medical screening today,” he added.

Mr Oppong said that early detection was essential to identifying health conditions before they developed into more serious problems.

He encouraged residents to check their health periodically, explaining that timely medical assessments could help them seek treatment before their conditions worsened.

The decision to hold the exercise in October was also linked to Breast Cancer Awareness Month, which focuses on raising awareness of breast cancer and encouraging women to undergo screening.

Mr Oppong said the clinic had made ultrasound services available to support women and other residents who wanted to undergo medical checks.

“We decided to organise this event to support the community members and also to encourage the community members to come around and check their breasts and their womb,” he said.

He added that the clinic was ready to use its ultrasound equipment to help residents access the necessary examinations.

The exercise was the clinic's first community outreach programme since it began operating.

According to Mr Oppong, the turnout was encouraging, with residents visiting the facility throughout the day to benefit from the free services.

He described the response as overwhelming and urged more people to take advantage of the opportunity to assess their health.

“We are expecting as many people as we can. We have had a lot of people coming in from morning till now, and it's been amazing the whole day.”

He said the clinic was providing several services at no cost during the exercise, including ultrasound scans and full blood count tests.

“We are doing ultrasound for free. We are doing full blood count for free. We are doing vaccinations for free. We are doing everything for free,” he said.

Mr Oppong encouraged residents to make use of the exercise, particularly those who might otherwise delay medical checks because of financial constraints.

Mr Oppong said the clinic intended to make the screening exercise an annual event, with future editions to be held at its facility.

Beyond the annual programme, the clinic also plans to use its medical van to extend its services to communities in other regions.

He said the expansion would allow more people to benefit from the facility's diagnostic services, particularly those who have limited access to healthcare.

“We will do that every year. We will do it in our facility here,” he said.

“We have a medical van that we want to extend to other regions so that other community members or other regions will also benefit from whatever Globe Health Assessment Clinic is doing to support the nation,” he said.

Mr Oppong described the initiative as part of the clinic's commitment to giving back to society by helping people access medical assessments.

He said the facility was prepared to support residents to undergo health checks and identify possible medical concerns.

He said the clinic offered ultrasound and other diagnostic services, laboratory testing, electrocardiography (ECG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

The facility also provides tuberculosis testing for people applying to travel abroad, including students who need medical screening as part of their travel requirements.

Ghana News.title: Agalga urges NDC members to maintain peace ahead of constituency elections
Ghana News.content:
The Majority Leader in Parliament and Member of Parliament for Builsa North, James Agalga, has appealed to members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to maintain peace and unity as the party prepares to hold its constituency elections on Saturday, October 24.

In a statement ahead of the polls, Mr Agalga urged party members and candidates to be circumspect in their utterances, engagements and conduct as campaigns draw to a close.

He called on the aspirants and their supporters to avoid insults and character assassination, stressing the need for the elections to be conducted in an atmosphere of love, unity and mutual respect.

“Let us conduct these elections in unity, love and peace, devoid of insults and character assassination,” he said.

Mr Agalga noted that all party members had a shared responsibility to protect the NDC’s future, cautioning against actions that could undermine the party’s broader political ambitions.

“We all have a stake in the 2028 journey. Let us not undermine that future in our quest to serve the Party today,” he added.

He expressed hope that the constituency elections would strengthen the party and foster greater cohesion among its members, wishing all candidates the best of luck.

“May the best candidates win, and may the NDC emerge stronger and more united after these elections,” he said.

Ghana News.title: GPL 26/27: Hearts pip Holy Stars to go top of the table after 3rd consecutive win
Ghana News.content:
Accra Hearts of Oak secured a 1-0 victory over Holy Stars at the University of Ghana Stadium on Friday.

Martin Karikari scored the decisive goal to ensure a third consecutive league win for the Phobians.

Before today's game, Hearts were unbeaten in three, thanks to a draw with Dreams F.C., followed by consecutive victories over Vision F.C. and Port City.

Their guests had won two of the last three, with a 2-0 defeat at Gold Stars being the only blemish.

When the match started, it was exactly as expected: a close contest of contrasting styles.

Hearts nearly took the lead after seven minutes, but Kwaku Boateng's effort from inside the box was cleared off the goal line.

Thirteen minutes later, Hearts were denied by the crossbar when Ransford Mensah's free kick from thirty yards rattled the post.

Hearts kept probing but their main creative outlets, Yaw Amankwaah Baafi and Kwaku Boateng, were kept under lock and key.

At the start of the second half, Holy Stars pair of Abdul Basit and Joseph Hudson began to impose themselves a bit more on the game, offering the visitors brief spells of possession to break Hearts' dominance.

With nine minutes remaining, Hearts found the breakthrough, and it was worth the wait.

Martin Karikari received the pass just inside the box and for a split second, he appeared to have been trapped by two Holy Stars defenders.

However, he shifted his body to the left and back across to his right, deceiving the defender to his left into moving.

With the speed of lightning, Karikari stepped between the small opening and fired a snapshot to the near post before the goalkeeper, Baffoe Razak, could react.

Friday's victory sends Hearts to the top of the Ghana Premier League with 17 points.

The Phobians are now unbeaten in four matches, with three wins in that time.

Meanwhile, Holy Stars have two wins and two defeats in their last four matches.

Ghana News.title: Ghana unveils world Armwrestling championship squad, appeals for travel support
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Armwrestling Federation has unveiled a formidable squad for the upcoming World Armwrestling Championship in New Delhi, India, while appealing to corporate Ghana, government institutions, philanthropists and sports enthusiasts to support the team's travel and participation.

The squad, comprising some of the country's most accomplished Armwrestlers, is expected to fly Ghana's flag at the global competition as the team targets medals and seeks to consolidate the country's growing reputation as a force in international armwrestling.

Leading the contingent are world-class performers Mabel Yeboah-60kg, Blessed Abeka Nunoo – 65kg and Grace Minta – 89kg, who have distinguished themselves through their performances at international competitions. They are joined by Florence Boakye – 110+kg, Afia Kumah – 110+kg and Comfort Dunyo – 60kg, who are masters in the women's category.

The men's contingent includes Edward Asamoah Yamoah, Haruna Tahiru, Godwin Sackey, Daniel Acquah, Charles Osei Asibey Jr., Henry Otoo and Asinu Dodzie, all expected to bring their strength, experience and competitive spirit to the championship.

Ghana's participation is particularly significant given the country's impressive progress in the sport over the years, with its athletes making their mark at continental and world competitions. The national team has consistently demonstrated its potential to challenge the world's best, earning recognition for Ghana on the international sporting stage.

However, despite the team's ambition and preparations, securing the necessary financial resources to facilitate the trip remains a major concern. The Federation is therefore appealing to corporate institutions, government agencies, sports-loving individuals and other stakeholders to support the squad's travel and participation.

The appeal comes at a crucial time, with the Federation seeking to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent the selected athletes from representing their country at the prestigious championship.

Support from the private sector and other well-meaning Ghanaians would provide an important boost to the team's campaign while offering sponsors an opportunity to associate their brands with a sport that continues to deliver results and enhance Ghana's international sporting profile.

The Ghana Armwrestling Federation has, over the years, built a reputation for developing athletes capable of competing at the highest level, while creating opportunities for talent development, employment and national pride.

The Federation is hopeful that the latest appeal will attract the necessary support to enable the team to travel to India and compete against the world's best armwrestlers.

The 2026 World Armwrestling Championship is scheduled for India from October 26 to November 7, 2026.

Ghana News.title: Newsfile to discuss Obuasi SHTS abuse case, GH₵49m SA evacuation, World Cup visa scandal
Ghana News.content:
This Saturday on Newsfile: three scandals, new revelations, unanswered questions.

When complaints are made, and institutions fail to act; when millions of cedis are spent, but records remain disputed, and when money allegedly connected to a visa scandal is returned, what does accountability really mean? This Saturday on Newsfile, we examine three controversies raising difficult questions about public trust, institutional responsibility and the search for the truth.

The Obuasi Senior High Technical School sexual-abuse scandal continues to deepen, with the number of reported complainants rising to 19. Two education directors have been asked to step aside to facilitate investigations, while allegations that 38 teachers were targeted for transfers have raised concerns about possible retaliation against whistleblowers.

The NDC, which initially directed the accused headmaster to withdraw from its constituency chairmanship contest, reversed that decision in the name of natural justice and the presumption of innocence, before directing him to step aside again. Meanwhile, the headmaster has reportedly sued Manasseh Azure Awuni and Multimedia Group Limited for GH¢2 million in defamation damages. But as the allegations are investigated, who is protecting the students?

Does the presumption of innocence prevent authorities from taking precautionary measures to safeguard children and preserve public confidence? If complaints were brought to the attention of school and education officials months earlier, who knew, what action did they take, and will anyone be held accountable for failing to act?

With civil society organisations calling for a sex offenders' register, mandatory background checks and stronger school safeguarding systems, how can Ghana protect children without unfairly branding people whose guilt has not been established? And what changes are needed to ensure that no school becomes the scene of similar allegations?

From the safety of schoolchildren, we turn to the management of public funds. The GH¢49.72 million spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa remains the subject of a heated dispute between the government and the Minority. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa insists that every cedi has been accounted for.

The NPP Minority, however, says its examination of the records has uncovered discrepancies involving passenger manifests, allowances and supporting documentation, raising questions about GH¢16.4 million in expenditure.

JoyNews' independent examination has also identified errors in passenger records, including impossible dates of birth, prompting Ghana's High Commission in Pretoria to acknowledge mistakes affecting 15 records.

The mission attributes those inaccuracies to passport expiry dates being entered in place of dates of birth, insisting that the errors do not establish financial loss. But the controversy has now moved beyond clerical mistakes to the cost of charter flights. The Minority is questioning the reported US$750,000 price tag for each of three flights and demanding original contracts, airline invoices and procurement records.

Were the flights procured competitively? What services were covered by the reported charges, and were any intermediaries involved? Can the Ministry demonstrate not merely that money was paid, but that the services were delivered at a reasonable cost? The government says the expenditure is fully accounted for, while the Minority insists that questions remain.

With a special audit reportedly requested, will an independent examination finally reconcile the figures and establish whether the discrepancies are administrative errors, weaknesses in record-keeping or evidence of more serious irregularities?

And in the unfolding World Cup visa scandal, a reported US$26,000 payment to police on behalf of suspended National Sports Authority Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has introduced another twist. The payment is said to be part of US$56,000 allegedly received as commission in connection with visa arrangements.

Ampofo Ankrah denies wrongdoing, and the reported repayment is not proof of criminal liability. But who made the payment, under whose instructions, and for what purpose? Was it a refund to an applicant, a recovery of disputed money or part of an arrangement to settle the matter privately?

And what happened to the investigation into alleged abuse of public office and financial irregularities involving public institutions and private intermediaries? Should the OSP become involved, and how should its mandate be coordinated with the CID's ongoing investigative role?

More importantly, can returning money extinguish criminal liability if an offence has been committed, or must investigators still establish how the money was obtained, who benefited, and whether public office was used for private gain? Is Ghana investigating a suspected criminal enterprise, or will the matter ultimately be treated as a financial dispute resolved by repayment?

Three stories, one fundamental test: whether institutions can be trusted to protect the vulnerable, account for public money and investigate allegations without fear or favour.

From the classrooms of Obuasi to the evacuation accounts and the World Cup visa controversy, the public deserves more than denials, accusations and promises of investigations. It deserves answers supported by evidence, fair processes and accountability where wrongdoing is established.

This Saturday, join Samson Lardy Anyenini and the Newsfile panel as we interrogate the latest revelations, examine the competing claims and ask the questions that matter.

Newsfile airs live on the JoyNews channel on digital satellite channels 421 on DSTV and 144 on GoTV, and streams on JoyNews’ Facebook or YouTube channels on Saturdays from 9 am to noon.

Viewers can also follow the discussion by tuning in to Joy 99.7 FM or Luv 99.5 FM on the radio or stream the discussion live on either Google or Apple Podcasts.

When it's Saturday, it's Newsfile!

Ghana News.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
Ghana News.content:
Seven people have been killed in an attack on a funeral in central Jordan, officials have said.

At least 34 others were injured as gunmen opened fire on a church in Hmoud, in the Karak governorate on Friday.

The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car, entered the church and opened fire before fleeing. No-one has admitted carrying out the attack.

In a news conference, Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were working to apprehend the perpetrators which he described as a "group of extremists".

Jordan's King Abdullah II, said the authorities would "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties".

"Whoever imagines that the bullets of treachery can divide the ranks of Jordanians will fail in his endeavour before our steadfastness and unity," the king added in a post on X.

Dozens of people had been inside the church for the funeral when the shooting began, Khaled Burqan, one of the mourners, told Jordan's al-Mamlaka state-run TV.

He said two attackers armed with a rifle and a pistol had been firing at the mourners for several minutes.

Al-Faraya added that the incident was "painful and horrific" and "unparalleled in the history of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan," during his news conference.

Public service television station al-Mamlaka has reported the king arrived in Karak on Friday evening "to check on the condition of the injured".

Initial reports indicated seven people had been killed in the attack. A government spokesperson later said six people had died, before officials again revised the death toll to seven.

CCTV footage, verified by the BBC, appears to shows three gunmen making their way from a road toward the church.

Two of the attackers are seen making their way on to what appears to be a vehicle entrance to the church grounds, before retreating briefly and returning with a third man. All three appear to be armed with handguns.

Separate footage believed to be from the aftermath of the attack appears to show several dead and wounded bodies on the ground amid some chaotic scenes.

There was a heavy security presence at the entrance to a hospital treating people injured in the incident in Karak, amid an atmosphere charged with anger among residents of the governorate, particularly the families of those injured and killed.

Karak has a sizeable Christian community in the majority-Muslim Jordan.

Such violence is rare in the country, but deadly attacks have been carried out in the past.

Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun, a Christian head of state, said the "heinous terrorist attack" on the church "violated the sanctity of death and funeral mourners, contradicts all religious and humanitarian values," according to Lebanese media.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Tigray official urges rebels to disarm
World.content:
An official in Tigray’s new federally backed administration has urged rebel forces to lay down their weapons in the northern Ethiopian region.

The call on Friday came hours after a rebel commander told his fighters to continue resisting government-backed forces despite losing control of Mekelle, the Tigray region’s capital.

Fighters from the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) were forced to withdraw from Mekelle in early October, after government-allied fighters entered the city to crush a rebel attempt to overthrow Ethiopia’s government.

Ethiopia’s government then installed a six-month caretaker administration in Tigray, promising to restore services, help displaced people return and prepare for elections.

But some fighting has continued, with Mekelle residents reporting a drone strike that killed four people and injured six others as they loaded goats onto a truck on Tuesday. The casualties could not be independently verified.

Redae Halefom Woldeselassie, a senior official in Tigray’s new caretaker administration, said rebel forces were collapsing and urged fighters to lay down their weapons.

“This is not the time for settling scores – I call upon you to return to your homes and continue your civilian lives,” he said in Mekelle.

He dismissed the prospect of the rebels retaking the city, maintaining the conflict served a small clique of leaders and not the people of Tigray.

Hours earlier, Lieutenant General Fisseha Kidanu, who was identified in a television broadcast as commander of the Tigray army, pledged to reverse recent military setbacks, saying Tigray was still at war.



“Local militias across the region – alongside all volunteers joining the resistance – are expected to engage the enemy,” he said Thursday on Tigray Broadcast Media, a new rebel television station. His location was not disclosed.

Fisseha urged attacks on government-held positions despite his opponents’ advantages in drones and heavy weapons. The TPLF has also claimed to have inflicted heavy losses on government forces. The Associated Press could not independently verify those claims.

The government’s allies include the Tigray Peace Force, comprising former members of the TPLF’s armed wing – a division within Tigrayan forces that has complicated the renewed conflict.

Redae said Ethiopian troops and allied forces were conducting joint security operations, including measures to prevent looting. He promised preparations for displaced residents to return but gave no timetable.

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, speaking Monday to the Ethiopian Broadcasting Corporation, accused the TPLF of forcibly recruiting young people to fight instead of disarming under the terms of the November 2022 Pretoria peace agreement.

The renewed fighting has effectively shattered the agreement, which ended the region’s devastating 2020-2022 war.

That conflict caused an estimated 500,000 civilian deaths through violence, famine and collapsed health services, according to researchers at Ghent University in Belgium.

World.title: Ecuador judge orders pre-trial detention of leftist presidential candidate
World.content:
Luisa Gonzalez, who lost to right-wing president Daniel Noboa in 2023, has called the arrest political persecution.

A judge in Ecuador has ordered that former left-wing presidential candidate Luisa Gonzalez remain detained following her arrest for alleged money laundering.

The order on Friday came the day after 48-year-old Gonzalez, who challenged right-wing President Daniel Noboa in the 2023 election, was arrested in the rural town of Canuto.

Gonzalez, her party and her close ally, former President Rafael Correa, have called the arrest political persecution.

Several other members of Gonzalez’s Citizen Revolution (RC) party have also recently faced charges.

They include Guayaquil Mayor Aquiles Alvarez, convicted of illegally selling subsidised fuel and former Vice President Jorge Glas, serving a sentence for corruption.

Prosecutors have said that Gonzalez is one of seven people under investigation for financing the 2023 presidential campaign. The probe focuses on $500,000 poured into advertising during the race.

Gonzalez has denied wrongdoing, dismissing the charges as “absurd”.

Citizen Revolution President Gabriela Rivadeneira told a news conference on Thursday that Gonzalez’s arrest “confirms or makes visible what we have been saying lately: Ecuador is living under a dictatorship”.

Gonzalez, a lawyer and former member of Ecuador’s National Assembly, lost to Noboa in an April 2025 run-off. She rejected the result as fraudulent.

Noboa, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, later accused Citizen Revolution of conspiring to attack him.

The party has since been banned from running in local elections next month.

World.title: Aston Villa vs Manchester City: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
World.content:
Man City are the only team with a perfect Premier League record, but face a Villa side determined to climb the table.

Who: Aston Villa vs Manchester City

What: English Premier League

Where: Villa Park in Birmingham, United Kingdom

When: Saturday, October 22 at 12:30pm (11:30 GMT)

How to follow: Al Jazeera will bring you all the build-up, before our live text commentary stream from 9:30am (08:30 GMT).

Manchester City can continue to put their off-field woes to one side in Saturday’s early kickoff in the Premier League when they travel to Aston Villa, where they will move six points clear at the top with a win.

Holders Arsenal entertain Everton later in the day and will very much hope to extend their winning run in the league to a third match.

City do, however, have a 100 percent record from their first seven games in the league this season, a run that defies the guilty verdict by an independent commission regarding more than 100 breaches of the competition’s financial rules.

The Manchester club have appealed the decision and no sanctions have, as of yet, been imposed.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at City’s trip to Villa Park, where the Cityzens ’ siege mentality is expected to continue.

Foden can be one of Premier League’s best again, says Maresca

Enzo Maresca said it is his job as Manchester City boss to help Phil Foden rediscover his best form after the England international ended his long goal drought.

Foden had not scored for 10 months before netting in City’s 3-2 win over Ipswich last weekend and then scored a Champions League hat-trick in a 5-1 rout of AEK Athens on Tuesday.

The 26-year-old swept the board of personal awards for the Premier League’s best player in the 2023/24 season after a 27-goal campaign.



But Foden, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, has failed to hit top form for the past two seasons.

“Since we started, I sat down with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning. Just to show him, I don’t know if love is the right word to use, but just to show him how important he is,” said Maresca, who took charge of City in June.

“I said many times that I know Phil from years ago, so I know how, for different reasons, the last few years it was not good enough.

“When you have more players like Phil available, you are a better team because again it’s a matter of improving players. If you improve the players, you improve the team.

“So for me, I think it’s my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England.”

How have Maresca and Man City shaped up this season?

Other than a 4-2 Champions League defeat by holders Paris Saint-Germain, Maresca has made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola at the Etihad Stadium.

The Italian is the first manager ever to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club.

However, City’s fine form has been overshadowed by the threat of severe sanctions against the club for the widespread flouting of Premier League financial rules.

A large points deduction, which could lead to relegation, is likely unless City win their appeal.

Maresca said the mood in the dressing room remained buoyant despite the cloud hanging over the club.

“In any club, when you lose important players, many important players, and you lose the manager after 10 years, it always takes time to compete again,” he said on Thursday.

“But this organisation last summer changed many important players, changed the manager after 10 years, and we are competing at the moment.”

How have Aston Villa fared this season?

Villa sit 12th in the table, but a win would propel them to sixth, at least for a couple of hours. Under former Arsenal manager Unai Emery, Villa have been regulars among the European spots in recent seasons, and were even challengers for the title at one point.

This term has provided a sterner examination of their credentials after the exit of a number of the top stars of recent campaigns, including Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez to Chelsea, Youri Tielemans to City’s rivals United and Ollie Watkins to Al-Hilal.

The Midlands club, who beat Freiburg 3-0 to win last season’s UEFA Europa League, are on a six-match unbeaten run – of which they have won five – across the league and Champions League.



What happened the last time Aston Villa played Manchester City?

Villa were 2-1 winners at City in Pep Guardiola’s last game in charge on the final day of last season.

Antoine Semenyo gave City the lead, but an Ollie Watkins brace turned the game.

What happened in Aston Villa and Man City’s corresponding fixture last season?

Villa emerged with a 1-0 win in their Premier League clash at Villa Park last October. Matty Cash scored the only goal.

When did Man City last beat Aston Villa?

City last beat Villa when they were 2-1 winners in the Premier League fixture between the sides at Etihad Stadium in April 2025.

Marcus Rashford, on loan from United, levelled matters from the penalty spot after Bernardo Silva’s opener, but Matheus Nunes sealed the win for the home side.

When did Man City last win at Aston Villa?

City have not won at Villa Park since December 2021, when Ruben Diaz and Silva netted in the first half of the Premier League match. Watkins’s strike in the second period proved only a consolation.

Prediction – Aston Villa vs Man City

The Opta supercomputer has given City a 43 percent chance of winning the match, while offering Villa a 32 percent chance of victory.

Head-to-head – Aston Villa vs Man City

This is the 186th meeting between the sides, with City winning 82 times and Villa emerging victorious on 61 occasions. There have been 42 draws in the fixture that dates back to 1899 – and a 2-1 home win for Villa.

Aston Villa team news

Amadou Onana, Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka miss out through injury. Johan Manzambi and Modou Keba Cisse both face fitness tests.

Predicted Aston Villa starting lineup

Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Manzambi, Buendia; Jackson

Manchester City team news

Forward Antoine Semenyo is set for a lengthy spell out ⁠with a knee injury, while wing back Nico O’Reilly and midfielders Mateo Kovacic and Matheus Nunes are doubts.

League-leading scorer Erling Haaland was rested for Tuesday’s 5-1 Champions League thrashing of AEK Athens because of a knock but is expected to be available against Villa.

Predicted Manchester City starting lineup

Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly; Anderson, Bouaddi, Fernandez; Foden, Haaland, Doku

World.title: Former FBI officials charged in connection with Hunter Biden laptop probe
World.content:
Lawyers for two accused officials say Department of Justice seeking to revive scandal before midterm vote.

Share Former FBI officials charged in connection with Hunter Biden laptop probe on social media

Two former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agents have been charged in connection with a 2020 probe into a laptop belonging to former President Joe Biden’s son, Hunter Biden.

The former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, were charged with lying to Congress. They made their first court appearance in Washington, DC, on Friday.

Lawyers for the officials accused the Department of Justice of filing the charges to revive the salacious saga just days before the November 3 midterm vote, in which Republicans face an uphill battle against Democrats to maintain control of Congress.
