A lawyer for Floris said she “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years”, while accusing the Justice Department of building its case on hearsay.

“Yet today, the DOJ [Justice Department] has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” the statement said.

“It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”

Floris and Benavides had overseen the Foreign Intelligence Task Force (FITF) at the FBI when Hunter Biden’s laptop was found. The pair testified to Congress that the unit, which focuses on foreign interference in US elections, was not involved in the laptop investigation.

In a criminal complaint, federal prosecutors alleged the statements contradicted messages sent during the same period.

While launched by Trump during his first term, the FITF was heavily targeted by Republicans under former US President Joe Biden. They charged the unit was politically biased and used to cover up information about Biden’s laptop.



The unit was disbanded when Trump took office for the second time in January 2025.

Scandalous saga

The existence of the laptop became known in October of 2020, just weeks before Biden and Trump faced off in a presidential election.

Its strange origins, having been dropped off at a Delaware computer repair shop and apparently abandoned by Hunter Biden, prompted suspicion. Its contents were first reported on by the New York Post, based on information provided to Trump lawyer Rudy Giuliani.

Several former intelligence officials warned that the laptop had the hallmarks of a Russian disinformation campaign. However, the FBI later seized and verified that the laptop and its contents, including messages related to the younger Biden’s foreign business ties and explicit photos of his drug use, were authentic.

The laptop was later used to back federal gun and tax evasion charges against Hunter Biden, although no wrongdoing related to his business ties or connection with his father was found.

Trump FBI Director Kash Patel has pledged to investigate the agency’s conduct throughout Biden’s presidency. Critics have accused him of flagrant politicalisation.

“Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system. No one is above the law,” Patel said in a statement posted on X.

The Justice Department has historically sought to avoid public and overt investigative acts in the direct lead-up to an election that involve candidates or that risk influencing an outcome.

But officials in the last two weeks have made a series of bold moves in cases with political undertones, including a search of Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar’s house in an immigration fraud investigation.

The department also unsealed a corruption indictment on Thursday against powerful Democratic Virginia state Senator L Louise Lucas.

World.title: Trump administration sues to block possible Democratic win in Alaska
World.content:
The Justice Department lawsuit raises concerns the administration may be looking to meddle in some of this midterm cycle’s races.

Share Trump administration sues to block possible Democratic win in Alaska on social media

With just more than a week until the pivotal US midterm elections, the US Department of Justice has filed a lawsuit to block certification of the results in Alaska’s hotly contested Senate race.

In a lawsuit filed on Thursday, the Justice Department argued that an independent candidate with the same name as the state’s incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is currently running for re-election, is purposefully running to mislead voters.

“Given the substantial likelihood that the inclusion of Daniel J Sullivan will confuse or mislead voters looking to cast a vote for Senator Sullivan, and thus distort the will of Alaskan voters, there is a substantial likelihood that a certification of the election will reflect an electoral process that lacked integrity,” the Trump administration’s filing read.

The Justice Department is asking a federal judge to delay certification to allow time for an investigation into “whether votes cast for Daniel J Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan”.

During a visit to Florida on Friday, Trump took credit for the lawsuit after reporters asked about it.

“I’m the one that said ‘do it,'” he told reporters in Fort Myers, Florida.

A Justice Department spokesperson did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

The lawsuit raises concerns among Democrats and voting rights groups that the Trump administration may be looking to meddle in some of the upcoming midterm races as Republicans across the United States struggle to push back a growing wave of Democratic support.



The Justice Department, as of late, has taken several actions against Democratic critics of President Donald Trump that have bolstered those worries, including charging a high-ranking Virginia lawmaker, state Senator L Louise Lucas, in a public corruption case and launching a probe into Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar over allegations of immigration fraud. Both have said the actions are politically motivated.

Trump critics have long expressed worries that the Justice Department could seek to block certification of elections the US president’s party loses.

On Wednesday, as Lucas’s indictment was announced, US Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters his agency would not do so unless extreme circumstances warranted such action.

“It is not DOJ’s intention to – and it’s never our intention to – improperly interfere with elections or the state certification process,” Blanche said.

The Brennan Center for Justice’s senior counsel, Lauren Miller Karalunas, said in a statement that election certification is handled by US states and the federal government has “no role” in it.

“Rest assured, state certification processes were created to meet this moment,” Karalunas said. “Centuries ago, state legislatures recognized that bad actors could use the process to manipulate election outcomes. They built in safeguards specifically designed to stop that from happening.”

The Alaska state Supreme Court in June rejected a previous Republican effort to remove Daniel J Sullivan from the ballot. He will appear without a party designation by his name, while Senator Sullivan will be listed as the Republican candidate.

However, under Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system, voters can select both Sullivans if they are unsure.

Which party controls the US Senate after November 3 could, ultimately, come down to Alaska’s Senate race, where Senator Sullivan is engaged in a challenging re-election fight against former US Democratic Congresswoman Mary Peltola.

Polling of the race has consistently shown a race that is well within the margin of error. A survey conducted by Public Policy Polling earlier this month suggested Peltola had a narrow one-point lead.

The campaign teams for both Sullivans and Peltola did not immediately return requests for comment.

World.title: Deadly shooting near Paris is a 'racist terrorist attack', Macron says
World.content:
French President Emmanuel Macron has labelled a gun attack in a Parisian suburb which killed one person and injured five others "a racist terrorist attack".

Macron said the attack was a "turning point in the life of our Republic and our nation" - the first time there has ever been a random racial killing like this.

The attack unfolded over some 15 minutes with the attacker opening fire from his car - first in Trappes to the south-west of Paris, and then in nearby La VerriÃ¨re - appearing to target people of migrant origin. He was subsequently arrested.

Three of those injured, including a 12-year-old girl, remain in a serious condition.

Visiting the scene of the attack in Trappes, Macron said people had been targeted for their skin colour or religion and urged the public not to give an inch in the face of what he called "ideologies taking root".

The exact motive remains unclear, but the National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) said the incident appeared to be "murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise".

The suspect has been named in French media as Kevin T who, according to PNAT, had four previous convictions which had been "automatically expunged".

The 39-year-old was known to police but not to France's intelligence services, local media report.

He was not on a list of individuals considered to be a serious threat to French security, the national anti-terrorism prosecutor's office told BFMTV.

A member of the suspect's "immediate family circle" was also taken into custody on Friday, it added.

The Mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, said that "an individual fired shots from his vehicle at several people he encountered" on Friday morning.

The gunman drove through several neighbourhoods in a grey Renault Clio, according to witnesses. Rabeh said he had "fired randomly" with the seeming intent of causing "as many casualties as possible... he wanted to cause carnage", he said.

The mayor said people had been targeted at a petrol station, a medical centre and a playground in Trappes before the attacker had driven on to nearby La VerriÃ¨re.

A police union official said the suspect had been detained in La VerriÃ¨re on the main N10 road that runs through the town.

World.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
World.content:
Seven people have been killed in an attack on a funeral in central Jordan, officials have said.

At least 34 others were injured as gunmen opened fire on a church in Hmoud, in the Karak governorate on Friday.

The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car, entered the church and opened fire before fleeing. No-one has admitted carrying out the attack.

In a news conference, Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were working to apprehend the perpetrators which he described as a "group of extremists".

Jordan's King Abdullah II, said the authorities would "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties".

Initial reports indicated seven people had been killed in the attack. A government spokesperson later said six people had died, before officials again revised the death toll to seven.

CCTV footage, verified by the BBC, appears to shows three gunmen making their way from a road toward the church.

Two of the attackers are seen making their way on to what appears to be a vehicle entrance to the church grounds, before retreating briefly and returning with a third man. All three appear to be armed with handguns.

Separate footage believed to be from the aftermath of the attack appears to show several dead and wounded bodies on the ground amid some chaotic scenes.

World.title: Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead
World.content:
The incident has already begun to influence the ongoing election campaign, with Netanyahu - who has built his campaign on the promise of security - saying that his Likud party would cancel campaign events which had been set for Friday morning.

Speaking later from the scene, Netanyahu said that the military would "demolish this place and completely transform it," referring to the Hebron neighbourhood where the attackers are said to have come from.

It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment.

Netanyahu likened his plans to previous operations in West Bank refugee camps where residential buildings were demolished and thousands were displaced.

He also said he had reviewed plans for the largest military operation in the West Bank in decades - though did not say when it could be carried out.

He added that he had imposed cordons around the city of Hebron - which has around 200,000 residents - and the nearby city of Halhul.

Netanyahu's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for Israel to launch a campaign in the West Bank "exactly like in Gaza or Lebanon," while far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for Israel to dismantle the Palestinian Authority.

On Thursday, Foreign Minister Israel Katz accused opposition leaders of undermining the government by criticising Netanyahu's warnings of an attack ahead of the election, saying they would be "responsible" for any future attack on the country.

Opposition chiefs, including frontrunner Gadi Eisenkot and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, offered their condolences to the families of the killed troops and praised those who killed the attackers.

The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers' vehicle, and that they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint - so instead decided to open fire there.

At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN.

Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says - not including those killed in Friday's attack.

World.title: White House says Melania Trump brokers truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
World.content:
The White House statement said Melania Trump and one of her representatives had worked "directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localised ceasefire".

"Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require," she is quoted as saying.

"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive co-ordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine."

Melania Trump added that Oleshky residents "have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks" and that "without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible".

The statement did not say how long the ceasefire would be in place for.

Davyd Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads President Volodymyr Zelensky's party in parliament, later said "an operation to unblock the settlement of Oleshky and its surroundings will begin in the near future".

"To achieve this goal, a ceasefire will be achieved in the near future, as announced by the First Lady of the United States, Melania Trump," he said.

In Russia, President Vladimir Putin's spokesman confirmed that, "those who wish to do so will be able to leave this settlement".

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
World.content:
Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink internet network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits had been reversed by Elon Musk who owns the satellite system.

The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations.

The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink's military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had "put it back".

Asked on Friday, Trump said: "If there is a problem, I will get it straightened out."

Trump added: "I have not spoken to him. I might have to, but I have not. I've heard it was fixed, but if it's not, I'll speak to him."

Musk previously said he was not behind the slowdown, which affected Ukraine's ability to use attack drones and co-ordinate defensive operations.

Trump told reporters he did not think the tech billionaire had too much power.

The Ukrainian defence ministry sources said the military was constantly monitoring the performance of both the Starlink and Starshield networks.

They added that there was "currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted".

Last week, Kyiv said uplink speeds to the low Earth orbit satellites had been restricted, affecting the speed at which drones could travel. Any drone travelling faster than 100mph lost its connection, officials said.

Shortly after, Musk said that Starshield, which Ukraine uses for some of its operation, was controlled by the US military and suggested that the Pentagon could be behind the issues.

The White House has since repeatedly denied deliberately placing limits on the network in Ukraine.

In a call with Trump on Friday evening, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham "underlined the importance for Ukraine to have full access to Starlink so they can continue to defend themselves against Russia's full-scale invasion", Downing Street said in a statement.

World.title: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike
World.content:
An oil spill from a tanker attacked near the Strait of Hormuz is spreading along the United Arab Emirates (UAE) coastline, forcing the closure of some beaches and coastal areas.

Satellite images from Monday show the beginnings of the oil spill from a ship matching the location and dimensions of Gem No.2, which was damaged between 9 and 10 October during a record surge of vessel strikes by Iran.

The slick of oil had spread more than 35km (22 miles) from the tanker by Wednesday, the satellite imagery showed.

UAE authorities said on Thursday that the incident is affecting beaches near the northern city of Umm Al Quwain and verified video from Friday shows the oil washing ashore, colouring the water black.

World.title: Denmark to ban mink farming in government U-turn
World.content:
Mink farming will end in Denmark by August 2029 after the government decided to drop plans to pursue an exemption to an EU-wide ban on the practice.

Denmark was once the largest producer of mink fur in the world, but the industry has declined due to global bans on fur farming, a decline in the fur trade and an earlier outbreak of a Covid strain in the nation's mink population.

The ban is due to come into effect on 7 August next year, and is followed by a two-year transition period to phase out the practice.

Danish Nature Minister Christian Rabjerg Madsen said the government had chosen animal welfare.

"A business should not continue just because it has existed for a long time. It should also make sense for society, for the economy and for the animals," he said.

The Danish government had initially sought an exemption for its mink industry when the EU added the mammal to its list of invasive species in 2025, prohibiting people from keeping them.

However, the current coalition government, elected in June, reversed this decision and decided not to proceed with the application on Friday.

Social Democrat MP Brigitte Vind said it was "a good day for animal welfare".

"It is absolutely the right decision not to apply for a special scheme for mink breeding in Denmark," she said.

The Danish Mink Association, which represents breeders, has been approached for comment.

Denmark is one of the few European countries to still produce mink fur, one of the more common pelts used in making fur garments.

However, its production has slipped behind that of other countries, such as Poland and China, in recent years.

The industry faced a crisis during the coronavirus pandemic, when the government ordered a mass cull of mink after a mutated strain of Covid-19 was found in the animals. Approximately 15 million were killed.

At the time, the country had huge export markets to China and Hong Kong. The government later admitted it had no legal basis for the culling.

There are now approximately 15,000 mink left in Denmark.

No costs have yet been determined for closing Denmark's seven remaining mink farms, but an animal welfare spokesperson for one of the governing coalition parties previously estimated it would be around 14m Danish krone (Â£1.56m), local media report, but the final amount could be higher.

The wearing of fur is a controversial subject within fashion circles, with publications and fashion brands choosing not to use or promote it several years ago.

But it re-entered the spotlight last year, with celebrities and fashionistas wearing both vintage and so-called faux fur.

World.title: PSG v Lyon moved as Paris prepares for more protests
World.content:
Paris St-Germain's Ligue 1 match against Lyon has been pushed back 24 hours to Monday as the French capital prepares for another weekend of protests.

The fixture at the Parc des Princes in Paris had been scheduled to kick off at 19:45 GMT on Sunday but will instead take place at 20:30 on Monday.

The Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP) announced the postponement in a statement, external on Friday after French police prohibited the fixture from taking place on its original date.

French authorities are preparing a major security operation for demonstrations planned for Saturday.

Around 550,000 people took part in demonstrations last Saturday to protest rising fuel prices, education standards and the cost of living, which have escalated after weeks of student protests.

Marches took place in several major French cities, including Paris, backed by unions and student groups, and were marred by some incidents of violence, looting and destruction.

The security challenge is further complicated by Sunday's NFL match between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France, an event expected to require a significant police deployment.

The game will be played in Saint-Denis, about 10km from Place de la Bastille, where the protests are expected to begin.

The disruptions have already affected France's domestic football schedule with Toulouse's Ligue 1 home game against Troyes moved from Saturday to Sunday at the request of authorities.

Reigning French and European champions PSG are second in the standings after seven matches, while Lyon lead the table on 14 points, ahead of the holders on goal difference.

The match will also now be played on the same day as the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London.

Injured PSG pair Ousmane Dembele, the 2025 winner, and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are among the contenders for the award.

World.title: EXCLUSIVE: French President Macron cancels scheduled visit to Nigeria
World.content:
Barring any further change of plans, French President Emmanuel Macron has cancelled his visit to Nigeria, PREMIUM TIMES can report.

Mr Macron cancelled his trip, initially scheduled for Wednesday, 28 October, due to concerns about the ongoing protests in France, Nigeria’s upcoming presidential election, and the new Ebola case.

Nigerian sources briefed about the planned visit told PREMIUM TIMES that Mr Macron and President Bola Tinubu agreed on Thursday to cancel the state visit.

Mr Macron feared that a trip to Nigeria amid the ongoing demonstrations across France could be seen as insensitive and irresponsible. The violent demonstrations in the country that began in September have led to the closure of over 900 schools, looting, and a face-off between rioters and security officials.

Mr Tinubu also reportedly expressed concern that Mr Macron’s visit, about three months before the Nigerian presidential election, could invite accusations of foreign influence.

Mr Tinubu is seeking reelection in a country where some citizens are angry at his performance. Many are dissatisfied with his administration, particularly over the high cost of living, inflation, fuel price increases, unemployment, and insecurity.

His relations with France have also come under scrutiny. Mr Tinubu’s last trip to Paris drew public condemnation, due to his absence from the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) and the extension of his “working vacation.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

There were also concerns about the recently confirmed Ebola case in the country.

PREMIUM TIMES reached out to the French Embassy press department over the cancellation of Mr Macron’s visit, but it declined to comment.

This paper also contacted the spokesperson of the Nigerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Olufemi Adeniyi, who said the ministry has not received any information about the cancellation of Mr Macron’s visit.

“We don’t have that information about this. If there’s an official update in that regard, we’ll put it out,” he said.

France has remained Mr Tinubu’s top destination since assuming office in 2025. The country is also one of Nigeria’s closest allies.

Mr Macron’s planned visit was scheduled to be part of the activities for this year’s French Week, organised by the Franco-Nigerian Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

The French leader was to be accompanied by a delegation of French businesspeople who will meet with Nigerian counterparts.

The trip also reciprocates Mr Tinubu’s three-day state visit to France in 2024, which focused on “strengthening political, economic, and cultural relations.”

READ ALSO: France reports first human case of Shamonda virus as patient dies

French Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Marc Fonbaustier, in July said the two leaders “will assess the progress of our roadmap and outline the key elements of our relationship for the years to come.”

He also noted that the visit would allow both countries to review their growing strategic partnership and chart a new course for future cooperation.

“These will undoubtedly be ambitious and mutually beneficial for our two peoples,” he said.

“We want the economic and social development of both our countries, for our citizens, for job creation, and for improving the standards of living, with due respect for the environment, biodiversity, water and air,” he noted.

World.title: KC Luxury arrives court in ambulance, seeks bail for treatment
World.content:
Socialite Kazeem Afolabi, popularly known as KC Luxury, was brought to the Federal High Court in Lagos in an ambulance on Friday as his lawyer made another attempt at his release on bail on medical grounds.

Mr Afolabi was said to be receiving oxygen and remained in the ambulance while proceedings were held inside the courtroom, The Cable reported.

A nurse at the Police Hospital, Falomo, Lagos, Bukki Yahya, told the court that Mr Afolabi was admitted on 7 October and diagnosed with asthma and sepsis.

An officer of the Nigerian Correctional Service had earlier told the court that the defendant was critically ill and had been hospitalised.

Mr Afolabi’s lawyer, Emefo Etudo, questioned why his client had been brought to court in that condition.

The trial judge, Musa Kakaki, ordered that he be returned to the hospital.

Bail application

Mr Etudo subsequently argued an application dated 16 October, asking the court to release his client so he could receive further treatment at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The lawyer said Mr Afolabi’s condition had deteriorated and alleged that he had suffered a collapsed lung.

He told the court that the Police Hospital referred his client to LUTH because it lacked the facilities to treat him.

However, Mr Etudo alleged that Mr Afolabi was taken from LUTH to a correctional centre on 13 October despite his condition.

Opposing the application, prosecution lawyer Abu Ibrahim said the court had already considered the defendant’s health when it ruled on an earlier bail application.

Mr Ibrahim said asthma remained Mr Afolabi’s underlying ailment, although his condition might have become more severe. He also described him as a flight risk and urged the court to impose stringent conditions if bail was granted.

Mr Etudo asked the judge to grant bail on liberal terms, assuring the court that his client would attend subsequent proceedings. He added that Mr Afolabi’s international passport was in the custody of the authorities.

Mr Kakaki adjourned ruling on the application until 28 October.

Drug trafficking trial

Mr Afolabi is standing trial alongside Boniface Freeman Ochoche Sule and Ikechukwu Ekugo Patriarch on a 22-count bordering on the alleged trafficking of 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine to the United Kingdom and money laundering.

All three defendants have pleaded not guilty.

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) arraigned them on 25 September after intercepting 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine at a DHL facility within the Nigerian Aviation Handling Company premises in Ikeja, Lagos, on 3 August.

The agency valued the cocaine at about N39 billion and described the seizure as its largest interception through a courier company in Nigeria.

According to the NDLEA, the cocaine was concealed in five consignments bound for London, with Yemi Ejide listed as the shipper.

The agency alleged that the defendants worked with Atandare Oladipupo Oluwarotimi and Latifat Yusuf, who were arrested in London in connection with the investigation.

The agency said Mr Afolabi was arrested on 13 August at the departure hall of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos while preparing to travel to Paris.

It also accused him of moving billions of naira through company and personal bank accounts and using some of the funds to acquire vehicles and properties linked to the alleged drug trade.

On 2 October, the court rejected the defendants’ earlier bail applications, citing the seriousness of the charges, the possible penalties and the risk that they might abscond.

The judge also referred to the prevalence and consequences of drug trafficking.

The allegations have yet to be proved in court.

World.title: Ebola: Atiku demands details of FG’s N10bn emergency fund
World.content:
Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has demanded details of the federal government’s utilisation of the N10 billion approved for Ebola emergency preparedness.

Atiku made the demand in a statement posted on his X account on Friday, in reaction to a statement by the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council that the fund approved by President Bola Tinubu in June remains untouched.

Atiku, in the statement signed by Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, asked the government to provide specific details on the status of the fund.

“Was the money released or was it not? If it was released, where is it held, who controls it, and why has it not been used for the preparedness President Tinubu announced?” the statement asked.

Atiku also demanded records showing the amount disbursed, payment dates, contracts awarded, beneficiaries and items delivered, saying the government should account for the fund rather than rely on a press statement.

The APC campaign council said the N10 billion remained untouched, while the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), and other surveillance agencies used other available resources for the Ebola response.

The council also accused Atiku of politicising the public health situation and criticised his comments on the government’s handling of the confirmed Ebola case in Abuja.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Atiku questions response

Beyond the fund, Atiku questioned the timeline of the government’s response to the Ebola case.

He asked when Ebola was first suspected, when public health authorities were alerted, when testing was ordered and when contact tracing began.

Atiku also questioned whether the 44 contacts identified by health authorities were sufficient, given information that the patient had visited another hospital and her home before being isolated.

He called for adequate protection and equipment for health workers involved in treating the patient and tracing contacts.

“Health workers treating the patient and tracing contacts deserve protection, equipment and every resource needed to act quickly. Questioning the government’s preparedness is no insult to them. Demanding applause for President Tinubu while refusing to explain an untouched emergency fund is an insult to Nigerians,” he said.

“The APC also objects to our warning that a health emergency must never be used to interfere with campaigning or voting. President Tinubu’s government can address that concern directly: publish any proposed restrictions, their medical justification and the advice of the health authorities. Public health guidance must protect people. It must never become a political tool.”

APC defends response

The APC Presidential Campaign Council, in its 22 October statement signed by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, said the N10 billion approved by Mr Tinubu had not been disbursed.

It said agencies involved in surveillance had continued to operate with other available resources and credited their surveillance efforts with helping authorities detect the imported Ebola case and identify 44 contacts.

The council also accused Atiku of seeking to politicise the health emergency, urging opposition figures to support health authorities and comply with public health protocols.

It rejected the suggestion that the ministerial briefing on the Ebola response was meant to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies or voting, calling the claim speculative and asking Atiku to provide verifiable evidence.

Lawmakers raise funding concerns.

The demand for details of the Ebola preparedness fund comes amid separate concerns by lawmakers over funding for Nigeria’s response to the disease.

On 21 October, the House of Representatives urged the federal government to immediately release outstanding appropriated funds to relevant health agencies to strengthen surveillance, contact tracing and emergency response measures.

The House also asked the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) to assess the additional resources Nigeria needs to strengthen its preparedness and response capacity, based on current epidemiological evidence and public health guidance.

In a separate resolution the same day, the Senate also urged the federal government to release emergency funds from the Service Wide Vote to strengthen measures against the spread of Ebola and called for stronger health screening at the country’s entry points.

World.title: Fatai is third, not first, child, received four flats, other benefits — Okoya family
World.content:
Billionaire industrialist Razaq Okoya’s family has disputed Fatai Okoya’s claim that he is the industrialist’s first-born child, insisting that he is, in fact, his third child.

The family issued the clarification in a statement signed by Nathaniel Omeninwan, senior public relations manager of Eleganza Industries Ltd, days after Fatai sought his father’s forgiveness and reconciliation.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that Fatai pleaded for an opportunity to reconcile after 40 years apart. He described his father’s rejection as painful.

Fatai alleged he is Mr Okoya’s first child and accused Shade Okoya, his father’s wife, of blocking his attempt to see his father on his birthday.

However, the family denied the allegations in a statement made available to journalists on Thursday, citing what it described as ‘substantial financial support’ from the industrialist.

The family said Fatai received considerable benefits from his father, including four flats in Lagos and financial assistance for his medical treatment.

They said: “The Okoya family finds it regrettable that Fatai Okoya (who is in fact the third child of Aare Rasaq Okoya, CON) has dragged what are otherwise private family matters into the public domain to attract public sympathy, gain attention and unjustifiably discredit other family members. Fatai Okoya fell out with his father and stopped visiting him long before his father married Chief Mrs Shade Okoya, MON.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Aare Rasaq Okoya, CON, has also publicly stated on numerous occasions that any child of his who is not prepared to respect, appreciate and abide by his wishes is on their own. Fatai Okoya has benefited immensely from his father and continues to benefit. He lives in, and has been given, four flats by his father in Ogunlana Surulere, and has at times been receiving payment for his medical bills.”

“Shade Okoya”

The family also said Mr Okoya has always supported every family member, including those who chose to start their own businesses.

They said it was unfair to overlook his contributions and portray him otherwise.

The family also said four highly influential family friends intervened in the dispute more than 40 years ago and held an all-night meeting to resolve it.

They further dismissed claims that Mr Okoya’s wife stopped Fatai from seeing his father during the birthday celebration, insisting that no such incident occurred.

“Surprised by what Fatai was asking for, they still concluded that his father should settle him with what he was asking for, and this was carried out accordingly. During the medical outreach organised for the Aare’s 86th birthday, Chief Mrs Okoya was introduced to Fatai Okoya.

“A family member then spoke to Fatai Okoya and advised him that the occasion was not an appropriate time or place to discuss the issues he has with his father. On that advice, which Fatai Okoya agreed with, he left the medical outreach venue. Other than exchanging pleasantries with him, Chief Mrs Shade Okoya, MON, said nothing to him that day, and several guests witnessed the entire incident.”

Privacy

Additionally, the family expressed displeasure over the public scrutiny, urging the media and members of the public to stop invading their privacy.

It insisted that any family member with a grievance against Mr Okoya must address it privately through the appropriate family channels, rather than turn personal matters into public spectacles.

“Aare and Chief Mrs Okoya, and indeed the entire Rasaq Okoya family, are very quiet, private and easygoing citizens focused on their family, their charitable work and their businesses.

“Chief Mrs Okoya respects her husband and his wishes. They do not intend to turn private affairs into disputes to air or discuss on social media. No misunderstanding can be settled online”, said the family.

World.title: Ebola: Africa CDC assures patient confidentiality amid contact tracing
World.content:
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has assured the public that patients’ personal information will remain confidential during ongoing Ebola containment operations, as authorities work to trace people who may have been exposed to the disease.

Wessam Mankoula, an epidemiologist and the agency’s Director of Emergency Preparedness and Response, gave the assurance during a virtual press briefing on Thursday. He explained that patients’ information was shared only with authorised investigators conducting contact tracing.

He said the information would not be disclosed publicly, emphasising the importance of protecting patients’ privacy during outbreak investigations.

The assurance follows the Nigerian government’s confirmation on Tuesday of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, is receiving medical care in isolation at a private hospital in the FCT.

Contact tracing

Mr Mankoula said Nigeria’s National Reference Laboratory confirmed that the imported case involved the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus.

He said 44 high-risk contacts had been identified, and the government was working to identify others who might have been exposed.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Contact tracing involves identifying and monitoring people who may have been in contact with an infected person, so possible infections can be detected early and further transmission limited.

Mr Mankoula also said investigators were examining a possible link between the Nigerian case and a case in Kenya. Both individuals had travelled through Entebbe International Airport in Uganda on 3 October.

He stressed that a connection remained under investigation and had not been established.

Regional response

Mr Mankoula said Africa CDC was working with partners, including the WHO, to strengthen disease surveillance and support preparedness measures. These included providing testing supplies at border areas near the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Nigeria’s case comes amid an Ebola outbreak in the DRC involving the Bundibugyo virus.

According to figures attributed to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), the DRC had recorded 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 related deaths as of 19 October, based on data up to 18 October.

The outbreak has affected 66 of the country’s 178 health zones across eight provinces, with Ituri the most affected province.

These developments have heightened concerns about Ebola’s cross-border spread and the need for countries to strengthen surveillance, laboratory testing and coordination to identify suspected cases promptly.

Africa CDC continues to work with national health authorities and international partners to support outbreak response efforts and limit further transmission.

World.title: BOI to expand financing for agriculture, healthcare manufacturing in 2027
World.content:
The Bank of Industry (BOI) said it will expand financing for agriculture, local healthcare manufacturing and digital businesses in 2027.

The bank stated this as it seeks to consolidate the gains of its 2025–2027 corporate strategy and strengthen Nigeria’s industrial development.

The bank’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Olasupo Olusi, disclosed the plan on Thursday at a meeting in Lagos, where he outlined the bank’s priorities for the final year of the strategy.

Mr Olusi said BOI would work with the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment on the National Industrial Finance Compact to attract more long-term capital into Nigeria’s industrial sector.

He also said the bank would deploy its new European Investment Bank facilities to agriculture and local healthcare manufacturing to increase domestic production of food and medicines.

The funding includes €85 million secured from the European Investment Bank for agriculture and another €50 million for healthcare manufacturing in 2026, as part of more than €2.2 billion in new funding the bank has secured for Nigerian industry since 2024.

“We will deploy our new European Investment Bank facilities into agriculture and local healthcare manufacturing, so that Nigeria produces more of the food and medicines it consumes,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The bank also plans to expand its information and communications technology (ICT) and digital economy portfolio through the Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) programme.

Mr Olusi said the initiatives formed part of the bank’s efforts to consolidate its achievements and meet the targets of its 2025–2027 corporate strategy.

“2027 is the final year of our strategy, and our task is to consolidate and meet every target we set,” the BOI boss, Mr Olusi, said.

BOI said it disbursed N644.9 billion in 2025, reaching 12,501 businesses and supporting 1.68 million jobs.

World.title: Oneremit taps Blockradar to enable Stablecoin flows across its cross- border network
World.content:
Stablecoins have given cross-border payment companies a faster way to move value between markets. They have also handed compliance teams a new set of questions.

For every stablecoin payment that passes through its network, Oneremit now asks three: Where did the funds come from? Where are they going? And can the company prove both, long after the transaction is complete?

To answer them, the Lagos-based cross-border payments company has integrated Blockradar, the stablecoin wallet infrastructure provider used by fintechs, exchanges and cross-border providers across emerging markets.

The first question is answered at the door. Wallet addresses involved in incoming stablecoin deposits are screened automatically against anti-money laundering (AML) and OFAC sanctions lists before funds are accepted. Oneremit identifies a deposit linked to a flagged or blacklisted wallet before it can enter its treasury.

The second is answered on the way out. Outgoing transfers go through the same screening, so Oneremit can pause, hold for review, or block a payout destined for a high-risk address, with Oneremit’s compliance team immediately.

The third is answered in the record. Every screening result, whether passed or failed, is attached to the transaction it belongs to. That gives Oneremit a clean, time-stamped trail for reconciliation, audits, and regulatory reporting across the jurisdictions it operates in, including Nigeria, Canada, and the United States. If a regulator in Toronto or Abuja asks about a single transfer months after it settled, the answer is already on file.

Behind the screening sits the rest of Blockradar’s infrastructure: non-custodial wallets, automatic sweeping of deposits into a central treasury, and support for major stablecoins including USDT and USDC across multiple blockchains. The result: stablecoin liquidity is easier to track and harder to lose sight of.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Speed only matters if you can stand behind every payment you move,” said Hammed Afenifere, CEO and co-founder of Oneremit. “Stablecoins let us settle faster than traditional banking allows. Blockradar means that speed doesn’t come at the expense of knowing exactly who is on either side of the transaction.”

The integration matters more as volumes grow. For a payments company working across several regulatory regimes, screening cannot rely on someone manually checking a list. It has to run on every transaction, in real time, and leave an audit trail.

“Stablecoins should work in the background whether users know they’re using them or not, and so should the compliance behind them work the same way,” said Morgan Williams, co founder and COO of Blockradar. “Oneremit is building exactly that way: screening every wallet on every transaction.”

The company has processed more than $200 million in outgoing cross-border transactions in under two years, while partnerships with providers including OwlPay and Blockradar are supporting the next phase of its settlement infrastructure. For the businesses paying suppliers and partners through Oneremit, most of this is invisible, and it is meant to be. What they see is a payment that arrives. What sits underneath is a system checking that it should.

World.title: Ebola: FG orders strict screening at Nigeria’s entry points
World.content:
The federal government has directed relevant agencies and health institutions to strictly enforce Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) screening and other entry protocols at Nigeria’s designated points of entry following reports of non-compliance with approved measures.

The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following concerns raised by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) over reported breaches of the government-approved protocols.

The directive was contained in a circular dated 22 October and signed by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, on behalf of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate.

The ministry said consistent and non-discriminatory enforcement of the protocols was necessary to reduce the risk of cross-border transmission and protect public health and national security.

Screening, surveillance

Under the directive, relevant ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs), health institutions and other stakeholders are required to comply with prescribed Ebola screening, health declaration, surveillance and other applicable entry requirements.

The ministry also called for stronger coordination, communication, and information sharing among the institutions responsible for implementing the measures.

It said these efforts would support effective disease surveillance, early detection and prompt responses to potential public health threats.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The directive comes as Nigerian health authorities respond to a confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), involving a woman who recently arrived in the country from Uganda.

The authorities have also begun contact tracing to identify people who may have been exposed to the virus.

Reporting breaches

The ministry directed relevant institutions to document and report any actual or attempted breaches of the approved protocols promptly through established channels.

It also urged them to support officials responsible for enforcing the measures and to establish monitoring and accountability mechanisms to sustain compliance.

The ministry stressed that personnel responsible for enforcement should be allowed to perform their duties professionally and without undue interference.

It further directed the immediate, widespread circulation of the advisory to relevant departments, units, field offices, and personnel to ensure they understood their responsibilities.

All concerned MDAs were instructed to treat the directive as a priority, promptly address identified lapses, and maintain compliance with the approved entry protocols.

The ministry said the measures were intended to safeguard public health and national safety.

World.title: Naira depreciates to N1,367/$ in parallel market
World.content:
*Interbank turnover rises 219%

By Elizabeth Adegbesan

The naira today depreciated to N1,367 per dollar from N1,363 in the parallel market on Thursday.

Similarly, the naira depreciated to N1,370 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM.

Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the naira rose to N1,370 per dollar from N1,365 per dollar on Thursday, indicating N5 depreciation for the naira.

Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets widened to N3 per dollar from N2 per dollar on Thursday.

The value of interbank turnover in NFEM increased by 219 per cent to $1.01 billion from $316.6 million on Thursday.

However, financial analysts expect the naira to remain depreciated.

In their weekly financial review and outlook, analysts at Cowry Asset Management said: “Going forward, the naira is expected to remain under pressure amid persistent demand for foreign exchange and prevailing market uncertainties, although the modest increase in external reserves could provide some support for currency stability.”

World.title: Police arrest suspect over murder of retired Ogun teacher
World.content:
police badge

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a suspect in connection with the murder of a 61-year-old retired teacher, Mrs Adedotun Adeteju Oluwaseun, who was found dead at her residence in Agbaakin Emere, Bode-Olude, Abeokuta.

The suspect, identified as Alhaji Saburi Lateef Ayinde, popularly known as “Oki-Ocean”, was arrested on Monday, October 19, 2026, following investigations by detectives attached to the Homicide Section of the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Eleweran, Abeokuta.

The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, who said the arrest followed sustained investigative efforts into the killing.

According to the statement, the deceased’s body was discovered in the toilet of her residence on February 28, 2026, a day after she reportedly returned from a retirement celebration organised by her colleagues.

The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the retired teacher was allegedly strangled and attacked with a machete during an altercation with the suspect.

The statement added that the case was subsequently transferred to the Homicide Section of the SCID for further investigation, which led to the suspect’s arrest.

“The suspect reportedly confessed to the killing and linked the incident to financial dealings with the deceased,” the statement said.

It explained that the suspect allegedly claimed he had entrusted ₦3.45 million to the deceased for safekeeping, with an understanding that she would lend him ₦1.5 million to purchase another vehicle.

However, the police said detectives were still working to corroborate the suspect’s account and establish the full circumstances surrounding the killing.

The State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, commended the investigating officers for their persistence, professionalism and commitment, which he said had resulted in a breakthrough in the case.

Ojajuni reiterated the command’s resolve to investigate serious crimes diligently, ensure accountability and bring offenders to justice through lawful prosecution.

The police said the suspect would be charged in court upon the conclusion of the investigation.

The command also urged residents to resolve disputes through lawful means and promptly report criminal activities to the appropriate authorities.

It assured members of the public that credible information provided to the police would be treated professionally and acted upon.

World.title: Messi receives top Spanish award from heir to throne
World.content:
Spain’s Princess Leonor shakes hands with Argentine football legend Lionel Messi as she awards him the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sport during the 2026 Princess of Asturias Awards ceremony at the Campoamor theatre in Oviedo on October 23, 2026. (Photo by ANDER GILLENEA / AFP)

Lionel Messi received Spain’s most prestigious sports award on Friday in recognition of his glittering career and his work for disadvantaged children’s access to health and education.

The Argentine forward, 39, was named winner of the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports in June, with the jury hailing “the most successful footballer of all time” and his social work.

Dozens of fans wearing Argentina football shirts cheered and chanted Messi’s name as he arrived to the sound of bagpipes and drums at the ceremony in Oviedo, capital of the northern Spanish region of Asturias.

Messi collected a formal roll of parchment from Princess Leonor, the heir to the Spanish throne after whom the awards are named, who lauded his “unique career”.

“He turned the extraordinary into routine by reading the game and deciding on the most effective option in fractions of a second, while respecting the collective essence above ego,” Leonor said.

One of the greatest footballers of all time, Messi has won eight Ballon d’Or titles, a World Cup and dozens of trophies at club level.

He spent 21 years at Barcelona where he played in a side that dominated Spain and Europe under Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique.

After leaving the Catalan club in 2021, Messi spent two years at French giants Paris Saint-Germain and currently plays for Inter Miami in MLS.

Argentina’s all-time top goalscorer, assist provider and caps holder called time on his international career earlier this year after losing the World Cup final to Spain in New Jersey.

“The most important thing is to know how to lose and how to win,” Messi told an event with children in Oviedo on Thursday, saying that attitude was “fundamental” in football.

Founded in 1981, the Princess of Asturias Awards are the most prestigious in the Spanish-speaking world and come with prize money of 50,000 euros ($56,000).

They encompass the arts, sciences and sports and are handed out annually in honour of efforts to improve human coexistence, solidarity and global cooperation.

British author Julian Barnes, trailblazing US astronaut Christina Koch and punk star Patti Smith were among the other winners who received their prize on Friday.

Previous winners of the sports award include tennis greats Serena Williams and Rafael Nadal, marathon record-breaker Eliud Kipchoge and US skier Lindsey Vonn.

World.title: BBNaija should take a break, re-strategise— Tacha
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Reality TV star Natacha Akide has urged Big Brother Naija organisers to take a break and re-strategise, saying the show needs fresh ideas to hold viewers’ attention in an entertainment landscape increasingly shaped by social media.

Speaking on Arise 360 on Arise News, the former housemate said the show’s earlier success came at a time when social media played a different role in people’s lives.

“I think they need to take a break, restrategise and just come up with something because we are really at an era where everything happens on social media,” she said.

Tacha argued that online conversations now compete with reality television for viewers’ attention, pointing to the ongoing public interest in the dispute involving music duo P-Square.

“You don’t want us watching housemates in the house, meanwhile P-Square is giving us part seven of his family issues… we have come to a point where everyone is so comfortable with social media right now,” she said.

She suggested that stepping away for a while could give audiences time to miss the programme before it returns with a refreshed format.

“You also give Nigerians a chance to miss you,” she said.

Tacha called on the organisers to develop concepts that would feel new and more compelling to Nigerian viewers. “They need to cook, like they need to try to do something different which will be much more mind-blowing and more interesting to Nigerians

because Nigerians are hard to please,” she added

Tacha rose to prominence on the 2019 “Pepper Dem” edition of BBNaija, but was disqualified following a physical altercation with fellow housemate Mercy Eke. Since leaving the show, she has pursued ventures in entertainment and fashion, worked as a radio host on 96.9 Cool Fm and launched Tacha FC in 2024.

Vanguard News

World.title: Russia says Ukraine, US talks ‘planned’ for Abu Dhabi
World.content:
AFP photo

Talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States are planned to resume in November in the United Arab Emirates, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday.

Russia indicated its readiness to resume the talks, which have been at a standstill since the beginning of the year, following a meeting this week in Saint Petersburg between President Vladimir Putin and US special envoy Steve Witkoff.

The next round of talks towards ending the Ukraine war, which is grinding through its fifth year, are “planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi”, and “will take place in a trilateral format”, Peskov told reporters.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the plan to meet in November in a post on X.

“Now we all need to focus on making these meetings happen –- together with America, Europe, and all our partners,” he said Friday.

The announcement came amid intensified diplomatic efforts by US President Donald Trump’s administration. Witkoff met on Tuesday with Zelensky and European leaders in Oslo, before meeting with Putin on Wednesday.

Following the meetings, both Kyiv and Moscow voiced their readiness to resume direct talks mediated by Washington.

Russia, which launched its full-scale offensive against Ukraine in February 2022, has suggested talks could take place “around November 10”. Zelensky has called for the discussions to happen “as soon as possible”.

In a televised interview aired late Thursday, Putin said that any trilateral talks would focus on the security arrangements of a final peace deal and not a “short” truce.

World.title: Coastal Road: ‘I’m local champion; you’re pretender’ —  Gov Diri replies Duke
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri has hit back at former Cross River State governor and Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) presidential candidate Donald Duke, calling him a “jester and a pretender” after Duke’s remarks about the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

In a recent interview on Arise Television, the PRP candidate called governor Diri a “local champion” while arguing that the coastal road project was not feasible because of its cost and Bayelsa State’s terrain.

Diri had earlier rejected Duke’s claim that building the highway through Bayelsa was not feasible, adding that the ex-governor is “not abreast of current developments in road construction and infrastructure” in Bayelsa.

Reacting to Diri’s comment, Duke said: “The governor of Bayelsa, if he did say so, I don’t know the fellow, but if he did say so, I think he’s just being a local champion.”

One week after Duke’s comment, Governor Diri, in a video which has now gone viral, fired back at the PRP candidate, saying he’s a local champion elected to defend his people.

“Yes, I’m a local champion, because that is where I was raised. I am elected to defend the local people. I am elected to champion their cause. But Donald Duke, let me ask you, you were on seat when Bakassi was ceeded out of Nigeria.

“You were the sitting governor of Cross River state. Because you are not a local champion, you did nothing about it. I believe that you are more of a jester and a pretender,” he said.

Diri also questioned Duke’s political standing in his own ward, and said the dispute was about his people and the region, not simply a personal disagreement.

“Donald Duke, I am not one who takes up people, I am not one of those who insult people; I don’t insult leaders; I don’t insult elders but what you have done is not just about me, it is about my environment, it is about my people.”

The governor further defended the region’s development potential, saying Bayelsa and other coastal communities should not be defined by their difficult terrain.

“Donald Duke, I am not that fellow, I am the sitting governor of Bayelsa state. All of us from this region, particularly from Bayelsa state, do not accept the narrative that your state cannot be developed.

We have a very rich ancestry, our terrain is one of the best if we develop it and we are prepared to take our destiny into our hands.”

Diri also thanked the President for supporting the coastal road, describing it as an opportunity to address poverty and the dehumanisation of coastal communities.

World.title: U-17 WWC: Flamingos beat North Korea 3-1 to reach knockout stage
World.content:
Photo: FIFA

By Ayobami Okerinde

Nigeria’s Flamingos have advanced to the knockout stage of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating defending champions North Korea 3-1 in their final Group B match.

The Flamingos secured the victory at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Salé, Morocco on Friday.

Nigeria went into the encounter needing a win to guarantee their progress after losing to Poland in their second match, having opened their campaign with a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico.

Akeem Busari’s side rose to the occasion, with Oluwakemi Adegbuyi opening the scoring in the 15th minute.

Oluebube Umejiaku extended Nigeria’s lead in the 38th minute, beating North Korea’s high defensive line before finishing past the goalkeeper.

Kanyisola Yusuf then put the Flamingos firmly in control with a third goal early in 56th minutes

North Korea pulled one back through a penalty in the 82nd minutes, but Nigeria held firm defensively to preserve their two-goal advantage and secure the victory.

The result saw Nigeria finish second in Group B behind North Korea, who claimed top spot on goals scored. Poland ended the group stage in third place despite finishing level on points with the top two teams.

World.title: Tinubu’s Kaduna rally won’t save him in 2027 — Makinde campaign
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organization (MDPCO) has dismissed President Bola Tinubu’s planned 2027 campaign flag-off in Kaduna State, declaring that insecurity, economic hardship and alleged marginalisation of the North would cost him re-election.

In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, the organisation said Saturday’s rally would not erase public anger over Tinubu’s record, insisting that the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Engr. Seyi

Makinde, was poised to defeat him.

The campaign organisation challenged Tinubu to justify his administration’s record in the North, recalling his 2022 campaign promise to eliminate bandits and kidnappers troubling Kaduna and other parts of the region.

“Since President Tinubu decided to flag off his 2027 Presidential campaign in Kaduna, the political headquarters of the North, we challenge him to explain what the region has gained from his incompetent and nepotic administration beyond a bumper harvest of bloodshed, crushing economic hardship, broken promises and shattered public trust,” Ihediwa said.

The MDPCO claimed that at least 13,000 people had been killed in northern Nigeria since Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while an estimated 3.7 million had been displaced.

It also accused the administration of protecting APC campaign billboards while communities remained vulnerable to attacks, and alleged that the North had been sidelined in strategic federal appointments.

“Under Tinubu, political s appear better protected than human lives,” the organisation said.

The organisation said Tinubu’s assurance that Northerners would never regret voting for him had been undermined by worsening

insecurity and economic hardship, arguing that the region deserved more than campaign promises.

It urged Nigerians to embrace Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda, expressing confidence that public discontent would translate

into an electoral setback for the APC in 2027.

World.title: Cross River Lauds DSS, Others For Intercepting 3 GPMGs, Cache of High-calibre Arms
World.content:
The Cross River government has lauded the Department of State Services (DSS) and sister security agencies for recently intercepting a huge cache of High-calibre weapons, which included three General Purpose Machine Guns (GPMGs).

The state Deputy Governor Rt. Hon. Peter Odey made the commendation on Friday after inspecting the seized weapons at the DSS state headquarters in Calabar.

Odey, whose visit was on behalf of Governor Bassey Otu, commended the Service on the intelligence operation that led to the seizure of the weapons which included seven A-K 47 assault rifles.

The deputy governor stated that the arrest of two suspected gunrunners during the operation, would help the DSS and sister security agencies apprehend those behind the illegal arms trade.

He noted that had the weapons not been intercepted, there was a strong possibility that it could be used to wreak havoc in the state and neighbouring states, particularly during the forthcoming general elections.

The deputy governor praised the growing synergy between the security agencies and the military, saying the development has helped the government increasingly turn the tide against criminal elements.

World.title: 24 State Houses Of Assembly Okay State Police Bill
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency on Friday has expressed happiness as State Police Amendment Bill scales constitutional hurdle in 24 out of the 36 states of the federation.

Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon Femi Gbajabiamila, noted with satisfaction that the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for a dual policing system, has been approved by 24 State Houses of Assembly, meeting the constitutional threshold of two-thirds of the 36 states.

Gbajabiamila, in a release,commended the State Houses of Assembly for their decisive action on this reform of national importance and appreciates the National Assembly for passing the amendment in both chambers.

According to him, in line with Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, the amendment can now be returned to the National Assembly for transmission to Mr President for assent.

Gbajabiamila further said: “The approval gives constitutional backing to the policing framework that the Working Group’s draft National Policing Bill, 2026 is designed to implement.

“The Working Group’s efforts remain on track. The draft Bills are currently undergoing legislative drafting review and validation at the Federal Ministry of Justice and are expected to be returned on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. Thereafter, the Group will give them final consideration before presenting them to Mr President.

“The Working Group urges all stakeholders to support a smooth transition to a dual policing system that makes Nigerians safer.”

The Presidency had on Tuesday disclosed that the draft of the 2026 National Policing Bill is ready.

Gbajabiamila, stated in a release that the group has completed the drafting stage of its assignment and has formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), together with 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting review and validation.

According to him, the submission took place on Monday, 19th October, 2026, to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan while the Ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws.

The Ministry of Justice, he further said, is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026 and the Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate.

Gbajabiamila further said: The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

“The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly.

“The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.”

The Presidency had last Thursday hinted that the National Policing Bill will be transmitted to the National Assembly within two weeks.

Gbajabiamila had told newsmen after the steering committee meeting at the State House in Abuja that “The National Policing Bill is more or less ready for transmission to the National Assembly. We will probably have one more meeting after this to cross the t’s and dot the i’s and make sure every area is covered. So, we are 90% ready.

“The governors have one or two observations, and we should be ready in about a week or so.”

He described the bill as ‘the most consequential Bill of the administration so far’ adding that it has undergone strenuous exercises in the last few weeks since the working group’s steering committee began deliberations on August 3, 2026.

Also commenting on the possibility of the states dragging their feet on the passage of the Sixth Constitution Alteration Bill (State Police), especially against the backdrop of the information that only about six states had passed the amendment out of the 36 states and the FCT, Gbajabiamila affirmed that there was a “national consensus” among Nigerians on the need for the amendments.

“I see no reason why anyone will want to have a rethink on it,” he said.

Members of the committee present at the Thursday’s meeting held at the conference hall of the Chief of Staff Office at the State House, Abuja, were Chairman of the Governors’ Forum and Governor of Kwara State, AbdulRazak AbdulRahman; Governors Dapo Abiodun, Ogun State; Uba Sani, Kaduna State; Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, and the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice represented by the Solicitor General and Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Justice, Mrs Beatrice Jedy-Agba.

Others included Chairman, Policy Advisory Committee, Justice Abdullahi Liman (rtd); Head, Nigeria Police Reform Secretariat, Professor Olu Ogunsakin; Special Adviser to the President on National Assembly Matters (House of Representatives), Dr Lanre Smart; Senior Special Assistant to the President on Planning and Research who also doubles as the Secretary of the Committee, Nnadubem Moghalu; representative of the President of the Nigerian Bar Association; and AIG Abraham Nabhon Thomas, representing the National Security Adviser, among others.

President Bola Tinubu had on July 7, 2026, inaugurated the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill to prepare the legal framework for the implementation of state police across the country.

The Working Group’s inauguration followed the National Assembly’s passage of the Constitution Alteration (State Police) Bill, 2026, in which the President proposes a dual policing structure comprising the Federal Police Service and 36 State Police Services.

Tinubu had pisited that while the constitutional amendment creates the framework for state police, the National Policing Bill would provide the legal structure for its implementation.“The Constitution Amendment Bill establishes the framework for dual policing, but it does not operationalise it. That work is left to the National Policing Bill.”

According to him, the proposed legislation would address issues necessary for a smooth operationalisation of the State Police system.

“The proposed National Policing Bill will include provisions on minimum policing standards, state readiness certification, federal-state coordination, accountability, human rights safeguards and fiscal conditions.”

The President said the committee will produce an implementation-ready draft bill immediately after the constitutional amendment process.

“The Working Group has been constituted to produce a technically robust, implementation-ready draft National Policing Bill for transmission to the National Assembly,” Tinubu said.

He said the committee was necessary to avoid delays after the State Police bill passed.

“We must not wait until the constitutional process is concluded before beginning this important assignment,” he said.

World.title: NUJ Honours FCC Commissioner, Peter Eze, for Youth Leadership in Enugu
World.content:
The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Enugu State Council, Correspondents’ Chapel, has honoured the Federal Character Commission (FCC) Commissioner representing Enugu State, Hon. Peter Ogbonna Eze, with an Award of Excellence for Outstanding Youth Leadership.

The award was presented on Thursday night, October 22, 2026, at the grand finale of the 2026 Correspondents’ Chapel Press Week, held at the NUJ Press Centre, Rangers Avenue, Enugu.

Eze was recognised for his contributions to youth empowerment, skills development, talent discovery and efforts to connect young people with employment and career opportunities.

The event was chaired by former Attorney General of Enugu State, Chief Anthony Ani (SAN), and focused on the theme ‘Strengthening Democracy Through Responsible Journalism: 2027 Polls in Focus.’

Other awardees at the event included the Minister of Works, Senator Dave Umahi; Deputy National Chairman South of the APC, Mr Ben Nwoye; the Executive Director of PRODA, Dr Peter Ogbobe, and the Enugu State Commissioner of Police, CP Mamman Bitrus Giwa.

Reacting after receiving the plaque, Eze said he was deeply honoured and humbled because the recognition came from journalists, people whose work is to inform the public, hold leaders accountable and shape opinions.

He thanked the NUJ Correspondents’ Chapel for finding him worthy and asked journalists to continue to stand as the conscience of the nation through courageous reporting, balanced stories and fair judgment.

According to him, the award is not just about what he has done before but a fresh call to do more, adding that he remains committed to creating opportunities for young people and to serving society in a way where leadership is judged not by title but by how many lives it touches.

“The honour is appreciated, the responsibility is understood, and the commitment to service remains unwavering,” Eze said.

Eze’s recognition highlights the importance of youth-focused initiatives amid continuing concerns about unemployment, skills development and economic opportunities for young Nigerians.

A major initiative highlighted was the Peter Eze Youth Connect 2026, which brought together thousands of young people for engagement, mentorship, career guidance and access to professional development opportunities.

The initiative seeks to bridge the gap between young people and available opportunities by connecting them with relevant institutions, professionals and stakeholders who can support their career aspirations and economic advancement.

Through Peter Eze Youth Connect-an event that was adjudged the most popular and impactful youth event in 2026, the FCC commissioner has sought to create platforms for mentorship, career exploration and professional networking, enabling young people to pursue greater economic independence and contribute to societal development.

World.title: Ebola Patient in Nigeria Identified as Wife of Swiss Diplomat
World.content:
Switzerland’s foreign ministry has confirmed that the woman who has tested positive for Ebola in Nigeria is the wife of a Swiss diplomat.

The woman, a 42-year-old Ugandan-born national who lives in the Nigerian capital, Abuja, tested positive for the virus on 20 October, becoming the country’s first confirmed Ebola patient in more than a decade.

They both travelled to Uganda earlier this month. Her husband is currently in isolation but has not developed any symptoms, according to the Swiss foreign ministry.

The ministry told the BBC that all 25 staff at its embassy in Nigeria were in good health and did not need to isolate.

The ministry said the woman had spent about a week at a private clinic in Abuja with symptoms before her diagnosis.

It believes she contracted the virus while travelling in Uganda, although health authorities have yet to establish the source of her infection.

Uganda borders Democratic Republic of Congo, where some 4,600 have died in the country’s most deadly outbreak of Ebola. Two people died in Uganda shortly after the outbreak began in May but it has been declared free of Ebola since August.

The ministry said the decision not to isolate the embassy’s eight Swiss and 17 local employees was taken in consultation with Nigeria’s Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization (WHO).

It added that the embassy remained open and operational, with health and safety measures in place.

The woman is receiving treatment in isolation and is showing signs of improvement, according to the WHO.

She returned to Nigeria on 3 October after spending about two and a half weeks in Uganda.

The patient did ​not travel to DR Congo, the Swiss ‌government told Reuters news agency on Friday, contradicting accounts from Uganda.

She developed symptoms four days after arriving in Abuja and sought treatment at two private health facilities before testing positive for Ebola on 20 October.

Health officials are now investigating whether she may have crossed paths with a Kenyan man who died from Ebola and had travelled through Uganda’s main airport on the same day.

Investigators are examining whether they could have been exposed through shared equipment or other contact, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) said on Thursday.
