World.title: Japan-Russia ties erode as journalist sits in Moscow jail
World.content:
Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. The Kremlin claims that Japan is using journalists as spies.

Japanese Foreign Ministry officials were in Moscow this week in an attempt to contact a journalist arrested in Russia's far east on allegations of spying.

Journalist Yuki Imai was arrested on October 14 by Russia's FSB security service in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk on Sakhalin Island. Televised footage of the arrest showed FSB officers barging into his hotel room as he slept.

The correspondent for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper was accused of attempting to obtain information on soldiers in the region, which is near the Kiril islands, a geopolitical sore spot in Russia-Japan relations.

Russian authorities quickly transferred him to Lefortovo Prison in Moscow, where a court ordered him to be held in pretrial detention until at least December 12. If convicted, 34-year-old Imai faces up to 20 years in jail, according to the International Federation of Journalists, which has called for his immediate release.

Officials from the Japanese embassy in Moscow have been denied access to Imai. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has condemned the arrest and dismissed the claim that Imai was a spy.

Russian Ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev said Imai had been caught "red-handed," the official TASS news agency reported. Nozdrev has claimed that Japanese intelligence agencies use journalists to collect classified information with the goal of "undermining Russia's security and defense capability."

Russia accuses journalists of being 'spies'

Yoji Gomi, a veteran journalist and author who has reported from across Asia, told DW that Japanese journalists may occasionally meet with diplomats in the course of their work and "share thoughts and impressions." However, he rejects the idea that reporters are paid spies.

"One-party nations often see foreign correspondents as spies because that is exactly what they use their journalists for," he said.

"I can completely see how the Russians decided that Imai was a spy, as it is how they operate, plus he was in a sensitive part of Russia where there are lots of North Korean laborers that they want to keep quiet," Gomi added.

Japan condemns Putin visit to disputed Kuril Islands To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Stephen Nagy, a professor of international relations at Tokyo's International Christian University, told DW that Russia might see Imai as a bargaining chip it can use to exchange for nationals detained overseas.

Nagy doubts that Japan will give in to pressure.

"They are going to resist because it means that Russia, or any other country, can then just seize a Japanese national, put them on trial for espionage and demand the release of one of their people," he said.

"It would set a dangerous precedent," he added.

The arrest comes after a member of the Russia-linked hacking group Qilin was arrested in Japan and extradited to Germany to face charges in connection with a 2024 cyberattack on a logistics center.

The last time a journalist was arrested in Russia was in 2019 for "attempting to obtain classified information about Russia's military potential in the Far East," Russia's Interfax news agency reported. However, in this case, the journalist was quickly released.

Imai's case is perhaps the most serious since 2023, when Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich was arrested in Russia and sentenced to 16 years in a penal colony before being released in a prisoner exchange with Western countries in 2024.

Russia has previously arrested foreign journalists for prisoner exchanges. US reporter Evan Gershkovich is seen here in a Moscow court. Image: Dmitry Serebryakov/AP/picture alliance

Strained Japan-Russia ties

Imai's arrest is the latest in a series of incidents that have sent bilateral relations into a tailspin.

Nagy said Imai's seizure was designed to put pressure on Tokyo. He added this is part of a coordinated approach with China to isolate Japan at a time when the US is preoccupied with domestic issues and the conflict in the Middle East.

"Moscow and Beijing are coordinating to create the image that Japan is not a reformed member of the international community but still the military state of the 1930s and that it poses a threat to stability in the Indo-Pacific region," Nagy said.

"This is all designed to smear Japan's efforts to lead diplomacy in the region at a time when the US is perhaps distracted," he said. "And it does not even matter much that it is not true; they will just continue to repeat the claim to discredit and weaken Tokyo."

Decadeslong row over disputed islands

Tadashi Anno, a professor of politics at Tokyo's Sophia University, told DW that he believes Japan had been working hard to maintain a stable relationship with Russia, even after Tokyo joined international condemnation of the invasion of Ukraine.

Anno said Russia's timing in turning up the heat on Japan was puzzling.

"Japan condemned the invasion of Ukraine in 2022 because it was a fundamental violation of international law, but Russia is only now pushing back hard," he said.

At the center of deteriorating ties is a territorial dispute about a chain of islands off the far north of Japan that were seized by Soviet forces after Japan's surrender in World War II.

There had been hopes in the past in Tokyo that a concerted diplomatic effort could be sufficient to convince Russia to return the islands — known as the Northern Territories in Japan and the Southern Kurils by Russia — to Japanese sovereignty.

That campaign has faltered in the past couple of years, and was further dented when Japan announced in the spring that it would be joining the NATO initiative to provide nonlethal assistance to Kyiv.

In August, President Vladimir Putin visited the disputed islands, becoming only the second Russian leader to do so. Earlier this month, a delegation of Chinese businesspeople was welcomed on one of the islands, and talks are underway on the possibility of economic cooperation.

Edited by: Wesley Rahn

World.title: El Supremo exige al Gobierno la lista de los afectados por la ‘ley de nietos’ y amenaza de multa y posible responsabilidad penal si no lo hace
World.content:
La retirada masiva del derecho al voto a los nacionalizados por la Ley de Memoria Democrática ha derivado en un pulso entre el Tribunal Supremo y el Gobierno de consecuencias, por ahora, imprevisibles. La Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo ha dado este viernes cinco días a los ministros Félix Bolaños y José Manuel Albares para que remitan al alto tribunal, a la Junta Electoral Central y a la Oficina del Censo Electoral la lista con los nombres de las 163.020 personas afectadas por la suspensión del derecho al voto de la llamada ley de nietos y les amenaza con una multa y posibles responsabilidades penales si no cumplen antes del 28 de octubre. En dos autos notificados para informar de esa medida, el alto tribunal revela que, según los datos aportados por la Abogacía del Estado, se han revisado 31.390 expedientes, de los que solo se han expedido 91 certificados por parte de los encargados de los consulados a descendientes del exilio, la condición que impusieron los jueces a los nacionalizados por la ley de nietos para poder votar en las elecciones del 29 de noviembre.

Tras conocer la decisión del Supremo, el ministro de Justicia ha asegurado que su departamento entregó el 15 de octubre a la Oficina del Censo Electoral la documentación con “todos los nombres” de los expedientes de nacionalidades otorgadas por la ley de nietos que están digitalizados, que Justicia cifra en unos 76.000 (los tramitados desde mediados de 2024). Fuentes de este ministerio explican que la información se envió a la Oficina del Censo porque fue este órgano el que lo reclamó, y que no se ha remitido nada al Supremo porque, hasta este viernes, desde el alto tribunal no se le ha requerido. Para revisar los expedientes que no están digitalizados, hace falta examinarlos uno por uno lo que, según estas fuentes, hace muy difícil tener la relación que pide el Supremo dentro del plazo de cinco días. Por su parte, fuentes de Exteriores han recalcado que el Ministerio y todos los consulados de España “están realizando todos los esfuerzos necesarios desde el primer auto del Tribunal Supremo para cumplir con estos”. “Se van a redoblar esfuerzos si aún cabe para cumplir con este nuevo auto”, informa Laura Llach.

En los autos por los que el Supremo comunicó la semana pasada su rechazo a levantar la suspensión del derecho al voto tras el adelanto electoral, el tribunal ya reprochó al Gobierno y al Instituto Nacional de Estadística, de quien depende el censo, que no hayan entregado aún el desglose entre las personas que se han nacionalizado bajo el paraguas de la Ley de Memoria (que reconocía el derecho a la nacionalidad a los descendientes de españoles exiliados por motivos políticos, ideológicos o de orientación sexual) de las que lo han hecho por la instrucción dictada por el Ministerio de Justicia (que extiende la posibilidad de obtener la nacionalidad a hijos o nietos de cualquier emigrado y presupone la condición de exiliado a todos los españoles que salieron del país entre el 18 de julio de 1936 y el 31 de diciembre de 1955), que, según el Supremo, no se ajusta a la ley. La Sala de lo Contencioso suspendió el voto de todos, pero acordó que quienes hayan obtenido la nacionalidad al amparo de la ley podrán votar si presentan un certificado del consulado que acredite su condición de descendiente del exilio.

El tribunal ordenó ese desglose el 10 de septiembre con la intención de que solo se mantuviera la suspensión del voto a los nacionalizados por la instrucción. Pero, ya antes del adelanto electoral, la Dirección General de Asuntos Consulares había advertido de que era “materialmente imposible” hacer esa distinción antes del 1 de enero de 2027, fecha que marca el censo que se usará en las elecciones autonómicas y municipales de mayo, que eran las únicas con fecha segura en ese momento. Y, una vez que se han convocado elecciones para el 29 de noviembre, los consulados consideran que esa posibilidad es inviable.

En los autos de este viernes, la sala reprocha al Gobierno que solo le haya facilitado la cifra de los nacionalizados por la Ley de Memoria Democrática inscritos en el CERA a fecha del pasado 1 de agosto, que es el censo válido para el 29-N. Los jueces exponen que el último escrito que ha entregado al tribunal la Abogacía del Estado, del pasado miércoles 21 de octubre, incluye tres documentos: dos informes de la Dirección General de Españoles en el Exterior y Asuntos Consulares y uno del Instituto Nacional de Estadística, en los que se explica que, hasta ese día, se habían revisado 31.390 expedientes de nacionalizados por la ley de nietos, de los que se han expedido solo 91 certificados por parte de los encargados de los Registros Consulares a personas que han acreditado el exilio de sus padres o abuelos. “Puesto que la Administración conoce perfectamente, porque ha tramitado y resuelto estos expedientes, la identidad de todas estas personas, no se acierta a adivinar cuáles puedan ser las razones por las que no se haya facilitado a esta Sala la relación nominal de los electores, máxime cuando hay un proceso electoral convocado y, por aplicación de las medidas cautelares de suspensión impuestas, estas personas pueden verse imposibilitadas finalmente del ejercicio de su derecho al voto por la propia inacción de la Administración”, señala el tribunal.

Hasta ahora, los magistrados habían dirigido sus peticiones a la Junta Electoral Central (JEC) y a la Abogacía del Estado, pero, en esta ocasión, lo hacen con apercibimiento directo al ministro de Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes y al de Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación. La sala les avisa de que, si antes de las 15.00 horas del próximo 28 de octubre no entregan los nombres de los 163.020 afectados, podrá acordar la imposición de una multa de 1.000 euros a Bolaños y Albares y repetirla “hasta la completa ejecución del fallo judicial, sin perjuicio de otras responsabilidades patrimoniales a que hubiere lugar”. Los jueces advierten también de la posibilidad de enviar el incumplimiento del Gobierno a la justicia penal para que se evalúe si los ministros hubieran incurrido en un delito de desobediencia.

El acuerdo del Supremo cuenta con el voto particular de uno de los seis miembros del tribunal, la magistrada Alicia Milán, quien ya se opuso a la suspensión del derecho al sufragio suscrita por el resto de la sala. En su voto, Millán defiende que las medidas adoptadas “afectan medularmente a la estabilidad del censo electoral, al que se califica como provisional, materializan la inseguridad jurídica y la incertidumbre operativa”, por lo que son “incompatibles con las exigencias de certeza, estabilidad y regularidad que constituyen las bases de todo proceso electoral democrático”.

Orden a la Junta Electoral

En los autos de este viernes, el Supremo da directrices a la JEC sobre cómo organizar el voto CERA para el 29-N. Este sábado 24 de octubre empieza el plazo para enviar a los inscritos en el censo del extranjero la documentación necesaria para poder participar en las elecciones, y la Junta Electoral acordó la semana pasada mantener este envío, pero incluyendo una advertencia con la posibilidad de que el derecho al voto haya quedado afectado por la decisión del Tribunal Supremo respecto a la ley de nietos.

La JEC envió al Supremo el texto pactado y el tribunal ha cambiado esa redacción por una advertencia expresa que recoge que quienes hayan obtenido la nacionalidad por la Ley de Memoria están en el censo “con carácter provisional” y “tal inclusión no significa que puedan llegar a ejercer su derecho al voto, pues únicamente podrán votar aquellas personas ‘con respecto a las cuales los encargados de los Registros Consulares expidan certificación acreditativa de su condición de nacidos fuera de España, de padre o madre, abuelo o abuela, que originariamente hubieran sido españoles, y que hubieran sufrido exilio por razones políticas, ideológicas o de creencia o de orientación de identidad sexual y que hubieran perdido o renunciado a la nacionalidad española’, sin haber aplicado la presunción” de exilio que recoge la instrucción dictada por Justicia el 25 de octubre de 2022.

Los jueces advierten también a la JEC de que, una vez que el Gobierno envíe el listado con los nombres de los nacionalizados por la Ley de Memoria, deberá “excluir” del CERA para las elecciones del 29 de noviembre “a todas ellas salvo aquellas a las que los encargados de los Registros Consulares hayan expedido” la certificación que acredite que son descendientes de exiliados por razones políticas, ideológicas o de orientación sexual.

Directrices para el día de la votación

Las directrices que da el Supremo se extienden al propio procedimiento del voto en el exterior. Los jueces ordenan que, para el depósito del voto en las urnas en las Oficinas Consulares (previsto el 21 y el 26 de noviembre) estas deberán disponer del listado del CERA remitido por la Oficina del Censo Electoral, una vez realizadas las correcciones impuestas por el tribunal. “En el caso de que una persona no aparezca inscrita en dicho listado, los responsables consulares recibirán su documentación electoral pero no la introducirán en la urna, sino que la mantendrán aparte para su envío [...] junto con el resto de la documentación electoral pero debidamente diferenciada. De ello se dejará constancia en el acta consular”, señalan los jueces.

Para el recuento del voto CERA, el tribunal insta a que, el día del escrutinio general, las Juntas Electorales Provinciales deberán utilizar el listado que la Oficina del Censo Electoral les haya facilitado antes de ese día, en el que se hayan incorporado las correcciones ordenadas por el Supremo. Únicamente introducirán en la urna los sobres de los electores que estén incluidos en el listado del CERA que resulte de excluir a quienes no tengan certificado de antecedentes de exilio. El resto, no se puede meter en la urna, sino que tendrá que guardarse junto con el resto de su documentación electoral, “haciéndolo constar además en el acta de la sesión”.

World.title: Todos los ojos se vuelven al norte: lo que pasa cuando se empuja a los creadores
World.content:
Faro Santander, el nuevo espacio cultural y museístico del norte de España, lanza la II convocatoria de Ayudas a la Creación para artistas cántabros de cualquier disciplina, un programa que, además de ayuda económica, provee de asesorías especializadas y garantiza una muestra pública en el museo. Los ganadores de la primera convocatoria cuentan su experiencia

Suelen identificarse solo a toro pasado: aquel momento me cambió la vida. Hay oportunidades, sin embargo, cuyo brillo se deja ver desde el principio. Esta es una de esas. Faro Santander lanza su II Convocatoria de Ayudas a la Creación, un programa que ofrece a los proyectos seleccionados una dotación económica de 10.000 euros, seminarios y mentorías con profesionales, la ocasión de compartir proceso creativo con otros artistas y, como remate, una muestra pública en un espacio tan espectacular como el Edificio Pereda, convertido desde su reciente rehabilitación y apertura en Santander en uno de los grandes focos culturales de todo el norte de España.

Hasta el 15 de febrero de 2027 puede disfrutarse gratuitamente, comisariado por Ane Rodríguez, del resultado de los cuatro proyectos becados en la primera edición. Talento cántabro que, a partir de distintas manifestaciones culturales ligadas a esa verde tierra, ha generado un trabajo variado, muy contemporáneo y de vocación universal. En Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas, Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva recuperan materiales de un archivo de educación sexual de hace décadas; una obra, la que proponen, que cultiva la sensibilidad, que induce a la reflexión sobre gestos cotidianos como el abrazo. En Una forma minúscula, de Salón de belleza, nombre del colectivo formado por Manuela Gutiérrez y Cristina Somavilla, el cine de arte y ensayo sirve como pretexto para encontrarse y hablar, para crear comunidad y traer a la conversación la olvidada contracultura santanderina. La pintora Amaia Bregel, por primera vez en su carrera en piezas de gran escala, en Ludarquías muestra instalaciones y dispositivos impregnados de todo su saber pictórico (“Casi todo el arte contemporáneo es hijo de la pintura”, cuenta). El dúo Casapalma —Irene Atienza y Yoel Molina—, cuya música bucea en el folclore cántabro, ha logrado terminar el rodaje de un documental titulado La Suite de los Riconchos que se estrena el próximo 22 de octubre y nos trae ese ancestral conocimiento que se esconde en las danzas tradicionales y la etnografía.

Entre todos los aspirantes, el jurado escogió proyectos en los que, además de formatos convencionales, cupieran investigaciones artísticas y apuestas valientes: se valora documentación, proceso, método y pensamiento tanto como pieza final. Una característica de este programa de ayudas que los cuatro beneficiarios destacan, por inusual en el panorama nacional: “Ojalá mantengan este espíritu”, indica Germán de la Riva. La visibilidad que les ha otorgado este reconocimiento, sobre todo al verse expuestos en Marisma, en la primera planta de Faro, vecinos a una colección permanente que abarca obra desde El Greco a Frida Kahlo, es el otro gran privilegio que los artistas unánimemente señalan: “Para mí supuso un punto de inflexión”, confiesa Amaia Bregel; para ella, esta ha sido la puerta hacia otras becas o ferias de enorme prestigio, como la de Casa Velázquez o Estampa.

“Animaos a participar, sea cual sea vuestra idea”, ese es el mensaje común de los primeros beneficiarios para quienes les sigan.

Segunda convocatoria Ayudas Plazo de admisión 2026 15 octubre -

09 de noviembre Dotación económica 10.000 euros Beneficiarios Cuatro artistas (o colectivos de artistas) de cualquier disciplina, residentes o nacidos en Cantabria Así funciona el programa de acompañamiento: El proyecto debe desarrollarse en Cantabria, entre enero y junio de 2027

Se priorizarán aquellos que fomenten la generación de tejido artístico en el territorio

Se realizará un encuentro inicial entre comisarios, coordinadores y beneficiarios

Los beneficiarios dispondrán de cuatro seminarios y talleres con profesionales invitados, uno a la semana durante el primer mes de trabajo

Estos encuentros colectivos periódicos que estarán abiertos a otros artistas que deseen inscribirse

Los beneficiarios podrán solicitar tutorías personalizadas y seguimiento continuo

Al final del programa, se organizará una muestra pública en Faro Santander, a partir de septiembre de 2027

Amaia Bregel y

Ludarquías

Cuando Amaia Bregel volvió a Santander en marzo de 2020, con la pandemia, no tenía intención de quedarse. Se había graduado en Bellas Artes en Valencia, donde continuó con un máster de Producción de Arte y Pensamiento Contemporáneo y donde, sin aquel terremoto mundial, seguramente se habría imaginado residiendo todavía. Hoy, sin embargo, reivindica las posibilidades halladas en su ciudad: “Mucha gente de mi generación volvió y entre todos hemos creado una red. Soy la que más defiende Santander ahora mismo”, reclama entre risas.

05:15 Amaia Bregel | Fundación Santander

Al borde de la treintena, la ayuda de Faro ha supuesto para ella un cambio de escala, literal y profesional. Su proyecto, Ludarquías, le ha permitido abordar una producción que no habría podido llevar a cabo en las condiciones con las que venía trabajando. La artista lo resume sin rodeos: «Para mí a nivel profesional es un antes y un después». Ha podido tomar por primera vez decisiones plásticas sin ver constreñida su ambición por cuestiones estrictamente económicas y, además, ha contado, cuando la duda más quemaba, con el consejo de la consagrada artista limeña Andrea Canepa. “Fue un regalazo”, cuenta. Fruto de toda esa meticulosa labor es el objeto pictórico titulado Escalera de Jacob. Uno de los imperdibles de la muestra.

Amaia Bregel y

Ludarquías Las ayudas supusieron la oportunidad para Amaia Bregel de llevar sus objetos pictóricos a unas dimensiones nunca antes experimentadas. En la imagen, parte del trabajo de montaje final de la instalación móvil. (Crédito: Jabata Films) Antes de llegar al objeto pictórico grande, Bregel trabaja con maquetas. La propia escala presenta problemas que ha de ir afrontando en el proceso plástico y que necesitan de ingenio. En este proyecto, contó con la asesoría de la artista peruana Andrea Canepa. (Crédito: Jabata Films) Su obra parte de lo pictórico y lo deriva hacia objetos donde el color y sus vibraciones son habitables. Amaia Bregel sigue considerándose, ante todo, pintora, aunque se maneje en muchos lenguajes y métodos. Esta pieza expuesta en Marisma, en Faro Santander, lleva por título ‘Escalera de Jacob’ y puede contemplarse así, como un cubo completo, o abierta. (Crédito: Jabata Films).

Casapalma y

La Suite de los Riconchos

Su álbum debut, Montañesas (2023), mezclaba canción tradicional con sonidos electrónicos; con JOTAS (2025) profundizan en la importancia de la pandereta y de una música que, sobre todo, estaba hecha para bailar. Y ahí, en todo ese universo —de los ritmos de percusión y los pasos de danza a la alfayatería y los trajes tradicionales— encuentran el germen del documental La Suite de los Riconchos que ahora estrenan en la Filmoteca de Cantabria y que esperan que tenga un gran recorrido por festivales y salas. Música y patrimonio, arte y sociología.

08:08 Casapalma | Fundación Santander

Las ayudas, además del crucial aporte económico para completar el rodaje que finalizaron en agosto (“¡Hacer una película es muy caro!”, exclama Atienza), le han procurado otra experiencia de esas difícilmente olvidables. Tocaron en la inauguración de Faro Santander, pudieron, gracias a la celebración de ese concierto, “subir a un escenario enorme el folclore de Cantabria para que lo viera toda la ciudad”.

Casapalma y

La Suite de los Riconchos Fotograma de ‘La Suite de los Riconchos’, con Yoel Molina (izquierda) a la guitarra e Irene Atienza a la pandereta. Molina se formó en Musikene (País Vasco) y en el Conservatorio Superior de Ámsterdam. Atienza, que vivió varios años en Brasil, regresó a su ciudad, Santander, tras la pandemia. Para la grabación del documental han llevado a cabo una importante investigación musicológica y etnográfica. El baile estaba en el centro del propósito de estas músicas, y esa misma relevancia tiene en la película. Los trajes tradicionales de montañesa suelen componerse de camisa de manca ancha, saya larga de colores con detalles de terciopelo y detalles como pañoleta o faltriquera. La película documental musical, que contó con la asesoría de grandes profesionales coreográficos y estudiosos de la etnografía de la región, se estrenó en la Filmoteca de Cantabria el 22 de octubre y está pendiente de su distribución en festivales y salas.

Para una formación que trabaja con el patrimonio inmaterial, con buena reputación ya bien ganada y una trayectoria importante en el campo de la música, compartir el proceso de su película con otros artistas con métodos y objetivos más abstractos, inmersos en proyectos de lenguajes variopintos, ha sido otro de los aprendizajes más enriquecedores. Cuenta Irene que, tras esta experiencia en común, Aurelio Vélez, vinculado al colectivo etnográfico Brañaflor y asesor fundamental del filme, tomó la determinación de presentar una propuesta sobre costura y cuadros de la colección permanente a la convocatoria que ahora se abre. “Él no se imaginaba que pudiera ser candidato a unas ayudas de arte, pero programas como este son una forma de abrir la mente”.

Salón de Belleza y

Una forma minúscula

Una conversación entre dos amigas, Manuela Gutiérrez y Cristina Somavilla, que eclosiona al abrirla al resto: así podría definirse qué es Salón de Belleza, el colectivo artístico que ambas fundaron y para el que ver películas, discutirlas y cuestionar ideas anquilosadas sobre el gusto o la cultura es la razón última de ser. Una forma minúscula parte de un hallazgo accidental: se toparon con el largometraje de Jesús Garay Manderley (1981) sobre la figura del artista y activista LGTBIQ+ José Pérez Ocaña y se obsesionaron con la peli: “Le pregunté por ella a mi padre”, cuenta Somavilla, “y me contó que él había conocido aquí a Ocaña”. Ahí comienza su investigación, ¿qué relatos de aquella Cantabria habían quedado fuera de la historia oficial? “Hemos abierto fisuras en lo que se supone que es Santander: hay mucho más”, explican.

06:42 Salón de Belleza | Fundación Santander

La ayuda les ha permitido poner en marcha un grupo de investigación intergeneracional en el que la memoria oral y el intercambio de pareceres ha ido hilando una conversación inacabada e inacabable (“¡seguiremos con estos encuentros y clubes en el futuro!”), siempre dispuesta a fluir fuera de cauce y al vaivén de las sorpresas, una investigación recogida parcialmente en textos y materiales de archivo disponibles en la muestra. “Nos gustaría ahora que la gente se acercara al espacio museístico, que Faro Santander se convirtiera en ese lugar de participación y encuentro que ha sido para nosotras”.

Salón de Belleza y

Una forma minúscula Sesión de trabajo del proyecto ‘Una forma minúscula’, en la que, a partir del visionado de una película y de ciertos materiales de archivo, se abre una conversación. Fotograma del drama dirigido por Jesús Garay ‘Manderley’, estrenado en 1981. La trama acompaña a tres jóvenes homosexuales que, en un mal momento personal, deciden pasar un verano juntos en Cantabria. Entre los protagonistas, destaca el ‘performer’ José Pérez Ocaña. Además de la película, las sesiones del proyecto utilizan material que reconstruye el contexto cultural en que surgió el filme para indagar más allá del relato oficial. En la imagen, el informe de calificación por edades de ‘Manderley’ (Archivo General de la Administración). Otro de esos materiales empleados fue el libro del artista e historiador Adolfo Fernández-Punsola ‘Nuestras vidas’, editado en 1996, que recoge fotografías y documentos de las décadas que retrata la película.

Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva y

Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas

Nunca sabe uno adónde le va a llevar abrir unas cajas viejas. Germán de la Riva recordaba vagamente el contenido de las que sus padres habían acumulado en la consulta. Psicólogos, fueron pioneros en materia de educación sexual en Santander en los años 80 y 90, con métodos traídos de su experiencia en Latinoamérica y EE UU. Dentro de las solapas de cartón, películas con imágenes artísticas pero explícitamente sexuales convivían con artículos y tesis científicas, un archivo que resultó idóneo para la labor investigadora que De la Riva lleva tiempo desarrollando junto a la también doctora en Bellas Artes y bailarina de danza contemporánea Itsaso Iribarren. Para ellos, toda su obra empieza en el cuerpo.

06:28 Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva | Fundación Santander

Memoria, sexualidad o cómo nos relacionamos físicamente son cuestiones que se pueden abordar apelando a los sentidos y la intuición. El arte tiene su propio camino hacia el conocimiento y, para Iribarren y De la Riva, mostrar ese proceso junto a la obra puede ser la mejor manera de hacer pedagogía: “El público entiende más o menos lo que ocurrió en las artes hasta las Vanguardias, pero existe un vacío, una desconexión, con las artes vivas y el presente de la creación”. Justo por ello, valoran y agradecen el compromiso de Faro Santander al generar un espacio que puede proveer al espectador de las piezas de puzle que le faltan.

Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva y

Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva, doctores en Bellas Artes y practicantes de danza contemporánea y artes vivas, inician todas sus investigaciones plásticas a partir del cuerpo: el movimiento, el tacto, los sentidos. Es otro de los caminos de conocimiento que permite el arte y que merece exploración. Para documentar el proceso del proyecto ‘Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas’ y generar un resultado expositivo, han empleado, entre otros métodos y lenguaje, la filmación analógica en 16 milímetros. Las artes vivas son una disciplina contemporánea en la que las fronteras genéricas se borran, donde conviven ‘performance’, danza, teatro físico, música, texto y artes visuales. De la Riva y Iribarren aplauden la apuesta de Faro Santander por proyectos así, donde mostrar el proceso creativo es casi más importante que alcanzar un resultado final.

Son cuatro historias, cuatro pulsos creativos distintos que, sin embargo, pintan un mapa justo de los derroteros del arte español de hoy, siempre vivo y siempre a punto del naufragio, sin tablas de salvación como la que ofrece esta convocatoria de Faro Santander. Hay oportunidades que de verdad cambian vidas, instituciones que verdaderamente tienen la capacidad de generar un tejido cultural que cosa todo el norte de España y enseñe el tapiz con lo mejor de nuestra creación fuera.

Para presentarse a la nueva convocatoria no hace falta tener respuestas, tan solo ganas de pelearse con el runrún que provocan esas preguntas que merece la pena hacerse.

World.title: Alquilé mi vivienda en 2019 y el contrato se prorrogó tres años más. ¿Podrá el casero echarme en 2027?
World.content:
Los lectores envían sus preguntas al consultorio de vivienda de EL PAÍS en colaboración con Legálitas

Pregunta. Alquilé mi vivienda en julio de 2019 por cinco años, hasta julio de 2024. El contrato se prorrogó tres años más, hasta julio de 2027, debido a que la propiedad no me avisó con cuatro meses de antelación de que quería rescindir el contrato. ¿Puede el propietario rescindir el contrato de alquiler en 2027 con los nuevos decretos de vivienda? Eduard.

Respuesta. Efectivamente, se encuentra disfrutando de la prórroga de tres años prevista en el artículo 10 de la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos (LAU). Al vencimiento del octavo año, el arrendador puede decidir no renovar el contrato, siempre que lo comunique con un preaviso mínimo de 30 días.

Si el arrendador realiza dicho preaviso en tiempo y forma, el artículo 10.3 de la LAU contempla dos supuestos en los que el arrendatario puede solicitar una prórroga:

Si el arrendatario acredita encontrarse en situación de vulnerabilidad económica , podrá solicitar una prórroga extraordinaria por un plazo máximo de un año, durante el cual se mantendrán los mismos términos y condiciones del contrato vigente. Para ello, deberá aportar un informe o certificado emitido en el último año por los servicios sociales municipales o autonómicos que acredite su situación de vulnerabilidad social y económica. Esta prórroga será obligatoria para el arrendador cuando tenga la condición de gran tenedor y siempre que las partes no hayan suscrito un nuevo contrato de arrendamiento.

Si la vivienda se encuentra en una zona declarada como mercado residencial tensionado y dicha declaración sigue vigente, el arrendatario podrá solicitar una prórroga extraordinaria por periodos anuales, hasta un máximo de tres años. Durante ese tiempo se mantendrán los términos y condiciones del contrato en vigor, salvo que las partes acuerden otras condiciones, se firme un nuevo contrato con las limitaciones de renta que correspondan o el arrendador necesite la vivienda para uso propio.

No obstante, si no concurre ninguna de las circunstancias anteriores, la disposición final quinta del Real Decreto-ley 29/2026, de 6 de octubre, permite solicitar una prórroga extraordinaria de hasta dos años adicionales, renovable año a año, manteniendo las mismas condiciones del contrato vigente. Esta medida resulta aplicable a los contratos cuyo vencimiento se produzca antes del 31 de diciembre de 2028.

Para acceder a esta prórroga, el arrendatario debe encontrarse al corriente de pago y haber mantenido esa situación durante los ocho meses anteriores. La solicitud deberá ser aceptada por el arrendador, salvo que exista un acuerdo distinto entre las partes, se formalice un nuevo contrato, se acepte un nuevo arrendamiento con una reducción de la renta de al menos un 5% o el arrendador necesite la vivienda para sí o para familiares de primer grado, siempre que acredite una necesidad real y lo comunique dentro del plazo legalmente establecido, aunque esta facultad no figure expresamente en el contrato.

Por último, debe tenerse en cuenta que esta prórroga extraordinaria de hasta dos años no es acumulable a la prórroga extraordinaria prevista en el artículo 10.3 de la LAU, que tiene carácter preferente.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.content:

The Dutch embassy in Cairo has closed to the public until further notice after nine days of protests outside the building, during which staff had to be evacuated, the embassy has announced on social media.

The demonstrators are demanding the release of Ahmed Nasser, deputy head of a pro-government Egyptian youth group, who was arrested in the Netherlands on October 10.

He was reportedly detained on suspicion of threatening Anas Habib, an Egyptian activist who lives in the Netherlands, and his pre-trial detention has been extended by 14 days, broadcaster NOS reported.

Habib drew international attention last summer when he filmed himself padlocking the gates of the Egyptian embassy in The Hague, in protest at the Egyptian government keeping the Rafah border crossing with Gaza closed.

His action sparked similar protests at Egyptian embassies in more than 16 countries, after which supporters of President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi began gathering outside embassies to “protect” them.

Days after Nasser’s arrest, Egyptian foreign minister Badr Abdelatty called his Dutch counterpart to demand his release and better protection for Egypt’s embassy in The Hague.

Foreign minister Tom Berendsen said on social media that the two had “discussed the need for progress on the security of our respective embassies and consular affairs.”

It is unclear exactly how Nasser is alleged to have threatened Habib.

World.title: Getting home safely: ADE festivals step up protection measures
World.content:
With the Amsterdam Dance Event (ADE), the world’s biggest electronic music event, underway, extra safety measures have been put in place by festival organisers and the city to make sure, Amsterdam says, that everyone feels “safe in the nightlife scene – free from any form of harassment, violence, discrimination, or (sexual) misconduct.”

To that end, there is a host of initiatives at various festival sites where techno lovers can recharge or get help getting home safely.

Bike buddies, hosts and Check-Ins

At the DGTL festival on NDSM island, cycling buddies will be on hand to help people get safely back and forth to the ferries. They will be working in pairs to ensure their own safety.

A Safe Check-In on NDSM wharf will be open all night for people who need physical help, feel unsafe at night or just need a breather. Phones can also be charged there.

At Awakenings in Halfweg, a Goodbye Host will be stationed at the exit, keeping a watchful eye on partygoers leaving solo. Hosts can help with route planning, and phones can also be charged here.

Both locations will also feature an Awareness Crew, trained teams identifiable by badges or vests that offer support to those feeling uncomfortable or unsafe.

Taking back the night

Some of the safety measures are not new. Last year, following the August murder of teenager Lisa while she cycled home alone and the resulting Take Back the Night campaign, the biking buddies programme was set up.

“We’ve been running social safety measures at our events since Covid, through our awareness teams and social safety hub, so this is something we’ve prioritized for a long time already,” Nikki Schuurs, who deals with Social Safety at DGTL, told Dutch News.

“Bike Buddies, however, was indeed introduced in response to the Take Back the Night campaign, following the murder of Lisa. Safety doesn’t stop at the dance floor.”

Visitors can find the Bike Buddy meeting point just outside the event. Group rides depart every 30 minutes between 21:00 and 07:00, on the hour and half-hour.

Safety concerns have again risen in the city following the violent death of 29-year-old Hajar, whose body was found in a suitcase in the Amstel River last week. She had last been seen cycling with a man near the RAI convention centre. He has since been arrested in connection with her death.

World.title: Inburgering with Dutch News: the great cycle path squeeze
World.content:
You can’t have failed to notice that Dutch cycle paths are no longer the preserve of old-fashioned cyclists. E-bikes, fatbikes, scooters, snorfietsen, speed pedelecs, disabled vehicles – a seemingly never-ending stream of other road users have moved in. But what exactly are the rules and regulations?

Lesson 64: what is allowed on the cycle path?

Fatbike

The fatbike, with its characteristic thick tyres and frequently thick riders, has become wildly popular. It’s not surprising because at the moment, riders do not need a helmet, driving licence, or third-party liability insurance. The fatbike is officially an e-bike, and therefore there is no age limit, but measures are afoot to make helmet-wearing compulsory for riders up to the age of 18.

Fatbikes are allowed to travel at up to 25 kph. However, many are doctored to go faster – as you will notice when you see them whizzing past cars that keep to the 30 kph limit, mandatory for cars in some Dutch cities.

Electric bike

The electric non-fat bike, so to speak, is literally overtaking the person-powered bike, and that is partly due to its popularity among older riders – who are also well represented in the annual traffic death toll. The same rules of the road as apply to fatbikes apply to ordinary e-bikes – none. You will, however, see more and more elderly riders with a helmet.

Electric cargo bike

The cargo bike, or moedermobiel, deserves a separate mention because of the riders’ mistaken opinion that everyone has to make way for this space-hogging vehicle because it carries cute little toddlers. A good place to spot cargo bikes is outside primary schools at 3pm, when they cause a veritable jam of their own.

Speed pedelec

Speed pedelecs are electric bikes as well, but unlike normal electric bikes, they can legally reach speeds of up to 45 kph. This makes them motorcycles in the eyes of the law, with the rules that then apply, such as mandatory helmet-wearing, a driving licence and insurance. Speed pedelecs can travel on cycle paths, but only at a maximum of 25 kph.

Snorfiets, or moped

No pedalling is needed for this motorised bike or moped, which has a maximum speed limit of 25 kph and is allowed on cycle paths. Although snorfietsen have the same speed limit as electric bikes, they are technically considered to be motorcycles, and riders need a helmet, a driving licence and insurance.

The introduction of helmets for all types of mopeds several years ago led to the downfall of the snorfiets – after all, if you need a helmet, why not drive a proper motorbike – or a fatbike?

Scootmobiel

The motorised wheelchair or scootmobiel is possibly the most dangerous vehicle on the cycle path. According to statistics agency CBS, the traffic death rate among mobility scooter riders is over six times that of motorbike riders and over 20 times that of cyclists.

Users don’t need to pass any tests or learn the rules of the road, and they can go pretty much wherever they like – shopping centre, pavement, cycle path, ordinary road – just not the motorway.

The Canta

The Canta looks like a brommobiel – a small electric vehicle with four wheels – but because it is considered a mobility aid for people with a disability, it is treated in the same way as a scootmobiel.

The Canta is not supposed to go faster than 30 kph on the cycle path and 45 kph on the road, but is allowed to mount the pavement and annoy pedestrians at 6 kph. It can also park anywhere and does not need a number plate.

The minimum age is 16, and you’ll need to take out insurance, but you don’t need a driving licence. The Canta became popular with youngsters who could not be bothered to cycle and has since spawned a surge in far hipper micro cars.

Micro cars

The Birò and its ilk are small, fashionable and, according to many, extremely annoying electric vehicles which are banned from cycle paths but whose drivers use them anyway – particularly as a sneaky escape when faced with a traffic jam.

Popular with estate agents and PR people, micro cars have a maximum speed of 45 kph. If you want one, you will need a brommobiel driving licence and must be 16 or over.

Electric scooter

The step, or scooter, used to be a children’s plaything, but since the invention of the electric version, they have been taking over cities throughout Europe. Steps which have been officially approved have been allowed on Dutch cycle paths since July 1 this year. In Dutch terminology they are known as “light electric vehicles”.

The step has a maximum speed of 25 kph, and riders have to be 16 or over. You will need third-party liability insurance, and the base must have a number plate which is clearly visible.

The e-step is predicted to rival the fatbike in popularity and ability to provoke cycle-path rage – as long as helmets are not compulsory.

World.title: Amsterdam exploring single-use packaging ban
World.content:
Amsterdam is considering banning single-use packaging, including coffee cups, fast-food containers and other single-use plastics that it says make up 30% of the city’s litter.

“Litter is a persistent problem; it is a symptom of a ‘throwaway society’ that pollutes our beautiful city and costs millions every year,” said Amsterdam executive Lian Heinhuis, who is responsible for waste and sanitation, in a statement.

“Yet the solution is within reach: putting an end to the throwaway culture.”

To that end, the city has commissioned a study into what it can legally do to tackle the problem. According to CircuLaw, which provides legal information on circular transitions, such a ban could be implemented, but only after less restrictive measures have proven not to work.

A ban also works best alongside other measures, such as a reliable supply of reusable packaging and a well-established return system.

The city says it will work with business owners and residents and also look at how other cities are managing the problem, including Copenhagen and Lisbon, the latter of which has already implemented a single-use packaging ban.

“Single-use packaging is a major problem,” the city said. “The plastics used in these items take hundreds of years to decompose – if they ever do at all. They pollute the soil and groundwater for a very long time, despite being used for an average of only about seven minutes.”

World.title: Student union furious as minister says interest cap unaffordable
World.content:
Despite a coalition promise to cap student loan interest rates at 2.5%, education minister Rianne Letschert has told parliament that the government can no longer afford to stick to its pledge.

The minister said that capping the interest rate at 2.5% is risky and expensive, and that the €40 million annual budget the coalition had set aside to cover the cap is only a quarter of what it would actually cost – €160 million – and could lead to other cuts in the education budget.

“I understand the concerns of current and former students regarding the rise in interest rates on student debt, driven by global instability and an increase in long-term interest rates,” Letschert said in a statement on Thursday.

“Unfortunately, I must conclude that it is not possible to implement a 2.5% interest rate cap with the €40 million per year that has been set aside. I find this very disappointing.”

Geopolitical costs

Since the coalition agreement was first presented at the end of January, the global landscape has significantly shifted due to geopolitical tensions and financial uncertainty. Long-term interest rates – to which student loan rates are linked – have risen from 2.7% to 3.3% and could climb higher.

“Recent shocks in the financial markets highlight just how unpredictable – and potentially financially risky – this interest rate policy is,” the ministry said.

But students aren’t buying it. “This effectively sends students out into the world burdened by an incredibly heavy backpack of debt,” LSVB, the national student union, told news service ANP. “The only certainty this cabinet offers students is the assurance that interest rates will rise even further in the coming years.”

Student union ISO added that once again, “students are the victims of empty promises.”

Letschert will discuss the issue with parliament later this month.

World.title: Cyber security centre warns PHP hacking situation could worsen
World.content:
The Netherlands’ National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is investigating the first signs of successful hacks on websites following the exposure of critical vulnerabilities on the web, and says the situation could “rapidly worsen”.

A spokesperson told the Volkskrant on Thursday that the signals came from the NCSC’s international network, and that there was no sign yet of abuse involving Dutch websites. The centre is still checking whether the reports are accurate.

Cybersecurity researchers, working with the help of AI, found that PHP, the programming language on which a majority of the web is built, had at least two serious vulnerabilities in its code.

Details of the weaknesses were leaked online on Monday, and the PHP developers announced they would issue an upgrade by Wednesday afternoon.

Hacking attempts began even before the leak, with Amazon reporting an attack attempt on October 17. US internet security firm Cloudflare said it saw hacking attempts run from thousands before the upgrade to millions afterwards.

Initially, the NCSC said that there were no signs of active hacks and the PHP developers said there were no indications of breaches.

Large amounts of government, healthcare and news sites were forced to go dark temporarily while awaiting the upgrade, including Dutch News.

The Netherlands was fast to act, closing a large amount of its sites and issuing warnings early on Wednesday, after which governments in Belgium, Germany, France and Finland did the same. The issue is now a global concern.

Dutch privacy watchdog AP said on Thursday it had not yet received any reports of data breaches linked to the vulnerabilities.

World.title: Weather warnings as storm Austen approaches Netherlands
World.content:
The weather office KNMI has issued code yellow warnings for Limburg, Zeeland and South Holland on Friday evening as storm Austen approaches, with gusts of at least 75 kilometres per hour expected.

The southwest and the hills of Limburg will be hit by the wind first, with the rest of the country following in the evening and overnight.

Saturday is expected to bring fewer showers, some sun and a calmer wind, before heavy rain and stronger gusts return in the evening. Very severe wind is possible along the coast.

On Sunday the wind will remain strong throughout the country, particularly in the north, where there will also be showers. The south will get more sun, but temperatures will not rise above 13° over the weekend.

Katarzyna Pełczyńska-Nałęcz, the leader of a junior party in Poland’s ruling coalition, has announced that her resignation from the government and the leadership of her party, the centrist Poland 2050 (Polska 2050), in protest over a parliamentary vote on Thursday. Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) is set to remain in the government, thereby maintaining Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s parliamentary majority. However, the dispute has highlighted tensions within the ruling coalition just a year ahead of parliamentary elections at which it will seek another term. Dwukadencyjność samorządów została utrzymana. Tak zdecydował dziś Sejm. Wygraliśmy! Zmiana, której chce 75% Polaków dojdzie do skutku! Stało się to jednak pomimo głosów K15X. Koalicja, w tym niestety znaczna część posłów Polski 2050, stanęła przeciw ludziom, a za politykierskimi… — Katarzyna Pełczyńska (@Kpelczynska) October 22, 2026 Pełczyńska-Nałęcz, who serves as minister for funds and regional policy, made her decision in the wake of an unusual voting result in the Sejm, the more powerful lower house of parliament, on Thursday. Another junior partner in the ruling coalition, the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), had proposed a bill abolishing two-term limits for mayors. Those limits had been introduced in 2018 with the aim of reducing corruption and cronyism by preventing local officials from becoming entrenched in power. However, PSL, which has a strong presence in local politics, argues that the limits prevent effective, popular mayors from being re-elected, thereby denying voters the right to decide who they want to represent them. Although the government has a majority in the Sejm, the bill was narrowly defeated, with 213 votes in favour and 215 against, after 15 MPs from the ruling coalition joined with the right-wing opposition in voting against it. Pełczyńska-Nałęcz herself is not a member of parliament, so did not vote. Her party was split, with six MPs voting for the bill, three against, three abstaining, and three not voting at all. Aftewards, Pełczyńska-Nałęcz made clear that she opposed the bill and celebrated the fact that it was blocked. She also announced her resignation from the government and the leadership of her party. “The coalition, unfortunately including a significant portion of MPs from Poland 2050, stood against the people and in favour of backroom political deals,” she wrote. “I am leaving Donald Tusk’s government because values are more important to me than positions.” “I am leaving the party in the hands of its founder, who stepped away but then returned,” she added, referring to Poland 2050’s founder, Szymon Hołownia. “I hope that he remembers what values he came to power in the name of.” Pełczyńska-Nałęcz’s decision follows a year of turmoil for Poland 2050. In September 2025, Hołownia, who had led the party since founding it in 2021, announced that he was stepping down. However, a first attempt to choose a new leader was invalidated in January after technical problems with voting. Hołownia then hinted that he may reverse course and seek to continue leading the party, though in the end that did not happen. In February, Pełczyńska-Nałęcz was chosen as the new leader. That prompted her rival candidate, Paulina Hennig-Kloska, to quit the party, taking half of its MPs with her. They formed a new group called Centrum (Centre). Both Poland 2050 and Centrum remain in the ruling coalition. However, Pełczyńska-Nałęcz has had an uneasy relationship with Tusk. Around half the MPs from Poland 2050, a junior member of Poland’s ruling coalition, have split from the party and formed a new parliamentary caucus. They expressed dissatisfaction with the actions of the party's recently elected new leader, @Kpelczynska https://t.co/IqU4vE1EEe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 18, 2026 On Friday, Tusk, who is on a state visit to India, sarcastically responded to Pełczyńska-Nałęcz’s resignation by saying, “I thought she’d at least call before she left”. He admitted that “cooperation [with her] has not been the easiest for a long time”. The prime minister, however, added that he “does not think [her resignation] will have any impact on the future work of the coalition…My intuition tells me that this is her individual decision”. Hołownia, who currently serves as head of Poland 2050’s parliamentary caucus, confirmed at a press conference on Friday alongside fellow MPs that the party intends to remain in Tusk’s coalition. But he also warned that, without Poland 2050, the government would not have a parliamentary majority. W @PL_2050 dowiedzieliśmy się o decyzji @Kpelczynska z mediów. Zaskakująca rezygnacja przewodniczącej z zaufania wyborców i odpowiedzialności powierzonej jej w bardzo trudnym momencie przez ludzi (w tym mnie) zaledwie po niespełna 1/3 kadencji – dla każdej organizacji byłaby… — Szymon Hołownia (@szymon_holownia) October 22, 2026 The episode highlights the tensions within the ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right and contains parties that disagree on a number of issues. It also points to the pressure smaller coalition partners are feeling ahead of next autumn’s parliamentary elections. Only parties that win at least 5% of the vote nationally can enter parliament. But Poland 2050 has been polling at around 1% and PSL is on 3%. In the 2023 election, Poland 2050 and PSL in fact stood together as an alliance called the Third Way (Trzecia Droga), helping ensure that the two parties won enough votes to enter parliament. However, in 2025, they split from one another and confirmed that they would not stand together again. PSL and Poland 2050, the two parties that make up the Third Way alliance, have confirmed that they are splitting and will stand separately at the next elections. They will, however, remain part of @donaldtusk's ruling coalition https://t.co/NduEJY25eE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 18, 2025 The fact that the bill to end two-term limits for mayors was defeated has also caused tension between PSL and its coalition partners. In the wake of yesterday’s vote, PSL immediately announced that it would push for the introduction of two-term limits for members of parliament, arguing that the same rules should apply to national and local elected representatives. The right-wing opposition has long hoped that it could tempt PSL, the most conservative element of Tusk’s coalition, to quit the government. A recent report even claimed that US President Donald Trump had, at the behest of Poland’s opposition, suggested to PSL’s leader that he leave Tusk. World.title: Protesters return to Poland’s streets demanding liberalisation of abortion law
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Protests took place in towns and cities around Poland on Thursday evening, demanding that the government fulfil its promise to liberalise the country’s strict abortion laws. However, the demonstrations, which took place on the sixth anniversary of the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) ruling that introduced a near-total abortion ban, were nowhere near the scale of the massive protests that emerged back in 2020. Było deszczowo, ale nie brakowało ludzi i emocji. Rzeszów pokazał czerwoną kartkę za aborcję rządzącej koalicji. pic.twitter.com/oJo8BiWXxS — Paweł Preneta (@pawelpreneta) October 22, 2026 In Warsaw, a few hundred people gathered in the rain outside parliament, reported broadcaster RMF. Many held up red cards, a symbol used by the protesters to warn the government that it could be thrown out of power at next year’s parliamentary elections. When Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, came to power in December 2023, it pledged to liberalise the abortion laws after eight years of rule by the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party. In particular, it wanted to reverse the 2020 TK ruling, which outlawed abortions in cases where a severe defect is diagnosed in the foetus. That means abortions can now only take place in two cases: where the pregnancy results from a crime (such as rape or incest) or if it threatens the mother’s life or health. However, in the almost three years since, the government has failed to introduce any new legislation on abortion. One effort to do so in 2024 collapsed amid disagreements between more conservative and liberal elements of Tusk’s coalition. Finally, earlier this week, the Sejm, the more powerful lower house of parliament, approved two abortion bills: one that would reverse the 2020 TK ruling; the other that would decriminalise providing help to women in obtaining unlawful abortions. However, those measures do not go far enough for many of those attending Tuesday’s protests, who are seeking abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy. In any case, both bills approved by the Sejm are likely to be blocked by President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of government bills. Nawrocki has made his opposition to abortion clear. Parliament has approved two bills that would liberalise Poland's abortion laws One would reverse the 2020 constitutional court ruling that introduced a near-total ban on abortion; the other would decriminalise helping women in obtaining unlawful abortions https://t.co/nVj8SQVIsv — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 21, 2026 In Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, around 1,000 people attended Thursday’s protest, according to police estimates cited by the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. Among the placards and banners was one showing Tusk with an extended, Pinocchio-style nose. “It’s sad that we have to engage in this fight again,” said one of the organisers. “For so long, they ignored us, only coming when they needed votes. Now let’s show that we can’t be ignored.” In Katowice, around 300 people gathered, according to the Polish Press Agency (PAP). In Poznań, around 400 or so protesters marched to the local headquarters of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, where they placed a symbolic red card and waved banners saying “You deceived Poland”. Czerwona kartka za aborcje. W #Lodz w proteście w strugach deszczu protestuje kilkadziesiąt osób @RadioZET_NEWS pic.twitter.com/okU7QjnhFw — Mateusz Szkudlarek (@m_szkudlarek) October 22, 2026 The 2020 TK abortion ruling triggered the largest protests seen in Poland since the communist era, with hundreds of thousands of people taking to the streets. That anger is seen as having played a major role in PiS losing power to Tusk’s coalition in 2023. Opinion polls consistently show that most Poles want the abortion law to be liberalised, though there remain divisions over whether there should be a return to the pre-2021 status quo or a move even further, to introduce abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy. In autumn 2027, parliamentary elections will take place, deciding who governs Poland for the next four years. Opinion polls currently show a fairly even split in support between Tusk’s coalition and the right-wing opposition. After the shooting, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that “everything points to this being a political assassination”. On 18 June, the Polish authorities announced they had captured Elnur A. in a hostel near Warsaw. The following day, he was charged with the murder of Kuzovkov. He has remained in custody since then. Police have detained a man suspected of carrying out the murder of Russian dissident Semyon Skrepetsky, who was shot dead near his home in Poland this week. "Everything points to this being a political assassination," says Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/z37sBBxgJn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 18, 2026 On Thursday, Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office revealed that Makhmud A. had been detained on 19 October by the Internal Security Agency (ABW) in a car park along the A2 motorway. The ABW itself confirmed that it detained the suspect after he flew to Poland from Georgia on 18 October. He had been travelling with two other Georgians, who will now be expelled from Poland and handed a 10-year re-entry ban. Makhmud A. was subsequently charged with aiding and abetting the killing of Kuzovkov by “undertaking a number of actions in the period from 1 to 11 June 2026 that made it easier for Elnur A. to commit the murder”. He is additionally charged with illegal possession of firearms and ammunition. Makhmud A. is accused of providing the perpetrator with a weapon, means of transportation and a mobile phone with an application enabling monitoring of the victim’s vehicle, a spokeswoman for the district court in Lublin told broadcaster TVN. The court has approved a period of three months’ detention for Makhmud A., with prosecutors saying that they fear he could otherwise “flee, go into hiding, or unlawfully obstruct proceedings”. Under Polish law, someone found guilty of aiding and abetting a crime can face the same punishment as the person who committed the crime itself, meaning that both suspects face potential prison sentences of between 10 years and life if found guilty. They have pleaded not guilty. A Russian man has been shot dead in Poland, with reports indicating that he was an artist whose work ridiculed Putin and that his killing appeared to be an “execution”. However, the authorities have not yet officially identified the victim or any suspects https://t.co/Zd2u7IE0A0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 15, 2026 The Polish authorities have not yet revealed who they believe was ultimately behind the murder of Kuzovkov. However, in June, Tusk said that, if Russia’s involvement was confirmed, it would be a case of “state terrorism”. In recent years, Poland has become a primary target for Russia’s campaign of so-called “hybrid warfare”, which has involved acts of sabotage, disinformation, cyberattacks, and airspace violations. Most known on-the-ground activity has been carried out not by Russian operatives themselves, but by so-called “disposable agents” hired through messaging service Telegram and paid in cryptocurrency. In some cases, Russia has used existing criminal networks to carry out such tasks. Four men – three Ukrainians and a Belarusian – have gone on trial in Warsaw accused of being part of a criminal group that carried out a series of arson attacks in Poland and Lithuania on behalf of Russia https://t.co/i4czRb9DYZ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 12, 2026 Earlier this month, a trial began in Warsaw of four men – three Ukrainians and one Belarusian – accused of being part of a criminal group that carried out a series of arson attacks in Poland and Lithuania on Russian orders. Shortly afterwards, Germany detained two Turkish men at the request of Poland, which believes they were responsible for the recent arson attack on a satellite internet ground station in Poland used by Starlink. Poland believes that incident was also carried out on behalf of Russia. Last year, the interior ministry claimed that Poland is facing a growing wave of “imported crime”, committed in particular by immigrants from Georgia and other former Soviet states. World.title: Poland and India aim to double trade by 2030 as PMs meet in New Delhi
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The prime ministers of Poland and India have, after a meeting in New Delhi, outlined aims to double bilateral trade by 2030 and expand cooperation in mining, shipbuilding, energy, space and defence technologies. Donald Tusk’s visit, the first by a Polish prime minister to India in 16 years, follows the upgrading of bilateral ties between the two countries to a strategic partnership during Narendra Modi’s trip to Poland two years ago, which was the first by an Indian prime minister in almost five decades. During a joint press conference with Tusk on Thursday, Modi said that his Warsaw visit had acted as a catalyst for the Polish-Indian relationship to “gain speed over the last two years”. Tusk added that the two leaders had now reviewed the results of their cooperation so far and outlined priorities for the coming years. They discussed, among other things, ways to deepen economic, investment and technological ties between the two fast-growing economies. Poland’s GDP is set to grow by 3.5% this year, the second-fastest rate in the European Union, while India will see economic growth of 7%. Poland’s economy is also on the verge of becoming the 20th largest in the world, with the country hoping to join the G20. “The economic strength of both countries offers a wealth of opportunities for strategic partnership,” Modi said. Tusk, meanwhile, underlined that “Poland and India are countries that have much in common and nothing that divides them…[with] no conflicting interests or historical grievances.” Poland hopes that the boost to bilateral trade will come from an EU-India trade deal expected to be signed in December. The agreement is designed to eliminate or reduce tariffs on goods accounting for 96.6% of the value of EU exports to the Indian market. Tusk said Poland wanted to capitalise on the opportunities created by the deal, with the ambition of becoming “India’s gateway to Europe”. Modi expressed confidence that Poland’s and India’s “shared goal” of doubling bilateral trade by 2030 “will certainly be achieved”. “Today, trade between Poland and India totals just over $6 billion,” said Poland’s finance minister Andrzej Domański, who joined Tusk on the trip to India. “We want this trade to grow, and the conditions for that are very favourable.” However, “it is no secret that we have a significant trade deficit with India”, Domański added. Last year, Poland exported goods worth €1.4 billion to India, with machinery, mineral products and metals the largest categories. Meanwhile, it imported €4.3 billion, in particular textiles, machinery and metals. The United States wants Poland to become a full member of the G20 "as soon as possible". "Poland’s economic growth, combined with its growing leadership position in the international arena, make it an ideal participant," says the @StateDept https://t.co/OjpWly4FTw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 12, 2026 According to the Polish prime minister’s office, the EU-India agreement could also help increase Polish investment in India, particularly in advanced manufacturing, food processing, biotechnology and mobility. To help facilitate such investments, Tusk travelled with almost 100 Polish business representatives, hoping the visit will help them to enter the large and rapidly growing Indian market. His office described the delegation as the largest of its kind in the history of Polish-Indian relations. Modi said he was “particularly happy” with Tusk’s decision to bring a business delegation and announced plans to strengthen links between startups in both countries, including through technology hackathons for young people. The countries plan to expand cooperation in critical minerals, raw materials and coal gasification, a process that converts coal into gas for energy and industrial use. Shipbuilding, defence, space and advanced technologies are also among the priority sectors. Indians are now the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, followed by Colombians, according to new data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Ukrainians remain by far the largest immigrant group, followed by Belarusians https://t.co/hNiOqmeUfX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2026 The leaders also highlighted historical ties and people-to-people exchanges as a foundation for closer relations. Modi recalled the role of Indian Maharaja Jam Saheb Digvijaysinhji Ranjitsinhji, known in Poland as the “Good Maharaja”, who provided shelter and care to around 1,000 Polish children evacuated from the Soviet Union during the Second World War. “In 2022, Poland helped our Indian students, demonstrating that same spirit of humanity,” added Modi, referring to the support Poland provided to Indian students escaping from Ukraine following Russia’s full-scale invasion. Modi said he hoped that the ongoing Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme, which recently took place for the second time, will “introduce the next generation to this Polish-Indian friendship”. The strengthening of bilateral relations has also come amid a rapid rise in Indian migration to Poland in recent years. This year Indians became the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, numbering around 25,500, up almost 5% in a year.
