World.title: Ukraine says two soldiers died after arrested girl sent Russian poison
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian police said Friday they had detained a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia’s security services to poison Ukrainian soldiers and that two had died.

Ukraine and Russia have throughout their war since 2022 accused each other of recruiting minors for sabotage acts including poisoning.

The girl, who was not named, is suspected of having packaged deadly drugs and sending them to Ukrainian soldiers she contacted by Telegram, said a police statement.

She was arrested by police in Zhytomyr, west of Kyiv, after allegedly following instructions from a Russian handler in exchange for at least 5,000 hryvnias ($111), they said.

After receiving packages with “free drugs”, the soldiers were “instructed to take them on camera”, the statement said.

“The recipients did not know that the capsules contained a lethal dose of methadone,” it said, adding that “two soldiers died from poisoning in the Zhytomyr region.”

Police said they had identified other recipients of the packages, which “prevented four more murders” across the country.

“The young woman was notified that she is suspected of aiding and abetting the premeditated murder of two people as part of a prior conspiracy,” the police statement said.

She was also suspected of “shipping drugs and psychotropic substances for the purpose of distribution”, it said, adding that she faced up to 15 years in jail if found guilty.

Police cautioned that Russia aims “to kill our people and destabilise the situation within the country”.

“Do not accept medication or other substances, as well as food or drinks of dubious origin, from people you do not know well,” police cautioned.

Since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Ukrainian authorities say they have opened thousands of investigations into collaboration with the enemy, and frequently arrest individuals accused of working for Moscow.

In 2023, Ukraine accused Russia of poisoning the wife of Kyrylo Budanov, who was then head of Ukraine’s military intelligence and is now a presidential advisor.

World.title: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts
World.content:
Stockholm – Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.

The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide.

Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year.

It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.

Shortly after 0800 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down almost 30 percent.

“We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change,” chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, “through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees”.

The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.

In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

“We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges,” Samuelsson said.

“However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient.”

Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.

The company said in September that Samuelsson would resign when his contract ends, with Skoda Auto CEO Klaus Zellmer set to replace him “no later” than October next year.

World.title: France braces for new protests as Macron seeks to restore order
World.content:
Paris – France was on Friday bracing for a weekend of new protests after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, as President Emmanuel Macron sought to reclaim the initiative and restore order.

Macron, who on Thursday announced that only union demonstrations would be authorised this weekend, was to hold a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and also meet security forces.

He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked a movement that has broadened nationwide into a show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city.

Macron is due to announce “additional decisions” after hosting the meeting of his defence council, on top of the limited curfews already announced, his office said.

At the meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP.

Pierre Sourzat, who heads the organisation Les Lyceens (The High School Students), was sceptical: “He’ll listen to us, pretend he’s understood us, and then nothing will come of it.”

Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday.

In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.

On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend.

– ‘Police have a responsibility’ –

Demonstrations in Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast have been banned at the weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares.

Marseille authorities however reversed a decision to halt all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short.

Some 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week.

“In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons.

The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors.

A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections.

It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 percent of the vote.

World.title: Kering shares tumble as Gucci fails to reassure investors
World.content:
Paris – Kering shares were down more than 10 percent in Paris Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand.

At 0730 GMT, Kering shares were down 10.8 percent at 190.40 euros, their lowest since June 2025. The market’s CAC40 index was down 0.3 percent.

Kering reported late Thursday that third-quarter sales were flat at 3.34 billion euros ($3.75 billion).

Sales at Gucci, by far the group’s largest single brand, fell by four percent to 1.29 billion euros, worse than the three-percent decline registered in the second quarter.

“Gucci has not shown convincing signs of stabilisation,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note.

Italy-based Gucci is key to Kering’s fortunes, but has been in freefall since 2023 as the brand lost its luxury cachet.

World.title: West Bank attack wounds 5 as Israel PM cancels events
World.content:
Hebron – An attack in the occupied West Bank wounded at least five Israelis on Friday and touched off a shootout that ended with two suspected Palestinian assailants dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel political events days ahead of elections.

An AFP journalist who witnessed the firefight saw two Palestinian men in casual attire and armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle exchanging fire with Israeli forces at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city of Hebron.

The journalist reported that Israeli forces eventually shot and killed the attackers, their two lifeless bodies on the ground next to a petrol station as Israeli troops patrolled in all directions.

The Israeli military said soldiers had rushed to the Judea Junction area, also known as the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint, after the early-morning shooting attack.

“IDF (Israel Defense Forces) soldiers eliminated two terrorists and continue searches in the area,” it said in a statement.

The initial shooting wounded five people, two of whom were in critical condition, said Magen David Adom, Israel’s emergency medical rescue service.

The Magen David Adom said one of the victims was a man in his 20s in “very serious condition” with gunshot wounds.

Netanyahu, running for a new term in elections on Tuesday, called for all political meetings to be cancelled Friday due to the attack.

Israeli National Security Minister and far-right firebrand Itamar Ben Gvir, who has been rising in the polls, called for the Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority to be dismantled because of the attack.

“The Palestinian Authority must be dismantled and demilitarized, and its terror infrastructure wiped out completely,” he said in a statement.

No evidence suggests that the Palestinian Authority, the Palestinian government in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, was connected to Friday’s attack.

Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief who is Netanyahu’s top rival in the election, praised the response by troops.

“Like all Israelis, I pray for the complete and quick recovery of the injured,” he said.

The incident comes as tensions soar in the West Bank, including over attacks by extremist Israeli settlers against Palestinian olive harvesters, and days ahead of Israeli elections.

According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces or settlers have killed 1,113 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023.

Israeli figures show at least 49 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period.

World.title: South Korea proposes holding border talks with North
World.content:
Seoul – South Korea proposed on Friday military talks with North Korea to “mutually confirm the precise location” of their border and discuss restoring communication channels, after an explosion in the DMZ further strained relations.

Tensions between the two Koreas have soared since the South last month blamed the blast inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) separating the countries on landmines laid by the North, an accusation it has fiercely rejected.

The South Korean defence ministry “formally proposes holding military talks with North Korea to mutually confirm the precise location of the land Military Demarcation Line (MDL) and discuss ways to restore military communication lines and prevent accidental clashes in border areas,” Kim Hong-cheol, deputy defense minister for policy, told reporters Friday.

The proposal comes just days after Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, announced that Pyongyang had moved new troop units into “firing position” along the border.

Seoul’s defence ministry said Friday it was difficult to predict “what further incidents could occur if this situation is allowed to continue unaddressed”.

The ministry said that “three-way talks involving the United Nations Command would also be possible”.

“Specific dates and locations could be discussed through Panmunjom,” said Kim, referencing the symbolic truce village where troops from both Koreas stand face-to-face.

He added they hoped for “a positive response from North Korea”.

The South Korean defence ministry also noted that talks proposed last year with the North did not get a response from Pyongyang.

– Grave situation –

Seoul’s military on Tuesday accused Pyongyang of attempting to shift the blame for escalating military tensions, while confirming the use of loudspeakers and warning shots as “legitimate defensive measures to prevent North Korean troops from crossing the MDL and to drive back troops that have crossed it”.

Jin Yong-sung, chairman of South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff, also ordered the military to “respond with firm resolve” should North Korea use Seoul’s actions as a pretext for aggressive action.

Pyongyang has rejected claims it was behind the explosion that injured three South Korean soldiers inside the DMZ and mockingly dismissed calls for an apology.

The country on Monday called the situation along the border “grave”, saying it was considering deploying additional “tactical strike means” to the area.

On Thursday, Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said the North would place loudspeakers on standby along the border “within days” and had put unspecified “new counter means” on alert.

South Korea’s foreign ministry also said Thursday it planned to send a letter to the president of the UN Security Council later in the day over the landmine incident, which it called a “clear violation of the armistice agreement”.

President Lee Jae Myung has called for the North to return to dialogue, an overture Kim Yo Jong later slammed as “the climax of the farce”.

World.title: Asian football endorses Infantino re-election as FIFA president
World.content:
Tokyo – The head of the Asian Football Confederation on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president following fierce criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan.

The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the AFC when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing.

The AFC in August had joined UEFA (Europe) and CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino has faced calls to quit and has lost the support of many associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term.

“I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as FIFA president,” said Sheikh Salman, in a significant boost to Infantino’s prospects.

“I think you’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent.

“I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear.”

Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extraordinary Congress and Infantino: “Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past.

“But let’s not relate the two things together. We need to move forward… football is strongest when we work together.”

Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March.

The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.

No heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against him so far, despite outspoken condemnation especially from Europe.

Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino over controversies including his relationship with US President Donald Trump.

World.title: Rooney calls United squad ‘selfish babies’ after Fernandes criticism
World.content:
Manchester – Manchester United great Wayne Rooney has labelled the current squad “babies” and “selfish” after a humiliating Champions League capitulation and post-match criticism by Bruno Fernandes of manager Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s men are 13th in the Premier League ahead of Sunday’s visit by Bournemouth and could drop into the bottom three if results go against them this weekend.

With the club beset by infighting and off to their worst domestic league start for decades, Carrick was left clinging to his job after the 4-1 defeat at Como on Wednesday.

Deepening the sense of crisis, the captain Fernandes afterwards took aim at his manager’s tactics, saying United had to be more “brave”.

Defender Lisandro Martinez last week criticised the club’s board for not investing enough in the transfer market.

Rooney, United’s all-time leading goalscorer, said he was in “shock” and “disbelief” at the Como display.

A friend and ex-teammate of Carrick, former striker Rooney pointed the finger at the players.

“When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart,” Rooney told The United Stand podcast on Thursday.

“That was the start. We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players because these players, they don’t want to take responsibility.

“You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players.”

He added: “These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

“If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.”

World.title: After Operation Sindoor friction, Delhi & Baku reset ties with EAM Jaishankar's visit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing efforts by both India and Azerbaijan for a reset in ties, EAM S Jaishankar and his counterpart Jeyhun Bayramov agreed to expand cooperation in energy, trade, investment and connectivity in a âvery productiveâ meeting in Baku.

Jaishankarâs visit to Azerbaijan was the first by an Indian foreign minister in eight years and built upon the diplomatic goodwill created by PM Modiâs meeting with Azerbaijan President Ilham Aliyev on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek last month.

Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while, mainly Azerbaijanâs ties with Pakistan â as evident from its support for Islamabad after Op Sindoor last year â and Indiaâs defence ties with Armenia.

While Bayramov spoke about taking the relationship to a higher level, setting aside past differences, Jaishankar underlined the significance of trade and energy cooperation. Terrorism was also among the issues discussed. âWe spoke about economic cooperation, including trade, investment and energy, which are central to our bilateral ties... We believe there is very good scope for further enhancement of bilateral trade and investment.

World.title: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map
World.content:
That atmospheric conditions regulate pollution levels was always known. (File photo)

Study traces how an El NiÃ±o changed the pollution map

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The winter of 2022-23 was remarkably clean in north India with PM2.5 levels down by up to 30% from the average of the previous three years, while peninsular India was considerably dirtier, with average PM2.5 levels in Mumbai spiking by 45%. The next winter (2023-24), the pattern dramatically reversed: PM2.5 spiralled in the North, while falling sharply in peninsular India.What changed within a span of a year? The big difference, as per a new study, was that 2022-23 was a La NiÃ±a year, while El NiÃ±o prevailed in the subsequent winter.Coming ahead of Indiaâs peak pollution season, the paper, titled âAir quality in flux: The baffling ENSO transition in Indiaâ, published in Atmospheric Pollution Research journal Thursday, found that La NiÃ±a/El NiÃ±o conditions altered atmospheric circulation, PM2.5 transport pathways and weather conditions that determine whether pollution disperses or gets trapped.That atmospheric conditions regulate pollution levels was always known. What the study shows is how the atmosphere in winters can behave very differently under El Nino and La Nina conditions, determining where pollutants accumulate and where they are carried away even when emissions remain broadly similar. However, the researchers caution that the study does not establish that El NiÃ±o invariably worsens air quality in Delhi or north India.âWe are not implying that the 2023-24 El NiÃ±o pattern will be repeated this winter. The two years that we studied were unusual and unique,â said atmospheric scientist Gufran Beig, one of the studyâs authors. âThis yearâs El NiÃ±o is likely to be the strongest on record.âThe study found that during the La NiÃ±a winter of 2022-23, stronger winds over north India helped disperse emissions from stubble-burning and local sources. The altered circulation bypassed Delhi and its surroundings and transported these pollutants southwards towards peninsular India. This resulted in substantially higher PM2.5 levels in cities such as Mumbai and Thiruvananthapuram.The following winter, the atmospheric setup changed. Under El NiÃ±o, winds over northern India were weaker and passed through areas, including Delhi and Jaipur, rather than carrying pollutants away. The resulting stagnation favoured the accumulation of PM2.5. Jaipur, for instance, recorded an increase of about 50% compared with the 2019-22 average, while Delhi logged a spike of over 10%.Weather conditions also mattered differently in the two years. Rain can remove pollutants from air, while high pressure, weak winds and a shallow boundary layer can trap them close to the ground. In Jaipur, rainfall was more strongly associated with lower PM2.5 during 2022-23, whereas surface pressure became a more important factor during 2023-24, leading to pollution spikes after rain.The researchers also used backward air-mass trajectories to trace where the air reaching cities had travelled from. Jaipur continued to receive air from polluted northern regions during the El NiÃ±o winter. Hyderabad, by contrast, received more marine and southern air, helping explain why its pollution pattern moved in the opposite direction.Overall, the study found substantial year-to-year PM2.5 variations from average levels in 2019-22 â ranging from about a 40% decline to a 70% increase, despite no major changes in emissions or pollution-control policies during the period. The authors underlined that the correlations neither establish direct causation nor can these be extrapolated to other years.For Delhi-NCR, this has an important implication: relatively low local or agricultural emissions do not automatically guarantee cleaner air if large-scale circulation turns stagnant. Conversely, even substantial emissions can have a smaller local impact when strong winds efficiently disperse or divert them.The winter pollution story may begin in Delhi and its neighbourhood, but increasingly, the weather that decides its intensity is being written on a much larger canvas.

World.title: Cabinet Secretary didn’t act on Election Commissioners’ plaint as it was unofficial: RTI
World.content:
The two ECs alleged the changes were made without prior discussion with the commission or officers concerned.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: After election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote to cabinet secretary T V Somanathan in July objecting to the revised allocation of work among senior commission officers by senior deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg without the EC approval, the cabinet secretariat refused to intervene, saying the communication was not from EC as a whole, and also cited poll panelâs status as a constitutional body that was independent of executive and empowered to conduct its own affairs.According to documents shared as part of an RTI response, two ECs in their separate but near-identical letters to Somanathan on July 29 objected to Gargâs conduct and an order he issued revising allocation of work among senior officers. The two ECs alleged the changes were made without prior discussion with the commission or officers concerned.The reallocation of work by Garg was ordered while he was filling in for DEC (administration) Bhanu Prakash Yeturu, who was then on leave. It would change how files were to be routed by IT division headed by DG Seema Khanna; they would no longer be routed through DEC Sanjay Kumar. Sandhu and Joshi, according to a report in The Indian Express, dated Sept 23, had in internal notes to DEC concerned, alleged that ECINET software conceived and managed by the IT division, was too centralised, blocking access to field officers who were authorised by law to make changes to the electoral roll.However, the reallocation order issued by Garg was never implemented, after the ECs objected.Explaining the rationale behind the reluctance to take any action, a confidential note on the file shared by the cabinet secretariat with transparency activist Commodore Lokesh K Batra (retd), as part of its RTI reply, said the EC being a constitutional body was insulated from the executiveâs interference by design.The cabinet secretariat, while stopping at only acknowledging letters from the two ECs, also marked a copy of its response to the CEC.âThe communications are from ECs in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from EC as a whole,â it said, adding that Garg was an officer of the poll panel and his conduct was to be regulated by rules and guidelines of the EC. It also emphasised that ECâs decisions are to be taken unanimously and, when not possible, by majority.âIn absence of any official communication from EC as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate. It may also be construed as interference in functioning of the constitutional body,â the note said, before stating the decision to merely send an acknowledgement to the two ECs, with copies marked to CEC and the DoPT.Sources said no follow-up action was taken by EC or the CEC as Garg, going by an office order of 1997, acted as per rules. The 1997 order had delegated commissionâs financial and administrative powers to DECs, with DEC (administration), the position held by Garg, given powers concerning appointment, recruitment, transfer and posting of employees, and posting and transfer of all personal staff of ECs and the DECs. âNo files related to transfers and postings thus needed to be put up routinely to the EC,â a commission officer said.Batra on Sept 24 sought copies of ECsâ communications, details of steps taken by the cabinet secretariat and the relevant file notings.

World.title: China’s patrolling deviations disturb border: MEA on ITBP DG's LAC face-offs remark
World.content:
ITBP chief flags âongoingâ China faceoff along Arunachal border.

The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off

Stronger drones must to counter PLA: ITBP

Cong slams govt over face-offs

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: Following confirmation by ITBP of the continuing India-China military stand-off on the Arunachal Pradesh border, India once again cautioned China that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral ties, echoing PM Narendra Modiâs message to Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting last month.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time.âAs we have noted in the past, the situation in India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns,â ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, adding that the two sides had also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the Line of Actual Control in appropriate areas for better border management.The official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control.ITBP DG Shatrujeet Kapur had on Thursday publicly said that Indian and Chinese troops had lately been locked in face-offs at select points along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, which âare still continuingâ. He, however, added that the âShauryaâ commandos of his force, deployed along the LAC, had done an âexcellent jobâ in dealing with the face-offs.The ITBP chief said India was focusing on building its drone and anti-drone capabilities as âconventionalâ military resources and infrastructure were not enough to take on the Peopleâs Liberation Army which had undergone a massive capacity upgrade and modernisation, making China a âvery strong adversaryâ.âDrones can pose a challenge as well as present an advantage,â Kapur said, citing the example of Ukraine and Iran which, despite being small nations and with much smaller or no conventional armed forces, had taken on superpowers like Russia and the US respectively.DG Shatrujeet Kapur said ITBP had included drone platoons for all its border units, with 70% of the Rs 400 crore allocated by MHA for modernisation of the force earmarked for upgrading drone warfare capabilities. The force is raising more âShauryaâ commando platoons trained in mountain warfare, new-generation weapons and unarmed combat.Kapur said ITBP must redefine itself as a high-altitude fighting force, distinct from the Army or any other central paramilitary force.Reports of border friction coincide with the ongoing efforts to normalise Sino-India ties that have seen considerable progress since Modiâs meeting with Xi in Russiaâs Kazan in 2024.In the meeting last month, Modi underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. The two leaders also expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question.Citing ITBP DG Shatrujeet Kapurâs remarks about continuing skirmishes with China, Congress Friday asked PM Modi whether the pre-May 2020 status quo ante had been restored in Ladakh and if India could patrol up to border points such as Shera-5 in Arunachal Pradesh.Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera said the govt should send an all-party delegation, including the opposition, to Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh to establish whether China had encroached on Indian territory.âPM gave China a clean chit in 2020. In 2026, the country deserves a clean account of what is happening on its borders. Enough of clean chits to China â it is time for govt to come clean before India.âKhera termed DG Shatrujeet Kapurâs remarks serious and claimed they showed that Chinaâs belligerence continued despite the govt âkowtowingâ to Beijing. He cited continuing skirmishes, reports of encroachment, including by BJP netas, and a trade deficit with China that had ballooned to $113 billion.Congress questioned outcomes of repeated meetings between Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping, asking why incursions and attempts to alter the LAC continued.

World.title: Northwest India turned drier, south wetter over 70 years, finds IMD study
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A new IMD study finds that northwest India has turned drier, with its dry climate zone expanding from about a quarter to one-third of the total geographical area, whereas the south peninsula became wetter due to a rise in overall quantitative rainfall over the past seven decades.

The findings, published in the IMDâs peer-reviewed journal Mausam, note that the dry zone that once ended in western UP is now extending into the east of the state, with the scientists warning the change could affect paddy cultivation in the north.

âHot, dry zone pushed east into UP over past 70 yearsâ

In northwest India, the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the regionâs area in 1951-1980 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth, meaning that an area equal to roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined, said the study.

It said peninsular India, on the other hand, reported shrinking of its hot semi-arid zone from about 30% of the region to 16%, and most of that land moved into the tropical savannah zone, which now covers three-quarters of the peninsula, a change the authors attribute to rising rainfall over southern India.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âWithin these broader shifts, Marathwada and west Vidarbha in Maharashtra moved into the hot semi-arid zone, and the tropical monsoon zone extended along the Konkan coast, coastal Karnataka and Kerala,â said the study, conducted by scientists from IMD and Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology.





âWhen we compared Indiaâs climate map decade by decade from 1951 to 2020, the clearest change was in the north, where the hot, dry zone has pushed east into Uttar Pradesh, and because this is one of the countryâs most important farming regions, the timing of sowing and harvesting there needs to be watched closely,â said Ananya Karmakar, the studyâs lead author.

Since the scientists highlight potential implications for agriculture and the need to track long-term climate shifts, the study could be handy for farm sector policymakers.

World.title: New car safety rules: Rear-crash tests from 2029 to prevent fire, immobilisers from 2027
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Aiming to prevent fires caused by rear-end collisions, all new cars manufactured from April 2029 will have to comply with a crash-test standard that ensures no fuel spillage or damage to the battery in petrol/diesel and electric vehicles, respectively.

The road transport ministry has made compliance with this automotive industry standard mandatory.

âTo meet the norm, cars will have to be designed and manufactured in a way that prevents damage to the fuel tank or battery in a rear-end collision,â an official said.

The ministry has also set mandatory timelines for automakers to comply with other Automotive Industry Standards (AIS), covering occupant protection in offset frontal and lateral collisions, protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and fitment of immobilisers.

The requirements will come into effect from April 2027 onwards.

In a notification, the ministry has also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from October 2029. EDRs remain optional but record crash-related data to help establish what happened immediately before and during a collision. Their function is similar to that of an aircraftâs flight-data recorder, or black box.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âThe rollout will be phased, as the data can help assess driving behaviour and identify corrective measures to prevent future crashes,â the official said.





He added that mandatory fitment of immobilisers in cars from October 2027 would be crucial to preventing vehicle theft. An immobiliser is an electronic anti-theft device that prevents an engine from starting unless it detects the correct key or an authorised electronic signal.

World.title: Arms training case: US mercenary VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24
World.content:
VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24

NEW DELHI: An NIA court Friday allowed US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals accused in the Myanmar arms training case to remain in their home countries till Feb 24. The permission came after NIA told special judge Prashant Sharma of Rouse Avenue court that it needed more time to probe the UA(P)A offences against them.âFurther probe is ongoing and more time is required in order to ascertain and verify the facts about the commission of offences under UA(P)A in view of import and recovery of huge quantities of drones and accessories through India,â it said.VanDyke attended the court hearing Friday and sought the release of his seized personal articles. The seven accused had earlier sought six weeks to meet their families and were allowed to stay abroad till Oct 23. They were arrested on March 13 for allegedly training insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar.

World.title: Opposition's 'mock Parliament' to step up fight against SIR & CEC Gyanesh Kumar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ahead of a rally on Nov 1, the joint opposition bloc is considering a âmock parliamentâ next week to further up the ante against SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The bloc is also mulling new demands on the controversial issues to surprise the govt.

Sources said a âmockâ gathering depicting an assembly of MPs may take place in the national capital on Oct 28. The event will involve MPs and others, but is unlikely to be a large gathering, given that a massive show of strength to push for the CECâs resignation is planned at Ramlila Maidan as a âDelhi chaloâ rally.

An opposition member said the mock session could have an agenda ranging from âimpeachment of CECâ and seeking his resignation to a discussion on SIR, which opposition claims has led to mass disenfranchisement. Sources said new demands, not yet unveiled by the bloc, were also being planned. âThere are groups of technocrats at work and new revelation leading to a fresh agenda can be raised,â a functionary said.

The idea is to sustain the agitation seeking CECâs removal. The campaign began with CJPâs call for a dharna on Oct 10, while the INDIA bloc marched to the EC office on Oct 6, to Rashtrapati Bhavan on Oct 9, and to the SC on Oct 12.

World.title: Legal action ordered against officials over irregularities in voter list in Pilibhit
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on Wednesday (October 23, 2026) ordered legal action against officials responsible for discrepancies in the electoral rolls of the Pilibhit Assembly Constituency, where searching certain voters’ EPIC numbers online displayed details of other electors.

“Legal action will be taken against both the current and former election officials responsible for the discrepancies found in the voter list for constituency 127 – Pilibhit. In addition to the legal action being taken against the two voter registration officials, instructions have also been given to initiate departmental action. The computer support staff will be terminated. The District Election Officer, Pilibhit, has received a detailed report regarding a complaint concerning the display of the EPIC number of one voter in the voter list of Assembly constituency 127 (Pilibhit), indicating the details of another voter,” reads an official statement by the State election commission.

According to the investigation report, the computer operator of the voter registration centre for Assembly Constituency 127 – Pilibhit, entered a total of 13,779 Form-8s between May 31, 2026, and August 29, 2026, to update voter details. Of these, a total of 4,717 forms were entered between July 16, 2026, and the remaining 9,062 forms were entered between July 17, 2026, and August 29, 2026. No Form-8s corresponding to any of these entries were found in the office records. A total of 10,470 Form-8s were approved, while 3,309 were rejected. This revealed discrepancies in 10,470 of the entries,” says the official statement.

The Election Commission of India has directed that the computer operator at the voter registration centre in 127-Pilibhit and the election registration officers (EROs) assigned to the Pilibhit constituency for the period between July 16, 2026, and July 17, 2026, be held responsible for the irregularities in the voter registration process.

“The commission has instructed that legal action be taken against them under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code. Furthermore, the commission has directed a thorough investigation into the role of the relevant assistant election registration officers in this case, with a report to be submitted. The District Election Officer, Pilibhit, has been instructed to direct the computer assistants at voter registration centres to conduct a thorough review of all Form 6s and Form 7s submitted for voter registration and deletion, respectively, between April 10, 2026, and October 21, 2026, and to provide a detailed report within one day. In addition, all discrepancies found in Form 8 entries are being addressed according to established procedures and standards,” added the official statement.

The Congress on Wednesday (October 21) alleged large-scale manipulation of electoral rolls in the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency, claiming that the names of 13,150 voters were changed while their EPIC and serial numbers remained the same. The party accused the Election Commission for the manipulation.

World.title: Chennai Corporation ramps up preparedness amid monsoon, El Niño concerns
World.content:
The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has issued detailed instructions to officials on measures to tackle heavy rain, strong winds, and possible flood-related emergencies this Northeast monsoon.

According to Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran, intensive precautionary measures were being implemented across the GCC limits, as directed by the Tamil Nadu government, in view of the Northeast monsoon and the El Niño phenomenon.

Zonal officers have been instructed to ensure readiness for any rain-related emergencies in Chennai and surrounding areas.

The officials are to conduct coordination meetings with Residents’ Welfare Associations and public representatives, while awareness campaigns are to be carried out in flood-prone areas through the media and public announcement systems. The preparedness of first responders, relief centres, and evacuation arrangements is also to be ensured, according to a press release.

Relief centres are to be equipped with adequate lighting, sanitation facilities, food, and other essentials. Fire and Rescue Services personnel, police, and medical teams are to remain on standby. Vehicles for evacuation, along with trucks, JCB excavators and tipper lorries, are to be kept ready for emergency operations.

Officials have also been instructed to remove hoardings and temporary structures, maintain fuel stocks and diesel generators, keep equipment ready for clearing fallen trees, ensure power backup at Urban Primary Health Centres, and maintain adequate stocks of essential medicines in hospitals. Residents are advised to avoid unnecessary travel during periods of heavy rain and strong winds.

World.title: CMDA plans ₹8.34-crore road, drain works at Koyambedu market after clogging issues
World.content:
The Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) has proposed road repairs and renovation of stormwater drains at the Koyambedu Wholesale Market Complex, at an estimated cost of ₹8.34 crore, as it steps up measures to address waterlogging and clogged drains.

A CMDA official said water stagnation on the main roads had reduced after a drain was constructed. However, clogging persisted near the L and M blocks and inside the flower market, where old drains required cleaning.

High-pressure jet-rodding machines would be deployed to clear clogged drains in the internal market areas, where manual cleaning would be difficult. The CMDA would procure the machines from the Chennai Metrowater and the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC).

Some locations require new drains, which would be constructed after the monsoon.

Motor pumps had already been deployed to remove stagnant water. The CMDA had also sought the GCC’s help in placing pumps in waterlogged areas and asked the Chennai Metro Rail Limited to install high-powered suction pumps at locations affected by its ongoing works, the official said.

Unsold vegetables

The CMDA also plans to work with the GCC to collect or purchase unsold vegetables from vendors for use in Amma Canteens, and breakfast and midday meal kitchens, the official said.

A new contractor has taken over solid waste management at the market. The official said the CMDA would closely monitor open dumping of waste along pathways and in areas where it could clog drains, and impose heavy fines on those responsible.

Scope of the project

The ₹8.34-crore project includes relaying the cement concrete road between Gates 7 and 14, repairing roads, and renovating stormwater drains in the vegetable market’s truck bays.

The work is scheduled to be completed within six months of the site being handed over.

The 67-acre complex houses vegetable, fruit, and flower markets. The project was announced by the State government during the 2026-27 Budget session.

Separately, the CMDA has proposed road upgrades at the Iron and Steel Market in Sathangadu at an estimated cost of ₹8.21 crore.

World.title: Delhi government inspects stores advertising buy one, get one free offers
World.content: The Delhi government stepped up inspections of stores advertising heavy discounts on social media during the festive season and seized over 322 kg of ghee on Friday for further testing for adulteration. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said in a statement that compromising on food quality or people’s health would not be acceptable. She said her government was working to curb irregularities such as adulteration, substandard quality, the sale of expired products and incorrect labelling. “Consumers should remain vigilant and check the quality and packaging of food products, along with their manufacturing date and expiry date, before making a purchase,” Ms. Gupta said. During the drive, the Food Safety Department conducted targeted inspections of stores promoting offers such as ‘Buy One, Get One Free’ and discounts of up to 60% through social media reels. The drive aimed to check compliance with food safety standards and prevent the sale of unsafe, substandard, expired or incorrectly labelled food products, Ms. Gupta said. According to the department, its teams inspected two stores in Vikaspuri, where they collected five enforcement samples of ghee from different brands and five surveillance samples of other food products. A total of 75.53 litres of ghee was seized. At another store in Hastal village, the team collected three enforcement samples of ghee from three different brands and seized 246 kg of ghee. The department said shortcomings in compliance with food safety standards were recorded at the establishments. The findings would be reviewed along with the laboratory test reports before further action was taken. “Further action will be taken in the respective cases in accordance with the law,” the department said.

World.title: Police unearth cyber fraud racket; bankstaffers among 6 held
World.content:
The Delhi Police have busted a cyber fraud network involving 37 suspected mule bank accounts that received ₹7.36 crore in connection with 99 complaints registered across India. Six people, including five bankers, have been arrested, officials said on Friday.

The arrested bankers included Shobhit Aggarwal, branch manager of Catholic Syrian Bank (CSB Bank) in Saraswati Vihar, and four members of the bank’s sales team. The branch manager of the Tri Nagar branch, Sushant Kumar, has not yet been apprehended.

The sixth accused, Mayank Kapoor, 35, allegedly used forged signatures and KYC documents obtained from unsuspecting daily-wage labourers to facilitate the opening of fraudulent bank accounts. A portion of the proceeds was allegedly converted into cryptocurrency, officials said.

The investigation uncovered 17 suspected mule accounts at the Saraswati Vihar branch and 20 at the Tri Nagar branch of CSB Bank.

According to the police, the investigation began after scrutiny of mule account data identified the Tri Nagar branch as a suspected centre for opening such accounts.

“A preliminary inquiry revealed that the purported holder of one account had neither visited the branch nor applied to open it. The addresses linked to two other suspected mule accounts at the branch could not be verified,” a police officer said.

“A technical analysis of registered mobile numbers, email IDs, linked devices and email connections led investigators to Kapoor, who was arrested from Baba Haridas Nagar in Delhi,” the officer added.

During interrogation, Kapoor allegedly told the police that he had contacted daily-wage labourers over the phone on the pretext of loan approval and obtained their KYC documents and photographs through WhatsApp. He also arranged SIM cards in their names and used the documents, photographs and SIM cards to facilitate the opening of mule accounts, the police said.

The police said Kapoor came into contact with Aggarwal, who allegedly helped process the account applications. Aggarwal later introduced him to Sushant Kumar, the Tri Nagar branch manager.

The accounts were allegedly opened without the purported account holders being physically present, and forged signatures were used on the applications. The applications were processed by four members of the bank’s sales team — Manoj, Ankur Kumar, Fatma and Pankaj Pandey — and subsequently approved by the branch managers.

Aggarwal, Manoj, Ankur Kumar, Fatma and Pankaj Pandey were arrested on October 18. Kapoor had been arrested earlier during the investigation.

The police recovered 63 Aadhaar cards, 60 PAN cards, 55 passport-size photographs and 11 SIM cards allegedly intended for use in opening bank accounts. They also seized seven mobile phones, seven cheque books, seven debit cards, a laptop, ₹60,000 in cash and approximately 150 grams of gold jewellery.

Investigators also found that Kapoor used the Trust Wallet application to receive and transfer Tether (USDT), a cryptocurrency allegedly linked to the proceeds of crime.

The case has been registered under Sections 317(2), 317(5), 338, 336(3), 340 and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation is under way to identify others involved in the racket and trace the proceeds of crime.

World.title: AAP flags ‘irregularities’ in textbook printing; BJP rejects allegations
World.content:
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Friday alleged that NCERT textbooks supplied free to Delhi government schools were printed on substandard paper and did not meet tender specifications. It sought an explanation from Education Minister Ashish Sood and the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

At a press meet, AAP Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj compared copies of the Class 8 NCERT textbook ‘Malhar’ (the new official Class 8 Hindi core book) sold in bookshops with those supplied to government schools, alleging a “scam” in printing.

“The specifications in these tenders are exactly the same as those of the books available in the market. The paper size is supposed to be A4, and the paper quality must be 80 GSM (grams per square metre).

However, the books printed are not of A4 size and are printed on substandard paper,” Mr. Bharadwaj said, accusing the Education Department of corruption. He said a printer had told him that the prices of the two books differed by at least 40%. “The government must explain who all took this commission. Have officials or politicians taken commissions for books meant for schoolchildren?” Mr. Bharadwaj said.

‘Deflecting attention’

Delhi BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor rejected the charge, saying textbooks had been supplied regularly for the past two years.

He alleged that during the previous AAP government, entire academic sessions often passed without textbooks being supplied to students. “It appears that Saurabh Bharadwaj considers himself an expert capable of judging the quality of paper as well,” Mr. Kapoor said.

World.title: CREDAI Chennai sets up anti-corruption panel, frames SOP for reporting graft
World.content:
In a move to promote transparency and accountability in the real estate sector, CREDAI Chennai has constituted an Anti-Corruption Committee and introduced a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to report instances of undue gratification, corruption, and coercion.

The Confederation of Real Estate Developers Associations of India (CREDAI), Chennai, the apex body for the real estate industry in India, has told its members through a letter that this SOP is framed in line with the vision of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, who has consistently and unequivocally declared his government’s zero-tolerance stance against corruption.

This SOP applies to matters relating to planning permissions, building permits, layout approvals, completion certificates, NOCs, inspections, registrations, utility connections, revenue/land records, statutory certificates, and other government-related services affecting member projects.

“Members have been told that genuine corruption-related issues will be formally reported to the Chief Minister’s Special Cell, with copies marked to the Ministry concerned and the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption,” said P. Kruthivas, president-elect, CREDAI Chennai.

A complaint may be submitted only by persons connected with CREDAI Chennai member developers, including promoters, managing director, partner, proprietor and authorised signatory of Public Limited companies.

CREDAI said in a letter that the term ‘Anti-Corruption Committee’ was used in the SOP as it was formal, clear, and aligned with the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and the Tamil Nadu Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption.

World.title: Delhi govt. directs officials to identify pollution hotspots amid decline in air quality
World.content:
With the city’s air quality remaining “poor” for the second consecutive day and no respite forecast for the next nine days, Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Friday directed officials to prepare hotspot-specific action plans, identifying the agencies responsible, and setting deadlines for corrective measures.

At a review meeting, Mr. Sirsa directed officials to use air quality index (AQI) monitoring data to identify local sources of pollution, focusing on road dust, heavy traffic, construction, unauthorised parking, and waste burning.

“Our approach is clear: identify the source of pollution and act at the spot. Every department must have a clear action plan, a deadline and accountability for results,” Mr. Sirsa said. He instructed agencies to remove encroachments, repair potholes, treat exposed soil along roadsides and ensure regular water sprinkling at locations prone to dust.

A higher AQI means an increase in air pollution. Delhi’s average AQI stood at 230 in the “poor” category, with Stage I of the Graded Response Action Plan in force. Three of the 56 monitoring stations recorded “very poor” air quality, with Pusa reporting the highest AQI at 324, according to the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) Sameer app.

Data from the app also showed transport accounted for 20.3% of Delhi’s air pollution, followed by residential sources (5.2%), industries (4.2%), construction (2.6%), energy (2%), waste burning (1.8%), road dust (1.4%) and other sectors (1.3%).

Mr. Sirsa called for better coordination between the traffic police and other agencies to regulate the movement of heavy vehicles, particularly during peak hours. Urging residents to help fight pollution, Mr. Sirsa asked them to avoid burning garbage or dumping waste on roads, keep vehicle Pollution Under Control certificates valid, and use public transport or carpool.

“Keeping Delhi’s air clean requires government action and responsible public behaviour, including avoiding waste burning and reducing private vehicle use,” he added.

World.title: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting
World.content:
Developments in the Gulf region amid the US-Israeli war on Iran came under discussion as the R4 foreign ministers — Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye — met with their counterparts from France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom.

The R4 group, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.

According to the Foreign Office (FO), Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar participated in the first meeting between the R4 and France, Germany, Italy and the UK.

“The meeting provided an opportunity for exchange of views on regional developments in the Gulf region, their social and economic impacts, and the urgent need to foster diplomatic engagement to resolve regional challenges of peace, security and stability,” it said.

“Dar briefed his counterparts on the diplomatic and mediatory role Pakistan continues to play in de-escalating tensions, preventing resumption of hostilities and promoting peace. All ministers agreed for continued engagement in this format,” it said.

The R4 bloc also held a separate meeting. According to the FO, Dar participated in the sixth R4 foreign ministers’ meeting alongside Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, and Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud of Saudi Arabia.

The ministers reviewed developments in the region since their last meeting in New York in September, with “particular focus on the situation in the Middle East and related security challenges and conflicts”, the FO said.

They expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed their support for its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The FO added that the ministers also condemned the Houthi attacks targeting Saudi Arabia and underscored the importance of respecting state sovereignty.

“They discussed ways to strengthen regional coordination and advance diplomatic efforts to promote lasting peace, security, and stability,” it said.

A joint statement issued after the meeting detailed that the ministers particularly condemned Houthi strikes on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, as well as attacks carried out against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab.

“They expressed their full solidarity with the government of Yemen and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and called on the Houthi militia to immediately cease all military actions, threats and attacks, and to return to the political process in good faith,” the statement said.

Regarding the US-Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz, they stressed the “urgent need” to address this conflict only through dialogue and diplomacy, as well as to prevent the targeting of civilians and civilian infrastructures, including vessels.

They expressed support for the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding and welcomed continued diplomatic efforts to prevent further escalation and reaffirmed their commitment to a lasting negotiated solution, the joint statement said.

The participants further underscored the “vital importance” of freedom of navigation, permanent maritime safety and security and safeguarding navigational rights and freedoms.

“They noted that disruption of sea lanes threatens the security and prosperity of all, through blocking global supply chains, flows of energy, fertiliser and food, impacting vulnerable populations in the region and beyond, and thus, requires collective efforts by the international community to address these challenges.”

The ministers also rejected any measures or restrictions that impair lawful navigation and called for the swift and full resumption of safe, secure and unimpeded passage through the Strait of Hormuz, the statement said, adding that the participants agreed to maintain close consultation and coordination on the afore-mentioned matters.

Moreover, they emphasised that the Israeli occupation in Gaza constituted the “fundamental source of instability” in the region and beyond, and that Israeli policies creates a “deep sense of injustice in global public opinion”.

They called for the early implementation of the two-state solution in Palestine, in accordance with the relevant UN resolutions.

“They reiterated their support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including their inalienable right to self-determination and to establish an independent, sovereign, viable, and contiguous State of Palestine on the basis of the 4 June 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions in order to achieve comprehensive peace in the Middle East,” the statement said.

The ministers called for an “urgent end” to the ongoing Israeli violence, as well as attempts to change the legal and historical status of Jerusalem, and to bring an end to further destruction and humanitarian tragedy in Palestine.

They condemned all the previous and current settlement activities in the West Bank and Jerusalem, as well as the settler violence against Palestinians and underlined the urgent need for uninterrupted flow of humanitarian aid to and reconstruction in Gaza.

Bilateral meetings

Dar earlier held bilateral meetings with the Turkish and Egyptian foreign ministers, on the sidelines of the R4 meeting and a meeting between the R4 and European diplomats in Istanbul, the FO said.

In a post on X, the FO said that Dar met with Fidan ahead of the ministerial meeting, thanking him for hosting the meetings. The pair discussed bilateral relations and regional developments, particularly the situation in the Middle East and Palestine.

“They expressed concern over threats to regional stability and underscored the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and coordinated efforts to promote regional peace and security,” the FO statement said.

Additionally, Dar and Fidan strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed their commitment to close coordination on regional issues, including under the Makkah Defence Agreement.

“Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the longstanding bonds of friendship and brotherhood between Pakistan and Turkiye, and to deepening cooperation across all areas of mutual interest, both bilaterally and in multilateral fora,” the FO added.

Later, the FO said that Dar also met with Egyptian FM Abdelatty on the sidelines of the ministerial meeting, where the two exchanged views on regional and international developments.

In particular, they discussed the situation in Palestine and the Middle East, and underscored the importance of “sustained dialogue and diplomacy” in addressing challenges in the region.

The two reaffirmed the “longstanding and fraternal ties” between Pakistan and Egypt, and highlighted the importance of sustained high-level engagement to further advance bilateral relations, the FO statement said.

“They agreed to impart greater momentum to cooperation across a range of areas, including trade, business-to-business linkages, agriculture, pharmaceutical, connectivity, renewable energy, defence, and people-to-people exchanges,” the FO added.

The ministers also reaffirmed their commitment to continued consultations and closer coordination under the R4 framework, as well as on matters of mutual interest, it said.

The deputy premier later had a “warm and cordial meeting” with Saudi FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan, where he expressed Pakistan’s full support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the kingdom.

“The two leaders reaffirmed the enduring strength of the fraternal ties between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and their commitment to further strengthening their strategic partnership through close cooperation across all areas of interest and regular consultations at all levels,” the FO said.

They also underscored the “special bond” between their countries, reinforced by their bilateral Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement and the Makkah defence agreement between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia; as well as their shared commitment to regional peace, security and stability, it added.

Separately, DPM Dar met with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the meeting and expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral ties “through sustained engagement and cooperation across multiple areas of mutual interest”, the FO said.

According to the FO, the two ministers discussed relations between Pakistan and Germany and exchanged views on regional and international developments. They stressed the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and sustained international engagement to promote peace and stability and to address the evolving challenges in the region.

Dar “welcomed the constructive engagement” of Germany, France, Italy and the UK with the R4 framework, the FO said, adding that he underscored the value of “continued consultations and diplomatic coordination on issues of shared concern”.

Talks to revolve around Hormuz, Saudi Arabia

British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband’s office said the talks would essentially revolve around “the Strait of Hormuz and the situation in Saudi Arabia”.

It said Miliband “will advocate for a diplomatic solution to the [Hormuz] crisis that restores full navigational rights and freedoms”.

He will also stress “how Iranian tactics are being replicated across the region, with attacks on Saudi Arabia further destabilising the region and increasing pressure on vital waterways and global chokepoints, such as Bab el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal”, it added.

France confirmed the talks on “the Iranian crisis in its various ramifications”, hailing it as a first “in this format … against a backdrop of extreme instability and uncertainty in the region.”

The meeting will aim to “strengthen coordination between Europeans and Middle Eastern countries in the face of crises that we did not choose and that affect us all,” the French foreign ministry said.

Fidan is expected to emphasise the need for a diplomatic solution to the war between the United States and Iran, the importance of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, and reiterate Turkiye’s support for Saudi Arabia’s security against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels under the Makkah defence agreement signed by Islamabad, Ankara, and Riyadh, the sources said.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia have completed ratification of Makkah defence pact: FO
World.content:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have completed the ratification processes for the Makkah defence pact while Turkiye was in the process of doing so, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday.

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

The pact has gained significance amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said earlier this week that Pakistan was providing “whatever support is needed” to defend the kingdom.

Prior to that, the FO had emphasised that signing the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and committing military capabilities under it were executive functions under Pakistan’s national laws and Rules of Business and did not necessarily require parliamentary approval.

Answering questions after the weekly press briefing, the FO spokesperson said that “matters related to the agreement, its ratification and operationalisation remain under discussion by the three parties”.

This included discussions during the Strategic Political and Defence Committee, which recently met on Oct 5, he added.

“The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement reflects the shared commitment of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to strengthening collective defence and cooperation for regional security and stability,” Khan said.

He further noted that each country followed its own constitutional and legal procedures to approve and ratify international agreements.

“Pakistan and [the] Kingdom of Saudi Arabia have already completed their ratification processes, while Turkiye is undertaking the requisite procedures in accordance with its domestic legal framework,” he said.

Turkiye submitted the Makkah defence pact to its parliament for ratification earlier this week.

The spokesperson highlighted Pakistan’s continued commitment to the letter and spirit of the agreement, which he said “is defensive in nature, consistent with the UN Charter, and aimed at promoting regional peace, security and stability”.

Answering a follow-up question regarding Article 2 of the pact, which states that an attack on one party would be considered an attack against all parties, Khan stressed again that the agreement was “essentially defensive in nature” and consistent with Article 51 of the UN Charter, which provides the right to self-defence”.

“The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement reflects the shared commitment of all three parties, primarily to strengthening collective defence, deterrence, and regional stability,” he said.

He added, “It is not directed against any particular country. It provides a framework for collective assistance in the event of external armed aggression against any party.”

According to Khan, the “nature and extent” of any such assistance would be determined collectively by the three countries as the situation arose, “following an objective assessment of the circumstances”.

To another question, he clarified that there were “no hidden provisions” in the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

“We endorse the text released in the media from the Turkish Parliament. There are no hidden provisions; the agreement is explicit and clear in its provisions and articles,” he said.

Regarding the potential invocation of the agreement in response to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the spokesperson reiterated that “This matter has to be decided by the three partner countries in accordance with the agreement.”

He also expressed Pakistan’s concern over the recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and its implications for regional peace and security.

“Our position has been clear and consistent,” Khan said. “We support Yemen’s sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity, and believe that a lasting solution to the conflict can only be achieved through dialogue and a negotiated political settlement … At the same time, we unequivocally condemn attacks against Saudi Arabia and reaffirm our commitment to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, and security.”

He stressed that Pakistan remained supportive of any meaningful diplomatic engagement that could contribute to “ending hostilities and achieving a durable political settlement”.

Earlier this month, the FO said that Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye had agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, following an emergency meeting of the SPDC formed under their joint defence agreement in Riyadh.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development came against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict.

The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive in September.

World.title: Govt raises high-speed diesel rate by Rs1.91 per litre; petrol price unchanged at Rs377.71
World.content:
The government on Friday raised the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.91 per litre, leaving the petrol rate unchanged at Rs377.71.

Following the revision, HSD will cost Rs393.66 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable from Oct 24 (Saturday) to Oct 26 (Monday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: German president meets Zardari, praises Pakistan's 'rising diplomatic profile' in dispute resolution
World.content:
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier praised Pakistan’s “rising diplomatic profile in the resolution of regional and global disputes”, in a meeting with President Asif Ali Zardari in Berlin on Friday.

President Zardari is currently on a three-day visit to Germany, having departed yesterday, as the two countries are set to mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.

According to a statement posted by the president’s office, the two leaders also discussed challenges related to Afghanistan.

President Zardari said that while Pakistan “has no conflict with the Afghan people”, it would not allow terrorists to use Afghan soil to attack Pakistan’s citizens and violate its sovereignty.

Steinmeier appreciated Pakistan for facilitating the verification of 500 Afghans “destined to be repatriated to Germany”, it said, adding that he also commended Pakistan’s humanitarian assistance to “millions of Afghans” over more than four decades.

He also took a “significant interest” in the Makkah defence pact, which has been signed between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. In response, President Zardari said the pact was aimed at “ensuring regional security and provided a security alternative to regional conflicts, and it is not directed against any specific country”.

The German president expressed hope that the two countries would continue to engage with reinforced efforts in the fields of business and trade to promote “bilateral business, education collaboration and technological cooperation”.

For his part, President Zardari thanked Steinmeier for his invitation and the hospitality extended to him and his delegation. President Zardari further expressed his gratitude for Steinmeier’s acknowledgement of Pakistan’s “sincere mediation role” in the conflict between the United States and Iran, the statement said.

He said Pakistan viewed the resolution of conflicts through the lens of sustained dialogue and constructive negotiations, “for the sake of regional as well as global peace and stability”.

During the meeting, President Zardari also stressed the need to “realise the available potential for expanding existing political, economic and defence cooperation” between Pakistan and Germany, with “greater focus on economy and trade, emerging technologies, climate resilience, skills development, people-to-people and cultural exchanges”, the statement said.

The president said that Pakistan “highly values” Germany as a major European partner, and expressed admiration for German support towards women’s empowerment, social protection and human development.

Pakistan was prepared for expanding bilateral cooperation beyond traditional areas into “innovative and mutually beneficial collaboration” with Germany, in the areas of scientific development, healthcare and education, vocational training and technological advancement, trade and investment, agriculture, commerce and industry, and climate resilience, through enhanced government-to-government, business-to-business and expert-level interactions, the statement further quoted President Zardari as saying.

He said the visit reflected Pakistan’s “commitment to deepening its longstanding cordial, friendly relations with Germany and readiness to translate existing relations into a stronger, robust and mutually beneficial partnership through sustained constructive engagement”.

President Zardari invited the German president to Pakistan, who responded that he would consider a visit “at an appropriate time”.
